findings.name: Red Foot Jolt
findings.defect: Parsed as a plain physicalAttack, so the engine deals full Physical Attack Table damage. The card explicitly deals zero damage — its entire payload is the drill discard.
findings.evidence: If successful it does no damage, forcing the defender to discard all drill cards in play
findings.expected: physicalAttack with powerStages: 0 (fixed base of 0 overriding the PAT). CRD battle-sequence step 8 confirms an attack is still 'successful' while dealing no damage.

findings.name: Red Blocking Hand
findings.defect: changeAnger delta is 1, but the only number on the card is 2. The engine raises the user's anger half as much as printed.
findings.evidence: Raise your anger and power stages by 2
findings.expected: changeAnger { target: 'user', delta: 2 }

findings.name: Red Blocking Hand
findings.defect: The power-stage gain is dropped entirely; only the stop and an anger change are parsed. changePowerStages exists in the vocabulary, so this is a catchable omission.
findings.evidence: Raise your anger and power stages by 2
findings.expected: changePowerStages { target: 'user', delta: 2 } alongside the anger change

findings.name: Orange Forceful Kick
findings.defect: lifeCards: 3 is set on physicalAttack, which per abilities.ts OVERRIDES the PAT base. The text adds 3 life cards on top of a normal physical attack ('also does'), so the parse deletes the card's actual physical damage and substitutes 3 life cards.
findings.evidence: Physical attack. If successful it also does 3 life cards of damage.
findings.expected: physicalAttack with no lifeCards (keep the PAT base), plus a rider/manual note for the additional 3 life cards — the engine has no additive life-card effect, so an override is strictly wrong here.

findings.name: Straining, Floating Attack Move
findings.defect: The self-anger reduction is missing entirely; only the energy attack is parsed.
findings.evidence: Lower your anger 1 level.
findings.expected: changeAnger { target: 'user', delta: -1 } added to the effects list

findings.name: Trunks Makes Himself Clear
findings.defect: Only the opponent's anger drop is parsed; the user's anger raise is dropped. The card changes anger on both sides.
findings.evidence: Raise your anger 2 levels.
findings.expected: changeAnger { target: 'user', delta: 2 } in addition to the existing changeAnger { target: 'foe', delta: -2 }

findings.name: Krillin's Power Block
findings.defect: stopAttack window is 'thisAttack', so the engine stops one physical attack. The card locks out every remaining physical attack for the whole combat.
findings.evidence: it also stops your opponent from making any more physical attacks in this combat
findings.expected: stopAttack { attackType: 'physical', window: 'thisCombat' }

findings.name: Mommy's Coming Dear
findings.defect: stopAttack window is 'thisAttack', so the engine stops a single attack instead of shutting down all attacks for the remainder of combat — a massive understatement of the card.
findings.evidence: Stops all attacks for the remainder of Combat.
findings.expected: stopAttack { attackType: 'any', window: 'thisCombat', scope: 'all' }

findings.name: Time Is A Warrior's Tool
findings.defect: stopAttack window is 'thisAttack'; the card stops every attack from the opponent for the entire combat, not one attack.
findings.evidence: Stops all attacks from an opponent in this combat.
findings.expected: stopAttack { attackType: 'any', window: 'thisCombat', scope: 'all' }

findings.name: Straining Focusing Move
findings.defect: stopAttack window is 'thisAttack'; the card has no single-attack stop at all — it is purely a combat-long energy lockout.
findings.evidence: Stops all energy attacks for the rest of this combat.
findings.expected: stopAttack { attackType: 'energy', window: 'thisCombat', scope: 'all' }

findings.name: Tien's Power Burst
findings.defect: stopAttack window is 'thisAttack'; the rider locks the opponent out of energy attacks for the rest of the combat.
findings.evidence: it stops the opponent from playing any other energy attack cards in this combat
findings.expected: stopAttack { attackType: 'energy', window: 'thisCombat' }

findings.name: Vegeta's Jolting Slash
findings.defect: stopAttack window is 'thisAttack'; the printed effect covers the remainder of combat.
findings.evidence: Stops all physical attacks performed against villains for the remainder of Combat.
findings.expected: stopAttack { attackType: 'physical', window: 'thisCombat', scope: 'all' }

findings.name: Saiyan Planet Explosion
findings.defect: Only the first clause is parsed. The second, distinct clause — a combat-long energy lockout — is dropped, so the engine stops one attack and lets every later energy attack through.
findings.evidence: and stops all energy attacks for the rest of this combat
findings.expected: a second stopAttack { attackType: 'energy', window: 'thisCombat', scope: 'all' } alongside the existing thisAttack stop

findings.name: Yamcha's Good Wishes
findings.defect: Only the single-attack stop is parsed; the combat-long physical lockout clause is dropped entirely.
findings.evidence: and all stops all physical attacks for the remainder of Combat
findings.expected: a second stopAttack { attackType: 'physical', window: 'thisCombat', scope: 'all' } alongside the existing thisAttack stop

findings.name: Recoome Boom
findings.defect: stopAttack window is 'thisAttack', which stops an attack in the current attack window. The card instead denies an energy attack in the opponent's NEXT combat phase — a completely different timing window that the vocabulary models as 'nextPhase'.
findings.evidence: stops a single named opponent from making an energy attack on his next combat phase
findings.expected: stopAttack { attackType: 'energy', window: 'nextPhase', scope: 'single' }

findings.name: Powerful Followers
findings.defect: The parse contains only removeFromGameAfterUse — the card's entire function is missing, so the engine plays it, removes it, and nothing is stopped. Vocabulary exists for both halves (stopAttack thisCombat / stunSkipNextPhase).
findings.evidence: Stops an opponent's current or next combat.
findings.expected: stopAttack { attackType: 'any', window: 'thisCombat' } or stunSkipNextPhase (CRD Frieza Saga #19: 'end the current Combat, or... make your opponent skip his next Combat step'), in addition to removeFromGameAfterUse

findings.name: Tien's Jolting Aura
findings.defect: drawCards is applied unconditionally, but the draw is gated on the performer being Tien. Any Hero using this card would illegally draw. Other conditional clauses in this batch (Orange Thumbs Up, Piccolo's Stomp) were correctly omitted rather than applied unconditionally.
findings.evidence: If performed by Tien, draw a card.
findings.expected: drop the drawCards effect (or flag it in needsReview) since the personality condition cannot be expressed; CRD Frieza Saga #16 confirms the conditional wording

findings.name: Smokescreen
findings.defect: The card stops EITHER attack type, but the parse restricts stopAttack to attackType 'energy'. The engine would let a physical attack through against a card that printed-text stops it.
findings.evidence: Stops a physical or energy attack.
findings.expected: stopAttack with attackType 'any' (window 'thisAttack'), plus removeFromGameAfterUse

findings.name: Saiyan Rapid Fire
findings.defect: The 4 power stages belong to a rider dealt to the opponent's ALLIES, not to the attack itself. Setting energyAttack.powerStages=4 overrides the default 4-life-card base, so the engine deals 4 power stages to the defending personality and zero life cards — the opposite of the printed card.
findings.evidence: Energy attack. If successful, deal 4 power stages of damage to every Ally your opponent has in play.
findings.expected: energyAttack with no fixed override (default 4 life cards); the per-Ally 4 power stages is not expressible and should be left unmodeled/manual

findings.name: Saiyan Left Hook
findings.defect: '+3 life cards' is a MODIFIER added on top of the physical attack's Physical Attack Table damage, but the parse encodes it as physicalAttack.lifeCards=3, which per abilities.ts is a FIXED base that OVERRIDES the PAT. The engine therefore deals a flat 3 life cards and drops all power-stage damage. Compare tts-f71532b6-58 (Saiyan High Jump Kick), whose text really is a fixed base ('doing 3 life cards of damage') and is encoded identically — two different card behaviors collapsed into one parse.
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing +3 life cards of damage.
findings.expected: physicalAttack with no lifeCards override (PAT damage stands); the additive +3 life cards has no Effect kind, so it should be left unmodeled rather than turned into a fixed base

findings.name: Saiyan Power Kick
findings.defect: The discard is an OPTIONAL upgrade cost that swaps +4 for +8 stages. The parse applies discardCards{user,1} unconditionally while keeping damageStages 4, so the engine makes the player discard a card and still deals only the base +4 — pure downside that appears nowhere in the text.
findings.evidence: you may discard a cards from your hand when performing this attack to do +8 power stages of damage instead
findings.expected: physicalAttack + damageStages 4 only; the optional discard-for-+8 mode is not modelable and must not be emitted as a mandatory discard

findings.name: Black Blasting Beam
findings.defect: The +2 power stages are gated behind two simultaneous conditions (Tokui-Waza declared AND attacker at 0 power stages), but the parse emits damageStages 2 unconditionally, so every use of this attack gets the bonus.
findings.evidence: If you declared a Tokui-Waza, and the personality that performed this attack is at 0 power stages, this attack does +2 life cards and +2 power stages of damage.
findings.expected: energyAttack alone (default 4 life cards); the conditional +2/+2 is not expressible and should be left unmodeled

findings.name: Red Jump
findings.defect: The card does two anger changes; the parse keeps only the opponent's and drops the user's. The engine never raises the user's anger.
findings.evidence: Lower your opponent's anger 1 level. Raise your anger 1 level.
findings.expected: stopAttack physical + changeAnger{foe,-1} + changeAnger{user,+1}

findings.name: Red Offensive Stance
findings.defect: The 5-stage gain is dropped entirely, even though changePowerStages exists in the schema. The engine stops the attack and raises anger but the defender never gains the power stages.
findings.evidence: Gain 5 power stages.
findings.expected: stopAttack physical + changePowerStages{user,+5} + changeAnger{user,+1}

findings.name: Orange Strike
findings.defect: The card states a fixed 5-card base, which overrides the 4-life-card energy default, but the parse omits lifeCards. The engine will deal 4 life cards instead of 5 — and 5+ life cards is the threshold for Dragon Ball capture (CRD Life Card Capture), so the parse also silently removes a capture trigger.
findings.evidence: Energy attack doing 5 cards of damage.
findings.expected: energyAttack with lifeCards: 5, plus changeAnger{user,+1}

findings.name: Black Anticipation Drill
findings.defect: window 'thisAttack' makes this stop the attack currently being resolved, like a starburst defense. A Defense Shield fires only at battle-sequence step 7 against the first attack that was NOT otherwise stopped — that is what window 'firstSuccessful' exists for. As parsed, the drill burns on any attack the player chooses rather than the first unstopped one.
findings.evidence: Defense Shield: Stops the first unstopped energy attack performed against you during Combat.
findings.expected: stopAttack{attackType:'energy', window:'firstSuccessful'}

findings.name: Black Anticipation Drill
findings.defect: This is a Non-Combat Drill that must already be in play; its Defense Shield activates automatically (CRD step 7: 'the defender must now activate any Defense Shields from his cards in play'). trigger 'defense' models it as a card played from hand to defend during Combat, which a Non-Combat card cannot do.
findings.evidence: Defense Shield: Stops the first unstopped energy attack performed against you during Combat.
findings.expected: trigger 'constant' (drill in play) rather than 'defense'

findings.name: Saiyan Flying Kick
findings.defect: 'If successful' governs the Life Deck discard rider, not the damage. The parse attaches ifSuccessful:true to the damageStages 5, so the +5 stages is treated as a post-step-15 secondary effect instead of part of the attack's own damage calculation.
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing +5 power stages of damage. If successful, your opponent discards the top 2 cards from his Life Deck.
findings.expected: damageStages{stages:5} with no ifSuccessful; the gated effect (opponent discards top 2 Life Deck cards) is the unmodelable part

findings.name: Black Face Slap
findings.defect: Same mis-attachment: 'If successful' introduces the hand-discard rider, but ifSuccessful:true is placed on the damage modifier, which the text states unconditionally as part of the attack.
findings.evidence: Focused physical attack doing +2 power stages of damage. If successful, choose 1 card from your opponent's hand and have him discard it.
findings.expected: damageStages{stages:2} with no ifSuccessful

findings.name: Saiyan Assault
findings.defect: An attack card is parsed as a pure defense card. The parser latched onto the phrase "cards that stop attacks" (part of a cost-increase clause that EXEMPTS stoppers) and produced trigger 'defense' + stopAttack any. The card stops nothing; it is a physical attack with a +2 stage modifier, and both attack effects are absent.
findings.evidence: Physicaly attack doing +2 power stages of damage. Empower 3. ... all your opponent's cards except for cards that stop attacks cost +2 power stages to use.
findings.expected: trigger 'attack' with effects [{kind:'physicalAttack'},{kind:'damageStages',stages:2}]; no stopAttack at all.

findings.name: Red Style Mastery
findings.defect: A Mastery that merely REFERENCES stopping (a recursion clause that fires after some other Red Style card stops an attack) is parsed as a card that itself stops any attack. The engine would gain a free universal attack-stopper. The card's own text grants no stop.
findings.evidence: After you stop an attack with a Red Style card that does not remove itself from the game, place it on the bottom of your Life Deck.
findings.expected: trigger 'constant' (Mastery) with a manual effect; no stopAttack effect.

findings.name: Orange Mouth Shot
findings.defect: lifeCards:1 was scraped from the floating clause that pumps OTHER energy attacks, and applied as this attack's fixed base damage. Per CRD line 449 an energy attack with no stated amount deals 4 life cards, so the parse under-deals by 3 and also silently drops the buff to other attacks.
findings.evidence: Energy attack. Empower 3. All your other energy attacks do +1 life cards of damage for the remainder of Combat.
findings.expected: {kind:'energyAttack'} with NO lifeCards field (default 4 life cards); the +1 to other attacks is an unmodelable floating effect.

findings.name: Multi-Purpose Strike
findings.defect: The card offers an exclusive choice of two modes ("or"), but the parse emits both simultaneously under trigger 'attack': the engine would perform a +5-stage physical attack AND stop an energy attack from the same play. The stop mode also cannot fire under an 'attack' trigger.
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing +5 power stages of damage or stops a focused energy attack.
findings.expected: Attack mode only — [{kind:'physicalAttack'},{kind:'damageStages',stages:5}] — with the defensive mode left to manual/needsReview; not both in one effects list.

findings.name: Red Passive Block
findings.defect: The power-stage gain is dropped entirely. changePowerStages is in the vocabulary and this is the CRD's standard wording for it (cf. CRD line 2029, "Stops a physical attack. Gain 4 power stages."). The user silently loses 5 stages of value every time the card resolves.
findings.evidence: Gain 5 power stages.
findings.expected: Add {kind:'changePowerStages',target:'user',delta:5} alongside the stopAttack and changeAnger effects.

findings.name: Majin Buu's Childish Taunt
findings.defect: The anger gain is conditional on the attack being used by Majin Buu, but it is parsed as an unconditional effect. Any personality playing this card would raise anger 1 level in the engine when the card grants nothing.
findings.evidence: If used by Majin Buu, this attack is focused and raises your anger 1 level.
findings.expected: changeAnger should be gated to Majin Buu (restriction.namedOnly on a separate ability, or dropped to manual/needsReview) — not applied unconditionally.

findings.name: Red Mouth Shot
findings.defect: The stated fixed base of 3 life cards is not captured, so the energy attack falls back to the CRD default of 4 life cards — one card too many, every time. (needsReview:'energyLifeCards' flags the ambiguity, but the parse as written still resolves to a wrong number.)
findings.evidence: Focused energy attack doing 3 life 4 cards of damage.
findings.expected: {kind:'energyAttack',lifeCards:3} — the printed base overrides the 4-life-card default.

findings.name: Namekian Precise Aim Drill
findings.defect: The discard cost is dropped, so the engine offers a free, unlimited energy-attack stop from a Drill in play. AbilityCost.discard exists and the parser does capture costs elsewhere in this batch (Orange 5-Finger Focus captures cost.powerStages:1), so this is an omission, not a vocabulary gap.
findings.evidence: You may discard a card in your hand that can perform an energy attack to stop an energy attack.
findings.expected: cost: { discard: 1 } on the ability (the 'card that can perform an energy attack' restriction on which card is unmodelable, but the cost itself is not).

findings.name: Majin Buu's Charged Attack
findings.defect: The alignment restriction is dropped. AbilityRestriction.alignment models exactly this, and the CRD treats "Villains only" as a binding usability restriction (line 904). The engine would let a Hero deck perform this attack.
findings.evidence: Villains only. Energy attack doing 3 life cards of damage.
findings.expected: restriction: { alignment: 'Villain' } on the ability, in addition to the parsed effects.

findings.name: Orange Hiding Drill
findings.defect: A Non-Combat Drill with a continuous, always-on prevention is parsed with trigger 'defense', i.e. as an activated defensive response. Nothing in the text requires the defender to use or activate anything; the reduction applies to every attack while the Drill is in play. 'constant' is the schema's documented trigger for Drills/continuous effects.
findings.evidence: Prevent 2 life cards of damage from all attacks performed against you.
findings.expected: trigger 'constant' with the same preventLifeCards effect.

findings.name: Majin Vegeta
findings.defect: This is a named personality power (the text carries a power rating and the "Majin Power:" label), but it is parsed with trigger 'defense', which models it as a card used from hand to stop an attack rather than an ability of a personality in play. The stopAttack effect itself is right; the trigger is not.
findings.evidence: 1.325.000 J fA Majin Power: Stops a physical attack.
findings.expected: trigger 'personalityPower' with the same stopAttack effect.

findings.name: Blue Energy Outburst
findings.defect: The foe anger effect has delta -1, but the card lowers the opponent's anger by 2. The parser appears to have grabbed the '1' from the user-anger sentence and applied it to the foe.
findings.expected: { kind: 'changeAnger', target: 'foe', delta: -2 }
findings.evidence: Lower opponent's anger 2 levels.

findings.name: Blue Energy Outburst
findings.defect: The parse contains no effect raising the card user's own anger; only the foe-anger effect is present. The user gets no anger at all when this resolves.
findings.expected: Additional effect { kind: 'changeAnger', target: 'user', delta: 1 } alongside the foe effect
findings.evidence: Raise your anger 1 level.

findings.name: Blue Stance
findings.defect: The foe anger effect has delta -2, but the card only lowers the opponent's anger by 1. The parser took the '2' from the user-anger sentence and applied it to the foe.
findings.expected: { kind: 'changeAnger', target: 'foe', delta: -1 }
findings.evidence: Lower opponent's anger 1 level.

findings.name: Blue Stance
findings.defect: No effect raises the card user's own anger; the parse only touches the opponent's anger, so the user gains nothing.
findings.expected: Additional effect { kind: 'changeAnger', target: 'user', delta: 2 }
findings.evidence: Raise your anger 2 levels.

findings.name: Frieza Smiles
findings.defect: attackType is hardcoded to 'energy', so the engine will refuse to let this card stop a physical attack even though the card explicitly stops either type. The 'any' attackType exists in the vocabulary.
findings.expected: { kind: 'stopAttack', attackType: 'any', window: 'thisAttack' }, plus a second stop for the remainder-of-Combat clause
findings.evidence: stops a physical or energy attack

findings.name: Goku's Super Saiyan Blast!
findings.defect: attackType is hardcoded to 'energy', silently removing this card's ability to stop a physical attack. The text covers both types and 'any' is available.
findings.expected: { kind: 'stopAttack', attackType: 'any', window: 'thisAttack' }
findings.evidence: Stops an opponent's physical or energy attack.

findings.name: Frieza's Force Bubble
findings.defect: Only the single-attack stop was parsed. The second, distinct sentence granting a blanket energy-attack lock for the rest of Combat is absent, so the card resolves as an ordinary one-shot stop.
findings.expected: Additional effect { kind: 'stopAttack', attackType: 'energy', window: 'thisCombat', scope: 'all' }
findings.evidence: Stops all energy attacks for the remainder of Combat.

findings.name: Black Swift Elbow Strike
findings.defect: The rider stop is given window 'thisAttack', which lasts only for the current attack. The card locks out energy attacks for the entire remaining combat, and 'thisCombat' with scope 'all' exists for exactly this.
findings.expected: { kind: 'stopAttack', attackType: 'energy', window: 'thisCombat', scope: 'all' }
findings.evidence: stops all energy attacks for the rest of this combat

findings.name: Jeice Flash Attack
findings.defect: The rider stop is given window 'thisAttack' instead of a rest-of-combat lock, so the engine drops the ongoing energy-attack denial after a single attack.
findings.expected: { kind: 'stopAttack', attackType: 'energy', window: 'thisCombat', scope: 'all' }
findings.evidence: stops opponents from making energy attacks for the rest of this combat

findings.name: A Hospital Stay
findings.defect: The power-up-to-highest-stage clause was dropped entirely; the parse only carries the anger gain and the remove-from-game. movePowerStage with to:'highest' is exactly the modeled vocabulary for this.
findings.expected: Additional effect { kind: 'movePowerStage', target: 'user', to: 'highest' }
findings.evidence: Power up your main personality to its highest stage.

findings.name: Alien Anger!
findings.defect: The 3-stage power up was dropped; only anger and remove-from-game were parsed. changePowerStages covers this exactly, so the user silently loses 3 power stages of gain.
findings.expected: Additional effect { kind: 'changePowerStages', target: 'user', delta: 3 }
findings.evidence: Power up 3 stages.

findings.name: Alien Anger!
findings.defect: No restriction was recorded, so the engine will let a Hero deck play a Villains-only card. The parser handled the equivalent 'Heroes only' clause on Gohan's Stomp and Hero Enraged! in this same batch.
findings.expected: restriction: { alignment: 'Villain' }
findings.evidence: Villains only.

findings.name: Goku's Energy Absorption
findings.defect: The rejuvenation clause was dropped; the parse keeps only the stop and the remove-from-game. rejuvenate is modeled vocabulary, so this is a lost effect, not a gap.
findings.expected: Additional effect { kind: 'rejuvenate', count: 2, from: 'choose' }
findings.evidence: Take two cards from your discard pile and put them at the bottom of your life card deck.

findings.name: Hero Enraged!
findings.defect: The rejuvenation clause was dropped; only the anger gain and remove-from-game were parsed, even though rejuvenate models this exactly.
findings.expected: Additional effect { kind: 'rejuvenate', count: 2, from: 'choose' }
findings.evidence: Take any 2 cards from your discard pile and place them at the bottom of your life deck.

findings.name: Frieza's Influencing Drill
findings.defect: Parsed as trigger 'onPlay', so the engine lowers the opponent's anger exactly once, the moment the Drill hits the table. This is a Drill: its effect is continuous and fires after each successful energy attack. The CRD (Drill Cards) states Drills 'are constantly in use ... and may even create effects multiple times within a turn', and the vocabulary has a 'constant' trigger for Drills.
findings.expected: trigger: 'constant' (the anger drop is a repeating conditional trigger, not a one-shot on play)
findings.evidence: after every successful energy attack against your opponent

findings.name: Gohan Anger Drill
findings.defect: Parsed as trigger 'onPlay', so the engine hands the user +1 anger immediately and unconditionally when the Drill is played. The card only grants anger inside a combat where both a physical and an energy attack succeed. Wrong trigger plus an unconditional payout.
findings.expected: trigger: 'constant' (conditional, once per combat), not an immediate onPlay anger gain
findings.evidence: Raise your anger 1 level when you successfully do a physical and energy attack in the same combat.

findings.name: Captain Ginyu Transformed
findings.defect: changeAnger with delta 0 is a no-op: the engine adds zero to the foe's anger and nothing happens. The card zeroes out the opponent's anger, which is a set-to-zero, not a delta. changeAnger has no toZero flag (unlike changePowerStages), so this parse silently discards the card's entire non-attack effect while appearing to model it.
findings.expected: Either a set-to-zero representation, or leave it as { kind: 'manual' } / needsReview rather than emit a delta-0 no-op
findings.evidence: Reduce opponent's anger to 0.

findings.name: Surprise Hit
findings.defect: damageStages is hardcoded to 1, but the +1 is per Non-Combat card in the user's discard pile. The engine will always add exactly +1 stage — too little in almost every real board state (and too much when the discard pile holds no Non-Combat cards).
findings.expected: A variable/count-scaled modifier, or { kind: 'manual' } instead of a fixed stages: 1
findings.evidence: +1 power stages of damage for each Non-Combat card in your discard pile

findings.name: Goku's Quickness
findings.defect: window is 'thisAttack' (the attack currently being resolved), but this is a Non-Combat card played outside combat that pre-empts an attack in a future combat. As parsed the engine would treat it as an in-combat reactive stop.
findings.expected: A forward-looking window ('nextPhase' is the closest modeled value), not 'thisAttack'; trigger is likewise closer to onPlay than to a reactive defense
findings.evidence: Stops the first physical attack in the next combat.

findings.name: Saiyan Protection Drill
findings.defect: window 'thisAttack' makes this a reactive stop that can be spent on any physical attack, including one another card already stopped. A Defense Shield only fires on the first attack that is still unstopped — CRD battle sequence step 7: 'If the attack was not stopped, the defender must now activate any Defense Shields'. 'firstSuccessful' is the modeled value for exactly this.
findings.expected: { kind: 'stopAttack', attackType: 'physical', window: 'firstSuccessful' }
findings.evidence: Stops the first unstopped physical attack performed against you during Combat.

findings.name: Saiyan Snap Kick
findings.defect: Parse adds a stopAttack{energy, thisAttack} effect. This card stops nothing — the clause is a rules note about how the *opponent* may stop THIS attack. The engine will let an attack card cancel an incoming energy attack.
findings.evidence: This attack can only be stopped as if it were an energy attack.
findings.expected: physicalAttack + damageStages 3 only; the stop-type clause has no vocabulary and should be dropped (or manual).

findings.name: Blue Diving Punch Drill
findings.defect: Parsed as a plain physicalAttack, so the engine rolls the Physical Attack Table and deals damage. The card explicitly deals NO damage at all — it is a damage-less attack used to trigger attack-dependent effects.
findings.evidence: Your opponent cannot take life cards or power stages of damage from this attack.
findings.expected: physicalAttack with powerStages: 0 (fixed 0 overrides the PAT default), or manual.

findings.name: Supreme Kai's Ki Push
findings.defect: lifeCards: 7 makes this a fixed 7-life-card attack. The +7 is an OPTIONAL, doubly-conditional bonus (Tokui-Waza declared, MP above level 1, pay a personality level). Base is the energy default of 4; if the bonus is taken it is 11, never 7.
findings.evidence: you may have him lose a personality level to have this attack do an additional +7 life cards of damage
findings.expected: energyAttack with no lifeCards override (default 4); the conditional +7 is not modelable.

findings.name: Saiyan Energy Toss
findings.defect: lifeCards: 2 caps this attack at 2 life cards. The +2 does not belong to this attack at all — it is a floating buff on OTHER attacks later in Combat, and it is conditional. This attack is a plain energy attack (4 life cards).
findings.evidence: for the remainder of Combat all of your other attacks do +2 life cards of damage
findings.expected: energyAttack with no lifeCards override (default 4).

findings.name: Black Strike
findings.defect: Only the life-card half of the damage was captured. The attack deals BOTH 2 life cards and 2 power stages; energyAttack has a powerStages field, so the second half is expressible and was dropped.
findings.evidence: Energy attack doing 2 life cards and 2 power stages of damage.
findings.expected: energyAttack { lifeCards: 2, powerStages: 2 }

findings.name: Saiyan Direct Strike
findings.defect: The +3 power stages of damage is missing entirely from the parse; the engine has damageStages for exactly this and the parser used it on every sibling card with the same wording (Saiyan Clothesline, Saiyan Surprise).
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing +3 power stages of damage
findings.expected: add { kind: 'damageStages', stages: 3 }

findings.name: Saiyan Direct Strike
findings.defect: lifeCards: 2 on physicalAttack is a FIXED override per abilities.ts, so the attack deals exactly 2 life cards and no Physical Attack Table damage. The text is a bonus (+2) added on top of the PAT base, not a replacement of it.
findings.evidence: and +2 life cards of damage
findings.expected: physicalAttack with no lifeCards override (PAT base) plus the +3 stage modifier; the '+2 life cards' bonus has no modifier vocabulary and should be flagged, not converted into a fixed base.

findings.name: Blue Evasion
findings.defect: The card changes anger in both directions; the parse only kept the opponent's. The user's own anger gain is dropped even though changeAnger{target:'user'} is available and used on nearly every other card in this batch.
findings.evidence: Raise your anger 1 level.
findings.expected: add { kind: 'changeAnger', target: 'user', delta: 1 }

findings.name: Blue Flip
findings.defect: The rejuvenation is dropped. This is exactly the rejuvenate effect kind (discard pile -> bottom of Life Deck, taken from the bottom of the discard pile), so it is vocabulary the engine has.
findings.evidence: Place the bottom card of your discard pile on the bottom of your Life Deck.
findings.expected: add { kind: 'rejuvenate', count: 1, from: 'bottom' }

findings.name: Saiyan Enraged
findings.defect: The 2-card rejuvenation is dropped, though rejuvenate models it exactly. The parse keeps the anger and the draw but silently loses the card recovery.
findings.evidence: Place the bottom 2 cards in your discard pile at the bottom of your Life Deck.
findings.expected: add { kind: 'rejuvenate', count: 2, from: 'bottom' }

findings.name: Saiyan Hurricane Kick
findings.defect: discardCards{target:'user', count:1} is parsed as a mandatory effect, but the discard is an OPTIONAL cost paid to buy a benefit the engine does not model (keeping the attack on the table). The engine will strip a card from the player's hand for nothing every time this attack is used.
findings.evidence: You may discard a card from your hand to have this attack stay on the table to be used one more time this Combat.
findings.expected: physicalAttack + damageStages 3 + removeFromGameAfterUse; no discard.

findings.name: Blue Head Charge
findings.defect: changeAnger{target:'foe', delta: 0} is a no-op — the engine applies nothing. The card zeroes the opponent's anger, which can be a swing of up to 5 levels. changeAnger has no toZero flag (only changePowerStages does), so this is not expressible and must not be emitted as a silent zero-delta.
findings.evidence: Lower your opponent's anger to 0.
findings.expected: a manual/needsReview flag rather than delta 0, since the anger-to-zero case has no vocabulary.

findings.name: Android 16's Battle Charge
findings.defect: damageStages: 1 hardcodes the per-Ally multiplier as a flat +1. The bonus scales with Allies in play: it is +0 with no Allies (the common case) and +3 with three, never a fixed +1.
findings.evidence: +1 power stage of damage for every Ally you have in play
findings.expected: physicalAttack with the variable modifier left unmodeled/flagged, since per-Ally scaling has no vocabulary.

findings.name: Underwater Kick
findings.defect: changeAnger{user,+2} is applied unconditionally, but the anger only happens for one specific Main Personality. Any other personality using this card would wrongly gain 2 anger levels. The parser correctly drops comparable conditionals elsewhere in this batch (Saiyan Surprise, Saiyan Clothesline).
findings.evidence: If performed by Videl and she is your Main Personality, raise your anger 2 levels.
findings.expected: physicalAttack + damageStages 3 only; the Videl-gated anger should be dropped or flagged.

findings.name: Saiyan Energy Toss
findings.defect: Second defect on this card: changeAnger{user,+1} is applied unconditionally, but it fires only when the attacker out-powers the defender. The engine will grant the anger on every use, including when the condition fails.
findings.evidence: If the personality performing this attack has a higher power rating than the personality defending against this attack, raise your anger 1 level
findings.expected: drop the conditional anger (as was done for the identical construction on Saiyan Surprise) or flag for review.

findings.name: Saiyan Enraged
findings.defect: Second defect on this card: drawCards{count:1} is applied unconditionally, but the draw is gated on a Main Personality power-rating comparison. The engine will draw a card even when the comparison fails.
findings.evidence: If your Main Personality's power rating is higher than your opponent's Main Personality's, draw a card.
findings.expected: drop the conditional draw or flag it, matching how the parser treats other power-rating conditionals in this batch.

findings.name: Heroic Charge
findings.defect: An attack card is parsed as a defense card. The parse has trigger 'defense' with a spurious stopAttack {any, thisAttack}, and drops the actual attack entirely. The parser latched onto the phrase 'stop an attack' inside a conditional clause that describes choosing a card from HAND to put into play, not stopping anything.
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing +4 power stages of damage. If performed against a Majin, choose a card in your hand that can perform an attack or stop an attack and place it into play.
findings.expected: trigger 'attack' with effects [{kind:'physicalAttack'},{kind:'damageStages',stages:4}]; no stopAttack effect at all.

findings.name: Heroic Head Throw
findings.defect: An attack card is parsed as a defense card. trigger is 'defense' with an unconditional stopAttack {any, thisAttack}, and the physical attack plus its +3 power stage modifier are missing. The stop clause in the text is conditional (only vs a Majin), applies to FOCUSED attacks in the opponent's next Attacker Attacks phase, and never stops the current attack.
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing +3 power stages of damage. If performed against a Majin, this attack does +5 power stages of damage instead and stops the 3 next focused attack your opponent performs TAA this Combat.
findings.expected: trigger 'attack' with [{kind:'physicalAttack'},{kind:'damageStages',stages:3},{kind:'changeAnger',target:'user',delta:1}]; the conditional focused-attack stop is not modelable and should be dropped, not asserted unconditionally.

findings.name: Black High Kick
findings.defect: Parsed as physicalAttack with lifeCards:2, which per abilities.ts is a FIXED base of 2 life cards that OVERRIDES the Physical Attack Table. The text prints a plain physical attack (PAT base) plus a variable bonus of +2 life cards per Dragon Ball controlled. With 0 Dragon Balls the parse deals a flat 2 life cards where the card should roll the PAT; the bonus is also multiplicative per Dragon Ball, not a flat 2.
findings.evidence: Physical attack. This attack does +2 life cards of damage for each Dragon Ball you control.
findings.expected: {kind:'physicalAttack'} with no lifeCards (PAT base); the per-Dragon-Ball bonus has no Effect vocabulary and should be left unmodeled/flagged.

findings.name: Black Uppercut
findings.defect: Spurious stopAttack {attackType:'any', window:'thisAttack'}. Nothing on this card stops an attack — the parser inverted a clause whose whole point is that it ONLY ends floating effects that do NOT stop attacks. The engine would let an attack card also cancel the opponent's attack.
findings.evidence: If successful, end any of your opponent's floating effects that do not stop attacks and that last "for the remainder of Combat."
findings.expected: Effects should be [{physicalAttack},{damageStages 3},{changeAnger user +1}] only; the floating-effect removal is not modelable.

findings.name: Blue Backhand
findings.defect: Spurious removeFromGameAfterUse. The text never removes this card from the game; the phrase 'remove themselves from the game after use' is part of a description of OTHER cards (your Non-Combat/Non-Drill cards), and the actual instruction is to place those at the bottom of the Life Deck. The engine would exile a card that should go to the discard pile.
findings.evidence: all of your Non-Combat/Non-Drill cards that do not remove themselves from the game after use are placed at the bottom of your Life Deck after use
findings.expected: Only [{kind:'physicalAttack',powerStages:5}]; no removeFromGameAfterUse.

findings.name: Devious Moves
findings.defect: changeAnger {user,+1} is applied unconditionally, but the text gates it on the personality being Majin Buu. Every other card in this batch with an 'If used by X' rider has that rider omitted, so here the engine will hand a free anger raise to any personality using the card.
findings.evidence: If used by Majin Buu, raise your anger 1 level.
findings.expected: Drop the changeAnger effect (or gate it via restriction.namedOnly ['Majin Buu']); unconditional effects are only the physical attack and +4 power stages.

findings.name: Black Shift Kick
findings.defect: stopAttack window is 'thisAttack', but the text delays the stop to the opponent's NEXT Attacker Attacks phase. As parsed, an attack card would consume its stop against the attack currently resolving (there is none during your own attack), and the real defensive window is lost.
findings.evidence: Stops an energy attack during your opponent's next "Attacker Attacks" phase.
findings.expected: {kind:'stopAttack', attackType:'energy', window:'nextPhase'}

findings.name: Black Shift Kick
findings.defect: Missing rejuvenation. The text moves 2 specific cards from the discard pile to the bottom of the Life Deck, which is exactly the rejuvenate effect kind (count 2, from 'bottom'); the parse drops it entirely.
findings.evidence: Place the bottom 2 cards of y our discard pile at the bottom of your Life Deck.
findings.expected: Add {kind:'rejuvenate', count:2, from:'bottom'}

findings.name: Energy Pouch
findings.defect: Missing rejuvenation. Moving the top card of the discard pile to the bottom of the Life Deck is the rejuvenate effect (count 1, from 'top'), and the engine has vocabulary for it, but the parse omits it.
findings.evidence: Place the top card of your discard pile at the bottom of your Life Deck.
findings.expected: Add {kind:'rejuvenate', count:1, from:'top'}

findings.name: Blue Knockdown
findings.defect: Missing movePowerStage. Raising your Main Personality to his highest power stage is directly representable as movePowerStage {target:'user', to:'highest'}, but the parse contains only the attack and its damage modifier.
findings.evidence: Raise your Main Personality to his highest power stage.
findings.expected: Add {kind:'movePowerStage', target:'user', to:'highest'}

findings.name: Goku's Quick Dodge
findings.defect: Missing movePowerStage. The card raises the user's Main Personality to his highest power stage — a modeled effect kind — but the parse contains only the stopAttack, so the power-stage swing silently never happens.
findings.evidence: Raise your Main Personality to his highest power stage
findings.expected: Add {kind:'movePowerStage', target:'user', to:'highest'} alongside the stopAttack.

findings.name: Yamcha's Skillful Defense
findings.defect: attackType is narrowed to 'energy' when the card stops either attack type. The engine would refuse to use this card against a physical attack, silently deleting half the card's function.
findings.evidence: Stops a physical or energy attack.
findings.expected: {kind:'stopAttack', attackType:'any', window:'thisAttack'}

findings.name: Goku's Flight
findings.defect: attackType is narrowed to 'energy' when the card stops either attack type, so the engine will not allow it against a physical attack.
findings.evidence: Stops a physical or energy attack.
findings.expected: {kind:'stopAttack', attackType:'any', window:'thisAttack'}

findings.name: Human Extinction Attack
findings.defect: The parse asserts lifeCards:8 although the damage figure is an unreadable glyph in the source text — the parser invented a specific number and did not flag needsReview. An energy attack defaults to 4 life cards, so a fabricated 8 doubles the card's output on a value the text does not support.
findings.evidence: Energy attack doing b life cards of damage.
findings.expected: No lifeCards override, or lifeCards flagged in needsReview pending a legible scan; the cost {powerStages:5} is correct.

findings.name: Majin Buu, Gohan Absorbed
findings.defect: stopAttack {physical,'thisAttack'} is attached as an unconditional rider on the attack, but the surviving text reads as an optional alternate use ('you may use ... stop physical attack') gated on a condition. As parsed, every use of this card both attacks for +8 power stages AND cancels a physical attack.
findings.evidence: If | 8 = Lou may use | stop physical attack
findings.expected: Keep [{physicalAttack},{damageStages 8}] and drop the stopAttack (or split it into a separate defense-triggered ability) until the card text is legible.

findings.name: Saiyan Face Stomp
findings.defect: The parse is `physicalAttack {lifeCards: 3}`, which per abilities.ts OVERRIDES the Physical Attack Table base with a fixed 3 life cards. Two errors compound: (a) the printed base modifier '+4 power stages of damage' is dropped entirely, and (b) the optional, Tokui-Waza-gated, discard-cost bonus of '+3 life cards' is promoted into the attack's fixed base damage. The card resolves as a flat 3-life-card attack instead of a PAT attack at +4 stages.
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing +4 power stages of damage. If you declared Toku-Waza, you may discard the top card from your Life Deck to do an additional +3 life cards of damage.
findings.expected: physicalAttack (no lifeCards, so PAT base is kept) plus damageStages {stages: 4}; the conditional/optional +3 life cards is not representable and should be left out or flagged for review.

findings.name: Saiyan Left Kick
findings.defect: Parsed as `physicalAttack {lifeCards: 4}`, which replaces the PAT base damage with a fixed 4 life cards. The text has no base override at all — it is a plain physical attack whose +4 life cards is ADDITIONAL damage gated on 'If successful'. The parse both destroys the power-stage base damage and makes the conditional bonus unconditional.
findings.evidence: Physical attack. If successful and you declared Tokui-Waza, this attack does +4 life cards of damage and raises your anger 1 level.
findings.expected: physicalAttack with no lifeCards field (PAT base preserved); the '+4 life cards' is an if-successful additional-damage rider, not a base override.

findings.name: Saiyan Flying Tackle
findings.defect: The parse applies `damageStages {stages: 6}` unconditionally. +6 is the 'instead' value that requires BOTH declaring Tokui-Waza AND discarding the top card of your Life Deck; the card's actual printed base modifier (rendered '3+ power stages', i.e. +3) is dropped. Every use of this card resolves at double the stage bonus it should have.
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing 3+ power stages of damage. If you declared Toku-Waza, you may discard the top card from your Life Deck when this card is played to do +6 power stages of damage instead.
findings.expected: damageStages {stages: 3} — the unconditional printed value; the +6 replacement depends on a declaration and a paid discard cost and cannot be applied by default.

findings.name: Saiyan Wrist Block
findings.defect: `attackType` is parsed as 'any', so the engine will let this card stop energy attacks. The card only stops physical attacks — it is a Physical Combat card and the text names the physical attack type explicitly. This makes the card strictly stronger than printed, which is the dangerous direction for a defense card.
findings.evidence: Stops a phisical attack.
findings.expected: stopAttack {attackType: 'physical', window: 'thisAttack'}

findings.name: Red Power Lift
findings.defect: The stopAttack is given `window: 'thisAttack'`. This card is an attack the user performs — there is no incoming attack at that moment for 'thisAttack' to consume. The text grants a stop against a FUTURE attack in the same Combat, so a 'thisAttack' window either fizzles or, worse, eats the wrong attack.
findings.evidence: Stops the next physical attack performed against you this Combat.
findings.expected: stopAttack {attackType: 'physical', window: 'nextPhase', scope: 'single'} — a single deferred stop, not a stop of the current attack.

findings.name: Saiyan Lightning Dodge
findings.defect: The parse contains only the stopAttack. The card's second sentence is an unconditional power-stage drain on the opponent and maps exactly onto an available Effect kind (`changePowerStages`), yet it is absent — the engine silently skips 4 stages of drain every time this card is played.
findings.evidence: Your opponent loses 4 power stages, to a minimum of 0.
findings.expected: add changePowerStages {target: 'foe', delta: -4} alongside the stopAttack.

findings.name: Red Lifting Kick
findings.defect: The parse has physicalAttack + damageStages 6 but omits the anger change entirely. This is an unconditional, immediate drawback (the cost of the large stage bonus) and `changeAnger` covers it exactly. As parsed, the card is pure upside with its downside deleted.
findings.evidence: Lower your anger 1 level.
findings.expected: add changeAnger {target: 'user', delta: -1}.

findings.name: Straining Jump Kick Move
findings.defect: The parse captures only the 7-life-card attack and the 2-stage cost; the anger swing is dropped. Raising the opponent 6 anger levels is the entire point of the card (it is a Straining card — the anger gift is its drawback) and `changeAnger` with target 'foe' covers it. Note the target here is the FOE and the delta is POSITIVE, the opposite of the usual anger rider, so silently dropping it changes the game state materially.
findings.evidence: If successful, raise your opponent's anger 6 levels.
findings.expected: add changeAnger {target: 'foe', delta: 6} (ideally gated on success; the Effect type has no ifSuccessful flag for changeAnger, so at minimum this belongs in needsReview rather than being dropped without trace).

findings.name: Yamcha's Right Cross
findings.defect: `changeAnger {target: 'foe', delta: 0}` is a no-op — a delta of zero changes nothing. The text is a SET-to-zero, not a delta: it wipes the opponent's anger entirely. The parse looks modeled but resolves as if the card's main effect did not exist.
findings.evidence: Lower your opponent's anger to 0 at the end of this Combat.
findings.expected: anger has no toZero flag in the Effect union (only changePowerStages has one), so this should be a manual effect or flagged in needsReview — not encoded as delta 0, which silently resolves wrong.

findings.name: Tien's Mental Conditioning
findings.defect: Parsed with trigger 'onPlay', but the card names the 'When entering Combat' timing, which is a distinct trigger in the AbilityTrigger union ('whenEnteringCombat') and a distinct step in the CRD Prepare Phase (CRD lines 261/267: both players use 'When entering Combat' effects during the Prepare Phase, each once). As 'onPlay' the engine would allow it at the wrong time.
findings.evidence: Use when entering Combat,
findings.expected: trigger: 'whenEnteringCombat'

findings.name: Tien's Mental Conditioning
findings.defect: Only the anger raise and remove-from-game are captured. The power-stage restoration is an unconditional effect with a dedicated Effect kind (`movePowerStage` with to: 'highest') and is missing, so the card grants none of its power recovery.
findings.evidence: Raise your Main Personality his highest power stage.
findings.expected: add movePowerStage {target: 'user', to: 'highest'}.

findings.name: Namekian Defensive Stance
findings.defect: The parse has no `restriction`, so the engine will let any personality play this card. The AbilityRestriction interface has a `namedOnly` field documented for exactly this wording ('Villains, Goku, and Gohan only'), and the card's first sentence is a hard personality restriction.
findings.evidence: Piccolo and Nail only.
findings.expected: restriction: {namedOnly: ['Piccolo', 'Nail']}

findings.name: Orange Uppercut
findings.defect: The parse is a bare physicalAttack plus removeFromGameAfterUse — the printed damage number is dropped completely, so the card resolves as an unmodified Physical Attack Table result. Whichever way the '4+' is read (a +4 stage modifier, or a 4-stage fixed base), the parse should carry a damage value and carries none. Same failure pattern as Red Knee Bash and Saiyan Flying Tackle, so it is systematic on this number format, not a one-off.
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing 4+ power stages of damage.
findings.expected: damageStages {stages: 4} (the '+4 power stages of damage' modifier form the parser handles correctly on Namekian Elbow Smash).

findings.name: Red Knee Bash
findings.defect: The parse captures the anger rider but drops the attack's damage number entirely, leaving a vanilla physicalAttack with an unmodified table result. The stage bonus is the card's primary effect.
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing 4+ power stages of damage.
findings.expected: add damageStages {stages: 4} to the existing physicalAttack.

findings.name: Blue Style Mastery
findings.defect: stopAttack is restricted to attackType 'energy', so the engine will refuse to stop physical attacks with a card that explicitly stops either type.
findings.evidence: to stop a physical or energy attack
findings.expected: stopAttack with attackType 'any' (window thisAttack)

findings.name: Blue Style Mastery
findings.defect: The mandatory hand-discard cost is missing, so the engine grants a free stop every Combat. AbilityCost.discard exists in the vocabulary and is unused here.
findings.evidence: you may discard a card from your hand to stop
findings.expected: cost: { discard: 1 }

findings.name: Blue Style Mastery
findings.defect: changeAnger foe -2 is applied unconditionally, but the card only lowers anger when the discarded card happens to be Blue Style. The engine will drain 2 anger levels on every use, including when a non-Blue card was pitched. Elsewhere in this batch the parser correctly DROPS unrepresentable conditionals (Cell's Last Strike, Namekian Dash Attack, Orange Deflection), so this is over-application, not a vocabulary gap.
findings.evidence: If that card is a Blue Style card, lower your opponent's anger 2 levels
findings.expected: omit changeAnger (condition is not representable), or gate it

findings.name: Cell's Choke Hold
findings.defect: '+1 life cards' is a MODIFIER on the Physical Attack Table result, but the parse sets physicalAttack.lifeCards = 1, which per abilities.ts OVERRIDES the PAT default. The attack is turned from 'table damage plus 1 life card' into a flat 1 life card, gutting its damage. (CRD confirms this wording is additive: Android 14 'physical attack doing +2 life cards of damage'.)
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing +1 life cards of damage
findings.expected: physicalAttack with no lifeCards override, plus a +1 life-card modifier (or manual flag) — never lifeCards:1

findings.name: Cell's Choke Hold
findings.defect: discardCards targets the wrong ZONE and the wrong COUNT. Per abilities.ts, discardCards is 'Discard from hand', but the card mills the opponent's LIFE DECK — and the amount is 2 per card in his hand, not a flat 2. With a 3-card hand the card removes 6 life cards; the parse removes 2 from hand.
findings.evidence: your opponent discards 2 cards from his Life Deck for each card in his hand
findings.expected: no discardCards effect (Life-Deck milling scaled by hand size is not representable) — leave as manual

findings.name: Just Thinking
findings.defect: The alignment restriction is dropped, so the engine will let Heroes play a Villains-only card. AbilityRestriction.alignment exists and is used correctly on Kami's Idea ('Heroes only') in this same batch.
findings.evidence: Villains only.
findings.expected: restriction: { alignment: 'Villain' }

findings.name: Namekian Energy Catch
findings.defect: The unconditional power-stage gain is missing entirely; the parse only stops the attack. changePowerStages is in the vocabulary and this clause has no condition or success gate.
findings.evidence: Gain 3 power stages.
findings.expected: add { kind: 'changePowerStages', target: 'user', delta: 3 }

findings.name: Namekian Fist Block
findings.defect: Same omission as Namekian Energy Catch: the unconditional 3-stage gain is dropped, leaving a plain stop. The defender silently loses 3 power stages of value every time this resolves.
findings.evidence: Gain 3 power stages.
findings.expected: add { kind: 'changePowerStages', target: 'user', delta: 3 }

findings.name: Namekian Fusion
findings.defect: The leading, unconditional power-stage reset is missing. movePowerStage { target, to: 'highest' } is exactly this effect and is unused, so the engine plays this card without ever raising the Main Personality.
findings.evidence: Raise your Main Personality to its highest power stage.
findings.expected: add { kind: 'movePowerStage', target: 'user', to: 'highest' } as the first effect

findings.name: Namekian Fusion
findings.defect: rejuvenate 2 is applied unconditionally, but the card only rejuvenates when the revealed card is a Namekian Style card. The engine will always return 2 cards to the Life Deck, regardless of what was drawn — a free 2-card swing on every play.
findings.evidence: If that card is a Namekian Style card, choose 2 cards from your discard pile and place them on the bottom of your Life Deck
findings.expected: omit the rejuvenate (the reveal condition is not representable), consistent with how other conditionals in this batch were dropped

findings.name: Namekian Side Kick
findings.defect: '+2 life cards' is a modifier on top of the Physical Attack Table result, but physicalAttack.lifeCards = 2 OVERRIDES the PAT default per abilities.ts. A strong rider attack becomes a flat 2-life-card attack.
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing +2 life cards of damage
findings.expected: physicalAttack with no lifeCards override (PAT damage plus 2 life cards); lifeCards:2 is only correct for 'doing 2 life cards of damage'

findings.name: Orange Energy Discharge
findings.defect: A spurious stopAttack (attackType 'any') was invented from a sentence that STOPS NOTHING — it is a restriction preventing the opponent from stopping THIS attack. The engine will let the attacker cancel one of the opponent's attacks that the card never stops.
findings.evidence: Your opponent may not use Energy Combat cards to stop this attack.
findings.expected: energyAttack lifeCards 6 only; the anti-stop clause is unmodelable and should be left out

findings.name: Orange Energy Focus
findings.defect: The printed cost is missing from the parse. Per CRD, an energy attack that does not state its cost gains the default 'Costs 2 power stages to perform', so the engine will charge 2 instead of the printed 1 — the card's whole point is the discount.
findings.evidence: Gosts 1 power stage to perform.
findings.expected: cost: { powerStages: 1 }

findings.name: Blue Straight Jab
findings.defect: ifSuccessful:true is attached to the damage modifier, but the 'If successful' clause in the text governs the anger reduction, not the +5 stages. The gate is on the wrong effect: the damage bonus is unconditional (compare Namekian Bash / Power Kick / Fist Smash in this batch, where identical '+N power stages' parse with no flag), while the anger loss — which should be gated — is applied unconditionally.
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing +5 power stages of damage. If successful, lower your opponent's anger 2 levels.
findings.expected: damageStages 5 with no ifSuccessful; the success gate belongs to the changeAnger, which the Effect type cannot currently express

findings.name: Black Pummeling Strike
findings.defect: An attack card is parsed as a defense card. The parse has trigger 'defense' with a stopAttack{any} and NO attack effect at all — the printed card is a physical attack. The parser almost certainly keyed on the phrase 'do not stop attacks' in the trailing restriction clause. As parsed, this card can be played to stop any attack (it cannot) and performs no attack (it must).
findings.evidence: Sensei Deck. Physical attack doing +3 life cards of damage.
findings.expected: trigger 'attack' with a physicalAttack effect (the '+3 life cards' is a modifier the engine has no kind for, but the base physical attack must be present); no stopAttack.

findings.name: Blue Buu Blast
findings.defect: Plain 'Energy attack' with no printed fixed damage was given lifeCards:1, which per abilities.ts OVERRIDES the 4-life-card energy default. The '1' was scraped from a conditional per-Drill bonus. The card is silently downgraded from 4 life cards to 1.
findings.evidence: Energy attack. If Earth Dragon Ball 1 or Earth Dragon Ball 2 is in play, this attack does +1 Life Card of damage for each Blue Style Drill you have in play.
findings.expected: {kind:'energyAttack'} with no lifeCards field (default 4 life cards); the conditional per-Drill '+1' is a modifier the engine cannot express and should be left out, not promoted to the base.

findings.name: Black Backstab
findings.defect: '+2 life cards' is a MODIFIER on top of the Physical Attack Table result, but it was parsed as physicalAttack{lifeCards:2}, which per abilities.ts is a fixed base that OVERRIDES the PAT damage. The attack loses all of its power-stage damage and becomes a flat 2-life-card hit.
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing +2 life cards of damage.
findings.expected: {kind:'physicalAttack'} with no lifeCards (PAT damage stands); the '+2 life cards' rider has no Effect kind and should be flagged, not encoded as the base.

findings.name: Majin Vegeta, the Malevolent
findings.defect: physicalAttack{lifeCards:4} turns a CONDITIONAL bonus ('an additional 4 life cards ... if performed against a Rogue') into the attack's fixed base, overriding the Physical Attack Table. Against a non-Rogue the card should deal PAT damage and zero life cards; as parsed it always deals exactly 4 life cards and no power stages.
findings.evidence: this attack does 7 an additional «4 life cards of damage
findings.expected: {kind:'physicalAttack'} with no lifeCards; the conditional +4 life cards is not expressible and should be left unmodeled.

findings.name: Majin Vegeta, the Malevolent
findings.defect: The printed, unconditional '+7 power stages of damage' is missing entirely from the parse. damageStages exists as an Effect kind and this is the plainest possible instance of it — the attack loses 7 stages of damage.
findings.evidence: Focused physical attack doing +7 power stages of damage.
findings.expected: add {kind:'damageStages', stages:7}

findings.name: Grand Kai's Palace
findings.defect: A Location with a replacement effect is parsed as a defense card that stops any attack and removes itself from the game. Both effects are spurious: the Location never stops an attack (it reacts to a Celestial Fighter's stop card), and the text does the OPPOSITE of removeFromGameAfterUse — it lets the stop card go to the bottom of the Life Deck INSTEAD of being removed. As parsed the player gains a free universal stop and the Location self-removes.
findings.evidence: When one of your Celestial Fighters stops an attack with a card that removes itself from the game after use, you may place that card at the bottom of your Life Deck instead of removing it from the game.
findings.expected: trigger 'constant' with {kind:'manual'} — a replacement effect the engine has no vocabulary for. No stopAttack, no removeFromGameAfterUse.

findings.name: Black Conservation Drill
findings.defect: A Non-Combat Drill is parsed as a defense card that stops any attack. The text does not stop anything — 'Whenever you stop an attack' is the TRIGGER CONDITION for a rejuvenation bonus. As parsed the player can play a Drill as a universal attack stop.
findings.evidence: Whenever you stop an attack, you may place the bottom card of your discard pile at the bottom of your Life Deck.
findings.expected: trigger 'constant'; the modelable payload is {kind:'rejuvenate', count:1, from:'bottom'}, never a stopAttack.

findings.name: Goku's Defensive Drill
findings.defect: Same defect as Black Conservation Drill: a Non-Combat Drill parsed as trigger 'defense' with stopAttack{any}. 'Whenever you stop an attack' is the condition that fires the Drill, not an effect the Drill grants. As parsed the Drill becomes a free stop for any attack.
findings.evidence: Whenever you stop an attack, you may shuffle the bottom card of your discard pile into your Life Deck.
findings.expected: trigger 'constant', no stopAttack; the rejuvenation/power-stage payoff is the actual effect.

findings.name: Majin Power Deflection
findings.defect: stopAttack{energy} is spurious. 'Use when you stop an energy attack' is the card's usage window — the stop has already happened by another card. As parsed this card itself stops an energy attack, doubling every real stop into two.
findings.evidence: Use when you stop an energy attack.
findings.expected: no stopAttack; the card's effects are the power-stage raise and the card draw.

findings.name: Majin Power Deflection
findings.defect: 'Raise your Main Personality to its highest power stage' is dropped, even though movePowerStage{target:'user', to:'highest'} exists for exactly this. The card's main benefit is unmodeled.
findings.evidence: Raise your Main Personality to its highest power stage.
findings.expected: add {kind:'movePowerStage', target:'user', to:'highest'}

findings.name: Android 18's Pressure Routine
findings.defect: stopAttack{physical, thisAttack} is spurious on an attack card. The text mentions stopping only to describe what the OPPONENT does ('if your opponent stops a physical attack'); the card grants the attacker nothing defensive. As parsed, performing this attack also stops a physical attack.
findings.evidence: if your opponent stops a physical attack performed by your Main Personality, your opponent must skip his next "Attacker Attacks" phase
findings.expected: physicalAttack + damageStages 2 + removeFromGameAfterUse only; the opponent-side skip is a conditional floating effect (stunSkipNextPhase gated on the opponent stopping) that should not surface as a stop for the user.

findings.name: Black Choke Hold
findings.defect: stopAttack is attached as an unconditional rider on the attack, but the text makes it a mutually exclusive ALTERNATIVE mode with a cost ('instead by removing 3 Rares'). As parsed, performing the attack also stops an attack for free. The attackType is additionally narrowed to 'energy' when the text covers physical too.
findings.evidence: You can use this card to stop a physical or energy attack instead by removing 3 Rares in your discard pile from the game.
findings.expected: attack ability = physicalAttack + damageStages 4 + removeFromGameAfterUse, with no stopAttack; the defensive mode is a separate cost-gated alternative and would be attackType 'any', not 'energy'.

findings.name: Blue Shifting Maneuver
findings.defect: 'a physical or energy attack' was parsed as attackType 'energy', silently dropping physical. The engine would refuse to let this card stop a physical attack, which is half of what it does.
findings.evidence: Stops a physical or energy attack.
findings.expected: {kind:'stopAttack', attackType:'any', window:'thisAttack'}

findings.name: Blue Speediness
findings.defect: Same narrowing as Blue Shifting Maneuver: 'a physical or energy attack' became attackType 'energy'. The card cannot stop physical attacks in the engine even though it is printed to.
findings.evidence: Stops a physical or energy attack.
findings.expected: {kind:'stopAttack', attackType:'any', window:'thisAttack'}

findings.name: Blue Energy Dive
findings.defect: The printed energy attack is missing entirely — the parse is trigger 'defense' with only a stop and a self-removal. This card is an Energy Combat card that performs a 6-life-card attack; as parsed it deals no damage at all.
findings.evidence: Energy attack doing 6 life cards of damage.
findings.expected: trigger 'attack' with {kind:'energyAttack', lifeCards:6} present alongside the stop rider.

findings.name: Blue Energy Dive
findings.defect: The stop's window is 'thisAttack', but the text explicitly delays it to the opponent's NEXT Attacker Attacks phase — the schema's 'nextPhase' means exactly 'foe's next'. As parsed the stop can be spent immediately in the current attack.
findings.evidence: Stops an energy attack performed against you during your opponent's next "Attacker Attacks" phase.
findings.expected: {kind:'stopAttack', attackType:'energy', window:'nextPhase'}

findings.name: Majin Dabura's Offensive Leverage
findings.defect: preventLifeCards was tagged attackType 'energy'. The word 'energy' in the text describes the TRIGGER (your own successful energy attack), not the attacks being mitigated — the prevention applies to every attack the opponent performs. As parsed, physical attacks are not mitigated at all.
findings.evidence: prevent 3 life cards of damage from every attack your opponent performs
findings.expected: {kind:'preventLifeCards', amount:3, attackType:'any'}

findings.name: Majin Dabura's Petrifying Spit
findings.defect: discardCards{foe,1} is spurious and the two effects are wrongly combined. The opponent is never forced to discard — discarding is his OPTION to deny the draw, and the draw and the discard are mutually exclusive ('Unless'). As parsed the engine forces a discard AND draws a card.
findings.evidence: Unless your opponent discards a card from his hand when the Ally is removed, draw a card.
findings.expected: drawCards 1 (plus a manual/needsReview flag for the opponent's opt-out); no forced discardCards on the foe.

findings.name: Majin Defense Drill
findings.defect: Window 'thisAttack' is wrong for a Defense Shield. The schema's 'firstSuccessful' is defined as 'the first that gets through', which is exactly 'the first unstopped attack'. CRD battle-sequence step 7 fires Defense Shields only after an attack is NOT stopped; 'thisAttack' lets the engine spend it on any attack at the defender's choosing.
findings.evidence: Defense Shield: Stops the first unstopped attack performed against you each Combat.
findings.expected: {kind:'stopAttack', attackType:'any', window:'firstSuccessful'}

findings.name: Majin Vegeta's Frantic Attack
findings.defect: The 'If successful' gate is attached to the wrong effect. The damage rider '+1 power stages' is printed unconditionally, while the anger raise is the gated one; the parse marks damageStages ifSuccessful:true and leaves changeAnger immediate. Net effect: the engine raises the user's anger even when the attack is stopped.
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing +1 power stages of damage. If successful, raise your anger 1 level.
findings.expected: {kind:'damageStages', stages:1} without ifSuccessful, and the anger raise gated on success (or flagged in needsReview since changeAnger has no ifSuccessful field).

findings.name: Majin Vegeta
findings.defect: The printed '+4 power stages' damage rider is dropped — the parse has a bare physicalAttack plus the anger. The damage clause is legible despite the surrounding OCR noise, and damageStages is available. The attack loses 4 stages of damage.
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing +4 ‘power stages of
findings.expected: add {kind:'damageStages', stages:4}

findings.name: Goku's Energy Clash
findings.defect: The mandatory discard cost is dropped. AbilityCost.discard exists (and discardCards with target 'user' is documented as a cost), so this is expressible. As parsed the stop is free, and a player with an empty hand can still use it.
findings.evidence: You must discard an energy combat card from your hand to use this card.
findings.expected: cost: { discard: 1 } alongside the stopAttack

findings.name: Majin Buu's Goo
findings.defect: The attack's fixed base of 3 power stages is dropped entirely, and the variable per-attached-card life-card bonus is turned into a fixed base override of 1 life card. The parse resolves as a physical attack dealing a flat 1 life card and no power-stage damage at all.
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing 3 power stages of damage and +1 life cards of damage for each of your attached cards in play.
findings.expected: physicalAttack with powerStages: 3 (a fixed base, per CRD 'Goku's Surprise Attack ... Physical attack doing 5 power stages of damage'), with the '+1 life cards for each attached card' left unmodeled/needsReview rather than written as lifeCards: 1

findings.name: Straining Power Move
findings.defect: '+1 life cards ... for each Straining Move card in your discard pile' is an additive, variable modifier on the default energy-attack damage, but it is parsed as lifeCards: 1, which per abilities.ts OVERRIDES the 4-life-card default. The engine deals 1 life card where the card should deal 4 + (1 per Straining Move card in discard).
findings.evidence: Energy attack doing +1 life cards of damage for each Straining Move card in your discard pile.
findings.expected: energyAttack with no lifeCards override (default 4), plus the per-card bonus left unmodeled/flagged in needsReview — never lifeCards: 1

findings.name: Narrow Escape
findings.defect: The card stops a physical OR an energy attack, but the parse restricts the stop to attackType 'energy'. The engine will refuse to let this card stop a physical attack, silently losing half the card's defensive coverage.
findings.evidence: Stops a physical or energy attack.
findings.expected: stopAttack with attackType: 'any', window: 'thisAttack'

findings.name: Orange Protection Drill
findings.defect: This is a Non-Combat Drill that has no stop of its own — it triggers off a stop you already made with another card and upgrades it to a combat-long, all-attacks stop of that same type. The parse gives the Drill a free single-attack energy stop it does not have: wrong source of the stop, wrong attack type (the type is whatever you just stopped, physical or energy), and wrong window (remainder of Combat / all, not thisAttack).
findings.evidence: you may remove this Drill from the game when you stop a physical or energy attack to stop all of your opponent's attacks of the same type for the remainder of Combat
findings.expected: no self-contained stopAttack; a constant/Drill-trigger ability with the upgrade left unmodeled (manual/needsReview), or at minimum window 'thisCombat' with scope 'all' and attackType matching the stopped attack — not a fabricated single energy stop

findings.name: Majin Buu's Taunt
findings.defect: Anger is applied to the wrong player: the text raises the OPPONENT's anger (pushing the foe toward a personality level), but the parse raises the USER's anger by 2. The engine advances the wrong player's Main Personality. (The effect is also optional and conditional on a successful attack this Combat, so it should not fire unconditionally.)
findings.evidence: You may raise your opponent's anger up by 2 levels if one of your attacks has been successful this Combat.
findings.expected: changeAnger with target: 'foe', delta: +2 (and ideally not applied unconditionally)

findings.name: Red Repeating Flares
findings.defect: The hand discard is optional and is the PRICE for +3 life cards of damage. The parse makes it a mandatory discardCards on the user while omitting the damage it buys, so the engine throws away a card from hand every time this attack is performed and still only deals 2 life cards.
findings.evidence: You may discard a card from your hand when you perform this attack to do an additional +3 life cards of damage.
findings.expected: no unconditional discardCards; either omit the optional trade entirely or model it as an optional cost paired with the +3 life cards

findings.name: Saiyan Spidletop Punch
findings.defect: The +1 anger is gated behind a compound condition — the attack must be successful AND the card you named must have turned up among the life cards of damage — but the parse applies changeAnger user +1 unconditionally, so the engine raises anger on every use (including when the attack is stopped).
findings.evidence: If successful and the named card was one of the life cards of damage from this attack, remove your opponent's discard pile from the game and raise your anger 1 level.
findings.expected: no changeAnger effect (the condition is unmodelable), or the anger flagged in needsReview — not an unconditional +1

findings.name: Majin Buu's Heel Kick
findings.defect: The self power-stage gain is dropped, even though changePowerStages is available vocabulary. The engine performs the attack and never gives the attacker his 3 power stages.
findings.evidence: The personality performing this attack gains 3 power stages.
findings.expected: add { kind: 'changePowerStages', target: 'user', delta: 3 }

findings.name: Piccolo's Destruction Attack
findings.defect: 'Gain 4 power stages' is omitted from the parse despite changePowerStages being available vocabulary; the attacker never gains the stages.
findings.evidence: Gain 4 power stages.
findings.expected: add { kind: 'changePowerStages', target: 'user', delta: 4 }

findings.name: Orange Strength
findings.defect: The power-stage reset is omitted, though movePowerStage is exactly the vocabulary for it. The engine performs the attack and leaves the Main Personality wherever it was.
findings.evidence: Raise your Main Personality to his highest power stage.
findings.expected: add { kind: 'movePowerStage', target: 'user', to: 'highest' }

findings.name: Saiyan Neutralization
findings.defect: The forced skip of the opponent's next attack phase is dropped, though stunSkipNextPhase is available vocabulary. The engine lets the opponent attack normally next phase.
findings.evidence: Your opponent must skip his next "Attacker Attacks" phase.
findings.expected: add { kind: 'stunSkipNextPhase' }

findings.name: Majin Buu's Bicycle Kick
findings.defect: The 'If successful' gate is attached to the wrong effect. The +5 power stages is stated unconditionally in its own sentence but is flagged ifSuccessful: true, while the anger drop — which the text does gate on success — is parsed with no gate, so the engine lowers the foe's anger 2 levels even when the attack is stopped.
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing +5 power stages of damage. If successful, lower your opponent's anger 2 levels
findings.expected: damageStages 5 without ifSuccessful; the changeAnger foe -2 gated on success (or omitted/needsReview, since the Effect type has no ifSuccessful on changeAnger)

findings.name: Red Static Shot
findings.defect: The anger gain is gated on the attack getting through, but is parsed as an immediate effect, so the engine raises the user's anger 2 levels even when the attack is stopped.
findings.evidence: If successful, raise your anger 2 levels.
findings.expected: the changeAnger user +2 gated on success, or omitted/flagged in needsReview rather than applied unconditionally

findings.name: Bracing for Impact
findings.defect: Parsed as an attack card (trigger 'attack' with an energyAttack effect), but the card performs no attack at all — it is a defensive damage cap on ALL energy attacks for the remainder of Combat. The parser's `startsEnergy` regex matched the plural statement 'Energy attacks do...' as a declaration of an energy attack. Playing it would launch a 4-life-card energy attack (engine defaults energyLifeCards to 4) that does not exist on the card.
findings.evidence: Energy attacks do a maximum of 2 life cards and 0 power stages of damage for the remainder of Combat.
findings.expected: No attack effect and no 'attack' trigger; a defensive/continuous damage cap (nearest vocabulary: a damage-limiting effect, otherwise manual). Certainly not { kind: 'energyAttack' }.

findings.name: Gohan's Kick
findings.defect: Spurious stopAttack rider. The text never stops an attack — it forbids the OPPONENT from using cards that stop attacks. The parser matched the phrase 'stops all physical attacks' inside a prohibition clause and turned it into an offensive rider, so the engine will stop a physical attack on top of dealing damage.
findings.evidence: Cards that end Combat, or cards that stops all physical attacks or energy attacks, cannot be used for the remainder of Combat
findings.expected: [{ kind: 'physicalAttack' }, { kind: 'damageStages', stages: 3 }] only — the stop-suppression clause has no vocabulary and should be dropped, not converted into a stopAttack.

findings.name: Blue Arm Blast
