findings.defect: 'If successful' is attached to the wrong effect. The +4 power stages is the attack's unconditional damage modifier (it is printed before the 'If successful' clause); the gate belongs on the stop. As parsed, a stopped attack loses its damage bonus and the free stop still fires.
findings.expected: damageStages 4 with no ifSuccessful; the stopAttack is what should be gated on success
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing +4 power stages of damage. If successful, stop an energy attack performed by your opponent during their next "Attacker Attacks" phase.

findings.name: Blue Forward Foot Sweep
findings.defect: The stopAttack window is 'thisAttack', but the card stops an attack in the opponent's NEXT Attacker Attacks phase — a later window. As parsed the engine would consume the stop during the current attack (where the user is the attacker and nothing is incoming), losing the actual effect.
findings.expected: stopAttack attackType 'energy', window 'nextPhase'
findings.evidence: stop an energy attack performed by your opponent during their next "Attacker Attacks" phase

findings.name: Blue Frustration Drill
findings.defect: Parse invents a stopAttack (any/thisAttack) and a 'defense' trigger. This Drill stops nothing — the opponent stopping YOUR attack is a trigger condition for you LOSING power stages. As parsed the engine gains a free universal attack-stopper and never applies the drawback or the +2 stage damage buff. It is also a constant Drill, not a hand-played defense (CRD line 636).
findings.expected: trigger 'constant'; no stopAttack effect (the stage loss and +2 stage damage buff are the real content)
findings.evidence: Whenever your opponent stops 1 of your attacks you lose 2 power stages.

findings.name: Blue Hip Spring Throw
findings.defect: The stopAttack window is 'thisAttack', but the stop applies to the opponent's next Attacker Attacks phase. The engine would burn the stop during the user's own attack instead of holding it for the opponent's next attack phase.
findings.expected: stopAttack attackType 'physical', window 'nextPhase'
findings.evidence: Stop a physical attack performed by your opponent during their next "Attacker Attacks" phase.

findings.name: Blue Shoulder Wheel
findings.defect: The card changes both players' anger, but only the opponent's decrease is parsed; the user's own +1 anger is dropped. Both clauses are plainly present and changeAnger handles both targets.
findings.expected: add { kind: 'changeAnger', target: 'user', delta: 1 } alongside the existing foe -1
findings.evidence: Raise your anger 1 level. Lower your opponent's anger 1 level.

findings.name: Burning Rage!
findings.defect: The anger gain is dropped; only the rejuvenation is parsed. Same omission as its sibling card Blazing Anger!.
findings.expected: add { kind: 'changeAnger', target: 'user', delta: 2 }
findings.evidence: Increase your anger level by 2.

findings.name: Burning Rage!
findings.defect: The card leaves the game after use, but removeFromGameAfterUse is absent, so the engine returns it to the discard pile where it can be rejuvenated and replayed. The parser caught the identical clause on Baba's Energy Blast.
findings.expected: add { kind: 'removeFromGameAfterUse' }
findings.evidence: Discard this card from the game after use.

findings.name: Cell's Aerial Maneuvers
findings.defect: '+1 life cards' is a modifier on top of the Physical Attack Table result, but the parse encodes lifeCards: 1, which per abilities.ts is a fixed base that OVERRIDES the default. The attack would deal exactly 1 life card and no power-stage damage — strictly worse than the printed card.
findings.expected: physicalAttack with no lifeCards override, plus a +1 life-card modifier
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing +1 life cards of damage.

findings.name: Goku, the Mighty
findings.defect: This is a Personality card (power levels 775,000 / 750,000 / 725,000, 'EXCLUSIVE'). Its power is a rejuvenation trigger that fires WHEN you stop an attack with a Frieza Saga card — the card itself stops nothing. The parse invents a full 'stopAttack any / thisAttack' defense ability, so the engine would let this personality card be played as a universal attack-stopper.
findings.evidence: Whenever you stop an — attack with a card from 750.000 \ the Frieza Saga, you may shuffle it back into your 725.000 Life Deck after use.
findings.expected: trigger 'constant' (or 'personalityPower') with effects [{kind:'manual'}] — no stopAttack effect at all

findings.name: Mighty Mask
findings.defect: Personality card with a Constant Combat Power (power levels 1,770,000 / 1,730,000). Like Goku the Mighty, the stop is the TRIGGER CONDITION for recycling a Red Style card, not an effect the card provides. Parse fabricates a 'stopAttack any' defense ability, so the engine would treat a personality as a playable stop card.
findings.evidence: whenever you stop an attack your hard with a Red Style card, you may that Red Style card into your Life Deck after use
findings.expected: trigger 'constant' with effects [{kind:'manual'}] — no stopAttack effect

findings.name: King Kai
findings.defect: The card's primary mode is an ENERGY ATTACK; stopping a physical attack is only a conditional alternative gated on declaring a Black Tokui-Waza ('instead'). The parse drops the attack entirely and files the card as a pure defense, so the engine can never use its main mode. Note the sibling parse tts-be34bddc-32 keeps the attack and the alternative — this one is inconsistent with it.
findings.evidence: Energy attack. If you have 3 or = more anger, this attack costs 0 power stages to perform. If you | declared a Black Tokui-Waza, you 0000 may stop a physical attack instead.
findings.expected: trigger 'attack' with an {kind:'energyAttack'} effect (default 4 life cards), not trigger 'defense' with only stopAttack

findings.name: It's the Little Things That Matter
findings.defect: Text stops EITHER an energy OR a physical attack; the parse narrows attackType to 'physical' only, so the engine will refuse to let it stop energy attacks — exactly half its function. CRD line 1762 confirms the errata wording 'energy or physical'. The window is also wrong: a Defense Shield fires on the first attack that gets through, not on an arbitrary current attack.
findings.evidence: Stops the first unstopped energy or physical attack performed against you this combat.
findings.expected: {kind:'stopAttack', attackType:'any', window:'firstSuccessful'}

findings.name: Mother's Touch
findings.defect: Text stops either a physical OR an energy attack; the parse narrows attackType to 'energy' only, so the engine will not let it stop physical attacks.
findings.evidence: Stops a physical or energy attack.
findings.expected: {kind:'stopAttack', attackType:'any', window:'thisAttack'}

findings.name: Gohan's Physical Attack
findings.defect: The power-stage gain is dropped entirely. The parse has physicalAttack + anger but no changePowerStages, so the user never gains the 5 stages — a large swing given stages drive the Physical Attack Table.
findings.evidence: Gain 5 power stages.
findings.expected: add {kind:'changePowerStages', target:'user', delta:5}

findings.name: Hidden Power Level
findings.defect: The parse contains only the physical attack; the power-stage move is dropped even though the vocabulary has an exact match for it.
findings.evidence: Raise your Main Personality to its highest power stage.
findings.expected: add {kind:'movePowerStage', target:'user', to:'highest'}

findings.name: Champion Drill
findings.defect: Only the discard COST is parsed; the actual payoff — drawing two cards — is missing. As parsed the card is pure downside: the player discards a card and gets nothing.
findings.evidence: discard a card from your hand and draw the top two cards from your Life Deck
findings.expected: add {kind:'drawCards', count:2} alongside the discardCards cost

findings.name: Garlic Jur.'s Palm Blast
findings.defect: The mandatory discard is dropped; the parse contains only energyAttack. The user would never pay the card's printed cost.
findings.evidence: Discard a card.
findings.expected: add {kind:'discardCards', target:'user', count:1} (or cost.discard = 1)

findings.name: Krillin's Energy Attack
findings.defect: '2 draws from the life card deck' is a fixed base that OVERRIDES the energy default of 4 life cards, but no lifeCards value was set — the engine will deal 4 instead of 2, double the printed damage. The identical construction on Chiaotzu's Energy Manipulation ('forcing 3 draws from the life deck') in this same batch was parsed as lifeCards 3, so this is internally inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Energy attack doing 2 draws from the life card deck if not stopped.
findings.expected: {kind:'energyAttack', lifeCards:2}

findings.name: Excitement
findings.defect: The draw count is variable (one per Non-Combat card in hand) but is hard-coded to 1. With a typical hand this under-draws badly, and it is never correct except by coincidence — a hand with zero Non-Combat cards still draws 1.
findings.evidence: Draw a card for each Non-Combat card in your hand.
findings.expected: a variable/manual draw, not a fixed {kind:'drawCards', count:1}

findings.name: Dragon's Demise
findings.defect: The printed performance cost is dropped, so the engine falls back to the energy default of 2 power stages instead of 7 — the card's entire drawback. The parser did capture cost.powerStages for 'Costs 1 power stage to perform' on King Kai (tts-be34bddc-31) and Krillin's Energy Disk, so the omission is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Costs 7/7 power stages to perform.
findings.expected: cost: { powerStages: 7 }

findings.name: King Kai
findings.defect: The stop is an ALTERNATIVE mode ('instead') conditional on a Black Tokui-Waza declaration, but it is placed in the same effects array as the attack, so the engine resolves the physical attack AND stops an energy attack from one play. The card can only do one or the other.
findings.evidence: If you declared a Black Tokui-Waza, you may use this power to stop an energy attack instead.
findings.expected: the attack mode alone ({physicalAttack} + damageStages 2); the 'instead' branch is not expressible and should not be a co-resolving effect

findings.name: Gohan's Defense Drill
findings.defect: The personality restriction is dropped — the parse has no `restriction`, so the engine lets any Main Personality use a Gohan-only Defense Shield. The parser did capture restriction.alignment for 'Heroes only' twice in this same batch.
findings.evidence: League and Gohan only.
findings.expected: restriction: { namedOnly: ['Gohan'] }

findings.name: Fall 7 times, get up 8 times.
findings.defect: Window is 'thisAttack' (the attack currently being resolved, player's choice of when to use it), but a Defense Shield is not a hand-played stop — CRD glossary: 'Defense Shields attempt to stop the first unstopped attack', and step 7 of the battle sequence activates them only after an attack is not stopped. As parsed the player could hold it and spend it on any attack they like.
findings.evidence: Defense Shield: Stops the first unstopped physical attack performed against you this combat.
findings.expected: {kind:'stopAttack', attackType:'physical', window:'firstSuccessful'}

findings.name: Fortify Your Spirit
findings.defect: Same as its physical counterpart: a Defense Shield fires automatically on the first energy attack that gets through, but the parse uses window 'thisAttack', letting the engine treat it as a freely-timed hand stop.
findings.evidence: Defense Shield: Stops the first unstopped energy attack performed against you this combat.
findings.expected: {kind:'stopAttack', attackType:'energy', window:'firstSuccessful'}

findings.name: Saiyan Conservation
findings.defect: The parse invents a drawCards effect. The card never draws cards — "If you draw 2 cards with your Mastery" is a CONDITION on a Mastery-granted draw, not an effect the card produces. The engine would hand the player 2 free cards every time this attachment is played.
findings.evidence: If you draw 2 cards with your Mastery while this card is attached, you may shuffle the top card of your discard pile back into your Life Deck
findings.expected: No drawCards effect. The card's only modeled content would be the conditional rejuvenate-1 / raise-to-highest-power-stage, which is gated on a Mastery draw; a bare manual effect (and trigger 'constant', since it is an attachment with an ongoing conditional benefit) is correct here, not drawCards:2 on onPlay.

findings.name: Saiyan Energy Aura
findings.defect: The card stops TWO energy attacks — the one being resolved now AND one in the opponent's next phase — but the parse emits only the nextPhase stop. Used as a defense, the engine would let the incoming attack resolve in full.
findings.evidence: Stops an energy attack and stops energy attacks in the next phase.
findings.expected: Two effects: stopAttack{attackType:'energy', window:'thisAttack'} plus stopAttack{attackType:'energy', window:'nextPhase'}. CRD errata confirms: "Stops an energy attack and stops an energy attack during your opponent's next Attacker Attacks phase."

findings.name: Saiyan Sweeping Defense
findings.defect: Same defect as Saiyan Energy Aura: the immediate stop is dropped and only the next-phase stop is parsed, so defending with this card would not stop the attack it is played against.
findings.evidence: Stops a physical attack and stops physical attacks in the next phase.
findings.expected: stopAttack{attackType:'physical', window:'thisAttack'} AND stopAttack{attackType:'physical', window:'nextPhase'}. CRD errata: "Stops a physical attack and stops a physical attack during your opponent's next Attacker Attacks phase."

findings.name: Saiyan Pressure Punch
findings.defect: The damage modifier is missing entirely — the parse is a bare physical attack, so the engine resolves plain Physical Attack Table damage with no bonus. The OCR misspelling "succesful" appears to have defeated the modifier match.
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing +3 stages of physical damage if succesful.
findings.expected: physicalAttack plus damageStages{stages:3, ifSuccessful:true} — identical shape to Red Reverse Punch in this same batch.

findings.name: Saiyan Training
findings.defect: The restriction lists a personality the card never names. "Gohan" is fabricated — the text (and CRD errata) restrict the card to Villains and Goku only, so the engine would legally allow a Gohan Main Personality to play it.
findings.evidence: Villains and Goku only.
findings.expected: restriction.namedOnly = ["Villains", "Goku"] — no Gohan.

findings.name: Straining Fake Left Move
findings.defect: The parse has no cost at all, so the engine grants the 3-life-card prevention for free. The card charges 4 power stages; the parser appears to only recognize "to perform" and missed "to use".
findings.evidence: Costs 4 power stages to use.
findings.expected: cost: { powerStages: 4 } alongside preventLifeCards{amount:3, attackType:'energy'} — the same cost the parser correctly captured on Straining Tripping Move ("Costs 4 power stages to perform").

findings.name: T-Rex Defense
findings.defect: Wrong stop window. This is a Defense Shield that sits in play and stops the first attack that gets through, not a card played against the attack currently being resolved; window 'thisAttack' makes the engine consume it on whatever attack is in front of it rather than the first unstopped one.
findings.evidence: stop the first unstopped attack performed against you
findings.expected: stopAttack{attackType:'any', window:'firstSuccessful'} — the enum documents firstSuccessful as "the first that gets through", and CRD battle-sequence step 7 activates Defense Shields only after an attack is not stopped.

findings.name: Saiyan City Destruction
findings.defect: The alignment restriction is dropped, so the engine would let a Hero deck play a Villains-only card. The parser demonstrably can emit restrictions (it emitted one for Saiyan Training in this batch), and 'Villain' is directly expressible via AbilityRestriction.alignment.
findings.evidence: Villains only.
findings.expected: restriction: { alignment: 'Villain' } on the parsed ability.

findings.name: Straining Energy Defense Move
findings.defect: The mandatory hand-discard cost is omitted, so the engine lets the player stop an energy attack for free. AbilityCost.discard (and discardCards with target 'user' "as a cost") exist precisely for this.
findings.evidence: You must discard a card from your hand as a cost to use this card.
findings.expected: cost: { discard: 1 } alongside the stopAttack effect.

findings.name: Straining Head Lock Move
findings.defect: Same as Straining Energy Defense Move: the required hand discard is not represented anywhere in the parse, so the physical stop resolves at no cost.
findings.evidence: You must discard a card from your hand as a cost to use this card.
findings.expected: cost: { discard: 1 } alongside stopAttack{attackType:'physical', window:'thisAttack'}.

findings.name: Namekian Tornado Attack
findings.defect: The 6 power stages of damage and the +1 anger are both conditional on having declared a Tokui-Waza, but the parse makes them unconditional. It sets physicalAttack.powerStages=6, which per the schema OVERRIDES the Physical Attack Table base for every use of the card, and fires changeAnger user +1 always. A deck with no Mastery/Tokui-Waza (optional per CRD: 'To declare a Tokui-Waza, your Life Deck must have a Mastery card') gets a free 6-stage attack plus an anger level it is not entitled to. The base attack is a plain 'Physical attack' (PAT damage). The removeFromGameAfterUse is likewise conditional ('Unless your Main Personality is Pikkon').
findings.evidence: If you declared a Tokui-Waza, this attack does 6 power stages of damage and raises your anger 1 level.
findings.expected: physicalAttack with no fixed powerStages (PAT base), no changeAnger; the conditional 6-stage/anger clause is not expressible and should be omitted or flagged for review.

findings.name: Orange Diving Attack
findings.defect: Damage is variable — 1 power stage PER Blue Style card in the discard pile — but the parse hard-codes powerStages:1, which per the schema overrides the Physical Attack Table with a flat 1 stage. This is wrong in both directions: it caps a potentially large attack at 1 stage, and it replaces the table base even when the discard pile is empty (in which case the attack should do 0).
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing 1 power stage of damage for each Blue Style card in your discard pile.
findings.expected: Variable damage is not expressible; leave the attack without a fixed powerStages value and flag for review rather than asserting a flat 1.

findings.name: Goku's Quickness Drill
findings.defect: The parse contains a discardCards effect targeting the foe, but nothing in the text ever makes the opponent discard. The text describes the OPPONENT's card making YOU discard from your hand — the user is the one discarding, and even that is a condition, not an effect this card produces. The engine will make the opponent throw away a card that the printed card never takes.
findings.evidence: Whenever an opponent's card makes you discard a card from your hand, draw a card afterward.
findings.expected: No discardCards effect at all (and certainly not target 'foe').

findings.name: Goku's Quickness Drill
findings.defect: Trigger is 'onPlay', so drawCards:1 resolves immediately when the Drill hits the table. The text's draw is a floating trigger on a Drill that only fires when an opponent's card forces a discard. This is a Drill (Non-Combat, continuous), which the schema covers with the 'constant' trigger. As parsed, playing the Drill is a free card every time.
findings.evidence: Whenever an opponent's card makes you discard a card from your hand, draw a card afterward.
findings.expected: trigger 'constant'; the conditional floating draw is not expressible and should be omitted rather than converted into an immediate on-play draw.

findings.name: Like Father, Like Son
findings.defect: Trigger 'onPlay' makes the engine lower the opponent's anger 1 level the moment this attachment is played, once. The text gives no on-play effect at all: it is a continuous attachment whose anger drain fires per successful physical attack by the attached personality. The opponent loses an anger level they should never lose, and loses it at the wrong time.
findings.evidence: All physical attacks this personality performs do +1 power stages of damage, and if successful, lower your opponent's anger 1 level.
findings.expected: trigger 'constant' (attachment); the per-attack, if-successful anger drain is not expressible as a one-shot onPlay effect and should be omitted or flagged.

findings.name: Namekian Elbow Strike
findings.defect: The rejuvenate is gated on the attack being STOPPED, but the parse applies it unconditionally, so it also fires when the attack succeeds. The parse gets the branch exactly backwards for the normal (successful-attack) case. Compare Hercule's Drop Kick in the same batch, where an identically gated 'If stopped, gain 3 power stages' was correctly omitted.
findings.evidence: If stopped, place the top card of your discard pile at the bottom of your Life Deck.
findings.expected: No rejuvenate effect (the 'if stopped' gate is not expressible), leaving physicalAttack + damageStages 3 only.

findings.name: Heroic Block
findings.defect: The card stops either attack type, but the parse restricts stopAttack to attackType 'physical', so an energy attack by a Majin will not be stopped. The schema provides attackType 'any' for exactly this case.
findings.evidence: Stops a physical attack or energy attack performed by a Majin.
findings.expected: stopAttack with attackType 'any'.

findings.name: Majin's Perfect Defense
findings.defect: The card stops either attack type, but the parse restricts stopAttack to attackType 'energy', so it silently fails to stop physical attacks — and 'physical' is the type named first in the text.
findings.evidence: Stops a physical or energy attack.
findings.expected: stopAttack with attackType 'any'.

findings.name: Namekian Pikkon's Defense
findings.defect: The card stops either attack type, but the parse restricts stopAttack to attackType 'energy', so physical attacks pass through unstopped.
findings.evidence: Stops a physical or energy attack.
findings.expected: stopAttack with attackType 'any'.

findings.name: Namekian Focused Kick
findings.defect: The unconditional power-stage gain is missing from the parse. 'Gain 4 power stages.' is its own sentence with no condition and no 'if successful' gate, and changePowerStages is in the schema vocabulary, so the parser had everything it needed. The user loses 4 stages of power they are owed on every use.
findings.evidence: Gain 4 power stages.
findings.expected: Add { kind: 'changePowerStages', target: 'user', delta: 4 } alongside physicalAttack + damageStages 5.

findings.name: Chapuchai, the Tiny
findings.defect: The rejuvenation is missing entirely. It is unconditional (no Tokui-Waza or success gate), comes off the bottom of the discard pile, and maps exactly onto the schema's rejuvenate effect with from:'bottom' — the same shape the parser produced for Namekian Eye Beam in this batch. As parsed the card only blocks and never returns the two cards.
findings.evidence: Place the bottom 2 cards of your discard pile at the bottom of your Life Deck.
findings.expected: Add { kind: 'rejuvenate', count: 2, from: 'bottom' } after the stopAttack.

findings.name: Namekian Eye Beam
findings.defect: The rejuvenate is gated on the attack being successful, but the parse applies it unconditionally, so the player also returns 3 cards to their Life Deck when the attack is stopped — the branch where the text instead removes 2 cards from the game. The rejuvenate effect kind has no ifSuccessful field, so this gate cannot be expressed and the effect should not have been asserted.
findings.evidence: If successful, place the bottom 3 cards of your discard pile at the bottom of your Life Deck. If stopped, remove the bottom 2 cards of your discard pile from the game.
findings.expected: energyAttack lifeCards 6 only, with the conditional rejuvenate omitted or flagged in needsReview.

findings.name: Face Off
findings.defect: The unconditional power-stage restoration is dropped. The schema has movePowerStage with to:'highest' for exactly this wording, and the clause has no condition attached. Only the anger raise was captured, so the card's main board effect never happens.
findings.evidence: Raise Majin Vegeta and Goku to their highest power stage.
findings.expected: Add a movePowerStage {to: 'highest'} effect (note the text raises both named personalities, so the single target field will need review) in addition to changeAnger user +1.

findings.name: Face Off
findings.defect: Trigger is 'onPlay' although the text names the timing window explicitly, and the schema has a dedicated 'whenEnteringCombat' trigger. As parsed the card can be used in any Non-Combat play window rather than only on entering Combat.
findings.evidence: Use when entering Combat.
findings.expected: trigger 'whenEnteringCombat'.

findings.name: Majin Fist Block
findings.defect: This is a dual-mode card and the parse keeps only the defensive half, silently deleting the offensive half. The attack mode is stated first in the text and is fully expressible (physicalAttack + damageStages 3). As parsed the card can never be played as an attack.
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing +3 power stages of damage or stops a physical attack.
findings.expected: Represent both modes — an attack ability (physicalAttack + damageStages 3) alongside the defense (stopAttack physical) — or flag the dropped mode in needsReview.

findings.name: Ultra Uppercut
findings.defect: `physicalAttack.lifeCards: 3` encodes a FIXED life-card base, which the engine uses INSTEAD of Physical Attack Table damage (combat.ts:248-255 takes the life-card branch and returns before the power-stage path). The text's '+3 life cards of damage' is an ADDITIVE rider on top of normal physical damage, not a replacement for it.
findings.evidence: Focused physical attack doing +3 power stages of damage and +3 life cards of damage.
findings.expected: physicalAttack with NO lifeCards override (so PAT damage still applies), plus the +3 life cards as an additive modifier. As parsed, a big attack silently becomes a flat 3-life-card attack that deals zero power stages.

findings.name: Triple Torpedo
findings.defect: `energyAttack.lifeCards: 2` sets a fixed base of 2 life cards, overriding the 4-life-card energy default. The text's '+2 life cards ... for each Ally' is a per-Ally ADDITIVE modifier on top of the default. The parse makes the card strictly WEAKER than a vanilla energy attack (2 instead of 4+), the opposite of what it does.
findings.evidence: Energy attack doing +2 life cards of damage for each Ally in play with the Bojack Unbound Subset Symbol.
findings.expected: energyAttack with no lifeCards override (default 4); the per-Ally +2 has no vocabulary and should be left unmodeled/flagged rather than collapsed into the base.

findings.name: Chiaotzu's Physical Defense
findings.defect: The card's entire defensive function is dropped — the only effect parsed is removeFromGameAfterUse. `preventLifeCards` exists in the vocabulary and covers this. CRD errata (line 1499) confirms: 'Stops all heroes from losing 1 life card of damage from every attack for the remainder of Combat.'
findings.evidence: Stops all heroes from losing 1 life card for this entire combat.
findings.expected: { kind: 'preventLifeCards', amount: 1, attackType: 'any' } alongside removeFromGameAfterUse. As parsed the card is played, removed from the game, and prevents nothing.

findings.name: Ally's Sacrifice
findings.defect: Parsed as stopping ONE energy attack right now. The card stops BOTH attack types for the whole combat: attackType should be 'any' (not 'energy'), window should be 'thisCombat' (not 'thisAttack'), scope 'all'. CRD errata line 1323 confirms the wording verbatim.
findings.evidence: Stops all of your opponent's physical and energy attacks for the remainder of combat.
findings.expected: { kind: 'stopAttack', attackType: 'any', window: 'thisCombat', scope: 'all' } — as parsed, physical attacks get through and the effect expires after one attack.

findings.name: Ultimate Defense
findings.defect: attackType is narrowed to 'energy', so the parse cannot stop a physical attack — but the card explicitly stops either type. (Note the card is even printed as a Physical Combat card.)
findings.evidence: Stops a physical or energy attack.
findings.expected: { kind: 'stopAttack', attackType: 'any', window: 'thisAttack' }

findings.name: Baba's Energy Blast
findings.defect: `discardCards` is hand discard — the engine resolves it via discardFromHand (abilities.ts:87-89, 141-143). The card discards off the opponent's LIFE DECK, which is a different zone and a different game consequence (life-deck loss is a step toward decking out / drawing damage, hand loss is not). CRD errata line 1365 confirms 'Life Deck'.
findings.evidence: Your opponent discards 3 cards from his life deck.
findings.expected: No discardCards effect. There is no life-deck-discard effect kind, so this should be left unmodeled (manual) rather than silently mapped onto the opponent's hand.

findings.name: Trunks Back Bash
findings.defect: The parsed stopAttack {any, thisAttack} appears nowhere in the text. The only mention of stopping is a past-tense CONDITION ('you stopped an opponent's attack during his previous phase'); the actual conditional effect is that the opponent must pass next phase. As parsed, this attack card also stops the current attack, unconditionally and regardless of who uses it.
findings.evidence: If used by Trunks and you stopped an opponent's attack during his previous "Attacker Attacks" phase, your opponent must pass during his next "Attacker Attacks" phase.
findings.expected: No stopAttack effect. At most a Trunks-restricted, condition-gated stop with window 'nextPhase' and scope 'all' — never window 'thisAttack'.

findings.name: Black Takedown Drill
findings.defect: Trigger 'onPlay' with drawCards 1 makes the engine draw a card the moment the Drill hits the table. The draw is a once-per-Combat option that fires AFTER a successful attack; the card is a Non-Combat Drill, which the vocabulary covers with trigger 'constant' ('Drills / continuous').
findings.evidence: Once per Combat, you may draw a card after performing a successful attack.
findings.expected: trigger 'constant' (the post-successful-attack, once-per-combat gating is a known vocabulary gap) — not an immediate draw on play.

findings.name: Blue Forward Foot Sweep
findings.defect: stopAttack window is 'thisAttack', i.e. the engine records a stop against the attack currently being resolved — but this is the attacker's own attack card, and the stop applies to a future phase. The vocabulary has 'nextPhase' ('foe's next') for exactly this.
findings.evidence: If successful, stop an energy attack performed by your opponent during their next "Attacker Attacks" phase.
findings.expected: { kind: 'stopAttack', attackType: 'energy', window: 'nextPhase' }

findings.name: Blue Hip Spring Throw
findings.defect: Same window error: the stop is scheduled against the opponent's next Attacker Attacks phase, but is parsed as window 'thisAttack' on the attacker's own attack.
findings.evidence: Stop a physical attack performed by your opponent during their next "Attacker Attacks" phase.
findings.expected: { kind: 'stopAttack', attackType: 'physical', window: 'nextPhase' }

findings.name: Ultra Uppercut
findings.defect: The '+3 power stages of damage' modifier is absent from the parse entirely — there is no damageStages effect. (Compounded by the lifeCards override above, the card currently deals no power-stage damage at all.)
findings.evidence: doing +3 power stages of damage and +3 life cards of damage
findings.expected: { kind: 'damageStages', stages: 3 }

findings.name: Black Fore FIst Punch
findings.defect: The if-successful power-stage drain on the opponent is dropped; only the energy attack is parsed. `changePowerStages` with target 'foe' exists in the vocabulary. CRD errata line 1386 confirms the text word-for-word.
findings.evidence: If successful, your opponent loses 3 power stages, to a minimum of 0.
findings.expected: { kind: 'changePowerStages', target: 'foe', delta: -3 } in addition to the energyAttack.

findings.name: Uub's Crushing Dive
findings.defect: The card raises the user's anger AND lowers the opponent's; the parse kept only the opponent's. The user-side anger gain is silently lost, which matters for anger-threshold level-ups.
findings.evidence: Raise your anger 1 level. Lower your opponent's anger 1 level.
findings.expected: { kind: 'changeAnger', target: 'user', delta: 1 } in addition to the existing foe -1.

findings.name: Blue Shoulder Wheel
findings.defect: Same both-directions anger text, and again only the opponent's anger reduction was parsed; the user's anger gain is missing.
findings.evidence: Raise your anger 1 level. Lower your opponent's anger 1 level.
findings.expected: { kind: 'changeAnger', target: 'user', delta: 1 } in addition to the existing foe -1.

findings.name: Blazing Anger!
findings.defect: The card's headline effect — a 2-level anger gain — is missing; only the rejuvenation was parsed. This is a Non-Combat card whose whole point is the anger, and anger drives Main Personality level-ups.
findings.evidence: Increase your anger level by 2.
findings.expected: { kind: 'changeAnger', target: 'user', delta: 2 } alongside the rejuvenate.

findings.name: Burning Rage!
findings.defect: Missing the 2-level anger gain (only rejuvenate was parsed). Also missing removeFromGameAfterUse — the card removes itself from the game, so as parsed it goes to the discard pile and can be rejuvenated back and reused.
findings.evidence: Increase your anger level by 2. / Discard this card from the game after use.
findings.expected: { kind: 'changeAnger', target: 'user', delta: 2 } and { kind: 'removeFromGameAfterUse' } alongside the rejuvenate.

findings.name: Enraged!
findings.defect: Missing the 2-level anger gain (only rejuvenate was parsed). Also missing removeFromGameAfterUse for the once-only removal clause, so the parsed card is reusable out of the discard pile.
findings.evidence: Increase your anger level by 2. / Discard this card from the game after one use.
findings.expected: { kind: 'changeAnger', target: 'user', delta: 2 } and { kind: 'removeFromGameAfterUse' } alongside the rejuvenate.

findings.name: Uub's Crushing Dive
findings.defect: The power-stage gain is not parsed. `changePowerStages` with target 'user' is available vocabulary. (It may be contingent on the preceding 'Discard an Ally in play' sentence, which is why I rate this medium rather than high — but the parse contains no trace of it either way.)
findings.evidence: Gain 3 power stages.
findings.expected: { kind: 'changePowerStages', target: 'user', delta: 3 } (Empower 3 and the in-play Ally discard are genuine vocabulary gaps and are not counted here).

findings.name: Piccolo's Flight
findings.defect: Parse restricts the stop to energy attacks only; the card stops either attack type, so the engine will refuse to stop physical attacks with it.
findings.evidence: Stops a successful physical or energy attack.

findings.name: Namekian Expendables
findings.defect: A conditional per-Ally BONUS was converted into the attack's fixed base damage. Setting lifeCards:3 overrides the 4-life-card energy default (CRD line 343), so a plain use of this card deals 3 instead of 4 — the parse both invents a base and lowers damage.
findings.evidence: For each ally discarded in this way. this attack does an additional +3 life cards of damage.
findings.expected: energyAttack with NO lifeCards field (default 4 life cards); the per-Ally +3 is an unmodelable conditional rider

findings.name: Namekian Punisher
findings.defect: Same class of error: a conditional per-Dragon-Ball bonus (+2) was written as the attack's fixed base, overriding the 4-life-card energy default. The card as parsed deals 2 life cards where it should deal 4.
findings.evidence: this attack does +2 life cards of damage for each Oragon Ball in both players' removed from game piles
findings.expected: energyAttack with NO lifeCards field (default 4 life cards)

findings.name: Red Back Kick
findings.defect: The anger effect on the card is entirely absent from the parse.
findings.evidence: Foe's anger level decreases by 1.
findings.expected: additional effect { kind: 'changeAnger', target: 'foe', delta: -1 }

findings.name: Red Back Kick
findings.defect: The combat-long energy shutdown was narrowed to a single-attack stop, so the engine drops the ongoing protection after one attack.
findings.evidence: Stops all energy attacks for the rest of this combat.
findings.expected: stopAttack { attackType: 'energy', window: 'thisCombat', scope: 'all' } rather than window 'thisAttack'

findings.name: Nappa's Energy Aura
findings.defect: Only the first clause was parsed. The second, independent clause — a combat-long shutdown of energy attacks, confirmed by CRD errata line 1930 — is dropped, so the engine stops one attack instead of every energy attack that Combat.
findings.evidence: and stop all energy attacks performed against you for the remainder of Combat
findings.expected: a second stopAttack { attackType: 'energy', window: 'thisCombat', scope: 'all' } alongside the thisAttack stop

findings.name: Nappa's Physical Resistance

findings.expected: a second stopAttack { attackType: 'physical', window: 'thisCombat', scope: 'all' }

findings.name: Raditz Total Defense
findings.defect: The card's cost is dropped entirely — no cost object on the ability — so the engine lets this stop be used for free. The parser does model costs (Piccolo's Energy Attack cost 5, Raditz Energy Burst cost 0), and CRD line 397 confirms the word 'costs' establishes a real cost.

findings.name: Pep Talk

findings.name: Pikkon's Leg Catch

findings.name: Red Coordination Drill

findings.evidence: When entering combat as the defender you may draw a card.
findings.expected: trigger 'whenEnteringCombat' (not 'onPlay'), with the defender-side condition noted

findings.name: Red Knee Pick Drill

findings.expected: trigger 'whenEnteringCombat' (not 'onPlay')

findings.name: Red Commander, Red's Command
findings.defect: The card deals POWER STAGES of damage, but the parse leaves energyAttack with no override, which per the schema comment falls back to the 4-life-cards energy default — the wrong damage currency, not merely the wrong amount. The OCR-garbled digit is not the issue; 'power stages of damage' is legible.

findings.name: Piccolo Sidestep!

findings.expected: additional effect { kind: 'removeFromGameAfterUse' }

findings.name: Raditz Flying Kick
findings.defect: Parsed as a bare physicalAttack, which resolves at normal Physical Attack Table damage — one third of what the card does. CRD errata line 2068 confirms the tripling is real. The parser flags uncertainty elsewhere (needsReview 'focusedAttack', 'energyLifeCards') but silently emits a normal attack here.
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing triple the base damage (damage from the physical attack table), before any modifiers are added.
findings.expected: no faithful representation exists in the Effect union, so the ability should carry a needsReview flag (or a manual effect) instead of a clean physicalAttack that resolves at 1x

findings.name: Unbelievable Strength

findings.name: Vegeta's Surprise Defense

findings.evidence: Stops a pysical or energy attack.

findings.name: Vegeta's Physical Stance
findings.defect: Only the single immediate stop was captured; the second, much larger clause — a blanket stop of all physical attacks for the rest of Combat — was dropped even though the engine has window 'thisCombat' / scope 'all' vocabulary for exactly this.

findings.name: Black Duck

findings.name: Victorious Drill

findings.expected: changePowerStages { target: 'user', delta: 2 } alongside the changeAnger

findings.name: Victorious Drill
findings.defect: Trigger is 'onPlay', so the effect fires once when the drill hits the table. The printed trigger is entering Combat, i.e. it recurs every Combat — 'whenEnteringCombat' exists in the trigger vocabulary.

findings.expected: trigger 'whenEnteringCombat' (or 'constant'), not 'onPlay'

findings.name: Taunting Drill
findings.defect: drawCards count 1 models a flat bonus draw. The card is an optional REPLACEMENT for the normal 3-card draw with a variable count (1 per Dragon Ball controlled). As parsed the user draws an extra card he is not entitled to, and with 0-2 Dragon Balls the real card is a net loss, not a gain.
findings.evidence: draw 1 card for every Dragon Ball that you control, instead of drawing 3 cards
findings.expected: not representable as a fixed drawCards count — should be manual, not drawCards { count: 1 }

findings.name: Tapion, Legendary Hero
findings.defect: changeAnger +8 is invented from the anger THRESHOLD condition; the card never raises anger by 8. The only anger gain on the card is +1, and that belongs to the granted ability on "Sword" attacks, not to Tapion himself.
findings.evidence: Whenever you reach S or more anger
findings.expected: no changeAnger effect on this card (the +1 is text granted to Sword-titled attacks); manual

findings.name: Blue Fire Kick
findings.defect: The attack effects and a physical-attack stop are both emitted, but the stop is an ALTERNATIVE mode of use, gated on Tokui-Waza + Pikkon. As parsed the card attacks for +5 stages AND stops an attack in the same use.
findings.evidence: you may use this card to stop a physical attack instead

findings.name: Black Back Power Hit

findings.name: Victorious

findings.name: Blue Defensive Stance

findings.expected: a prevention effect for 5 (units are power stages, which preventLifeCards does not express) — at minimum a manual/needsReview flag rather than an anger-only parse

findings.name: Blue Lightning Block
findings.defect: The +2 anger is applied unconditionally, but it is double-gated on Tokui-Waza declarations the engine cannot check. Sibling cards in this batch (Black Fist Catch, Black Diving Elbow Strike) correctly DROP their Tokui-Waza-gated riders; this one fires them always.

findings.name: Vegeta's Gutter Wallop
findings.defect: The +3 anger is applied unconditionally by any personality, but the card gates it on both success AND the user being Vegeta / Majin Vegeta.
findings.evidence: If 4 successful and used by Vegeta Majin Vegeta. Raise your anger 3 levels.
findings.expected: changeAnger dropped or gated; at minimum restriction/needsReview noting the named-personality and success gate

findings.name: Blue Right Power Strike
findings.defect: ifSuccessful is attached to the damage modifier, while the effect the text actually gates on success (the anger gain) is emitted unconditionally — the gate is on exactly the wrong effect. The +3 stages are unconditional on the printed card.
findings.evidence: Physical attack doing +3 power stages of damage. If successful and you declared a Tokui-Waza, raise your anger 1 level.

findings.name: Black Light Jab

findings.name: The Smackdown

findings.name: Saiyan Kamehameha

The parser picked up 'energy' from the attack sentence, not the prevent clause. It is also applied unconditionally despite being gated on both players declaring a Tokui-Waza.
findings.evidence: prevent 5 life cards of damage from the next attack performed against you this Combat
findings.expected: attackType: 'any' (and gated, or omitted since the condition is not expressible)

findings.defect: cost.powerStages is set to 0 for THIS card, but the text grants the 0-stage cost to the NEXT energy attack, and only if a Tokui-Waza was declared. findings.evidence: Stops the first unstopped energy attack performed against you during Combat.
findings.expected: window: 'firstSuccessful'

findings.name: Red Energy Drill
findings.defect: A Non-Combat card in play with a Defense Shield is given trigger 'defense', which the schema defines as a card used to defend (starburst) from hand. This Drill is never played from hand during combat; its shield activates from play.
findings.evidence: Defense Shield: Stops the first unstopped energy attack performed against you during Combat.
findings.expected: trigger: 'constant' (Drill / continuous card in play)

verdicts.reason: Printed text gates the anger on 'If the personality performing this attack has a higher power rating than the personality defending', but the parse emits changeAnger{user,+1} as a flat second effect with no needsReview marker, so it fires on every use. Not a vocabulary gap: the parser handled the byte-identical construction on Saiyan Surprise (tts-6a69cdcc-17) by dropping the conditional clause entirely, so this is inconsistent over-application.
verdicts.fixHint: Drop the changeAnger effect (Effect has no condition field), or keep it and add needsReview:['conditional anger'] so it is not silently auto-applied. Match the Saiyan Surprise treatment.

verdicts.reason: 'If your Main Personality's power rating is higher than your opponent's Main Personality's, draw a card' is a gated clause, but drawCards{count:1} sits unconditionally between changeAnger and removeFromGameAfterUse. The engine draws even when the comparison fails. The unconditional 'Raise your anger 2 levels' was parsed correctly, which shows the parser did read sentence boundaries — it just ignored the conditional.
verdicts.fixHint: Remove drawCards{count:1}, or flag via needsReview. (Separately, the unconditional rejuvenate from 'Place the bottom 2 cards in your discard pile at the bottom of your Life Deck' is also missing — rejuvenate{count:2,from:'bottom'} — but that is outside this claim.)

verdicts.reason: Blue Style Mastery / stopAttack attackType. The vision-verified text reads 'to stop a physical or energy attack', but the parse pins attackType:'energy'. The vocabulary explicitly supports AttackKind|'any', so the engine will refuse the stop against a physical attack that the card plainly covers. Plain contradiction between printed text and parse.
verdicts.fixHint: Change to { kind:'stopAttack', attackType:'any', window:'thisAttack' }.

verdicts.reason: Blue Style Mastery / missing discard cost. 'you may discard a card from your hand to stop' is a mandatory cost for the stop, and AbilityCost.discard exists in the vocabulary but the ability has no cost object at all. As parsed the engine gets an unconditional free stop, which is a strictly stronger card than printed.
verdicts.fixHint: Add cost: { discard: 1 } to the ability. (The 'Once per Combat' limiter is a separate, genuinely unmodeled concept — not part of this fix.)

verdicts.reason: Blue Style Mastery / spurious anger drain. 'If that card is a Blue Style card, lower your opponent's anger 2 levels' is gated on the identity of the discarded card, yet changeAnger{foe,-2} is emitted unconditionally with no needsReview. The target and sign are right, but the gate is gone, so every stop drains 2 anger. The same parser dropped unrepresentable conditionals on Cell's Last Strike, Namekian Dash Attack and Orange Deflection in this batch, so this is over-application rather than a missing-vocabulary complaint.
verdicts.fixHint: Omit the changeAnger effect (the 'discarded card is Blue Style' predicate is not representable), or retain it only with needsReview flagging the condition.

verdicts.reason: Cell's Choke Hold / damage. Text is 'Physical attack doing +1 life cards of damage' — additive. abilities.ts states that setting lifeCards OVERRIDES the default, and CRD line 343 says PAT supplies base damage 'unless it is already stated on the physical attack'; '+1' does not state a base. CRD line 1332/1335 (Android 14, 'physical attack doing +2 life cards of damage') confirms the additive reading of this exact wording. physicalAttack{lifeCards:1} therefore replaces the whole PAT result with a flat 1 life card, gutting the attack.
verdicts.fixHint: Emit { kind:'physicalAttack' } with no lifeCards override. There is no '+N life cards' modifier in the Effect union (damageStages is power stages only), so add the +1 via needsReview/manual rather than encoding it as a base — never lifeCards:1.

verdicts.reason: Cell's Choke Hold / discardCards. abilities.ts defines discardCards as 'Discard from hand', but the card reads 'your opponent discards 2 cards from his Life Deck for each card in his hand' — a different zone (CRD line 154 treats Life Deck discarding as life-card damage, not hand discard) and a hand-size-scaled count, not a flat 2. This is an actively wrong effect, not merely absent vocabulary: against a 3-card hand the card mills 6 life cards while the parse strips 2 cards from hand. The 'If successful' gate is also lost, since only damageStages carries ifSuccessful.
verdicts.fixHint: Remove the discardCards effect and leave the clause manual/needsReview until a life-deck-mill effect with a scaling count (and a success gate) exists.

verdicts.reason: 'Villains only.' is the first sentence of the printed text and the ability carries no restriction object. AbilityRestriction.alignment exists and the same batch applies it correctly on Kami's Idea (tts-76cb49e3-64, restriction:{alignment:'Hero'}) from the identical 'Heroes only.' construction, so this is a straightforward dropped restriction, not a gap. CRD line 904 confirms alignment restrictions are enforced (even Rogues cannot bypass them).
verdicts.fixHint: Add restriction: { alignment: 'Villain' } to the ability. The energyAttack{lifeCards:6} and cost{powerStages:1} parts are correct.

verdicts.reason: Text is 'Stops an energy attack. Gain 3 power stages.' — two sentences, the second with no condition and no 'if successful' gate. The parse contains only stopAttack, so the second sentence is silently lost even though changePowerStages{target,delta} covers it exactly.
verdicts.fixHint: Append { kind:'changePowerStages', target:'user', delta:3 } after the stopAttack effect.

verdicts.reason: Identical omission to Namekian Energy Catch: printed text 'Stops a physical attack. Gain 3 power stages.' but the ability holds only stopAttack{attackType:'physical'}. The unconditional 3-stage gain is representable with existing vocabulary and is simply absent.
verdicts.fixHint: Append { kind:'changePowerStages', target:'user', delta:3 }. Likely one parser bug shared with tts-f71532b6-44 — a 'Gain N power stages' sentence following a stop clause is not being consumed.

verdicts.reason: Namekian Fusion / missing power-stage reset. The card's first sentence, 'Raise your Main Personality to its highest power stage', is unconditional, and movePowerStage{target,to:'highest'} models it exactly, yet the parse begins at drawCards. The engine plays the card without ever raising the Main Personality. Confirmed representable: the same phrase appears on Kami's Idea, where it was dropped only because it sat behind a condition — here there is none.
verdicts.fixHint: Insert { kind:'movePowerStage', target:'user', to:'highest' } as the first effect, before drawCards.

verdicts.reason: Namekian Fusion / spurious rejuvenate. The rejuvenation is gated on the revealed card: 'If that card is a Namekian Style card, choose 2 cards from your discard pile and place them on the bottom of your Life Deck.' The parse emits rejuvenate{count:2,from:'choose'} unconditionally with no needsReview, so every play returns 2 cards regardless of the reveal. Same over-application pattern the parser avoided on Cell's Last Strike, Namekian Dash Attack and Orange Deflection.
verdicts.fixHint: Omit the rejuvenate effect (the reveal predicate is not representable), or keep it only with needsReview naming the condition.

verdicts.reason: Text reads 'Lower opponent's anger 2 levels' but the foe effect carries delta -1. The mirror card Blue Stance ('Raise your anger 2 / Lower opponent's 1') parsed as foe -2, proving the parser binds the FIRST numeral in the text to the foe clause rather than to its own sentence. No CRD errata exists for this card, so the printed text stands.
verdicts.fixHint: Bind each anger magnitude to the sentence/clause it appears in rather than taking the first numeral matched in the card text; the raise/lower clauses must be tokenized as separate statements before number extraction.

verdicts.reason: Printed text contains 'Raise your anger 1 level' and the parse has exactly one changeAnger effect, targeted at foe. Per the stated rule, 'raise your anger' targets the USER, so a {user,+1} effect is plainly absent. Same root cause as the wrong-number claim (parser emits one anger effect where the card prints two), but a distinct required change to the output.
verdicts.fixHint: Emit one changeAnger per anger clause instead of collapsing to a single effect; map 'raise your anger' to target user and 'lower opponent's anger' to target foe.

verdicts.reason: Text reads 'Lower opponent's anger 1 level' but the foe effect carries delta -2, which is the magnitude from the preceding 'Raise your anger 2 levels' sentence. Confirms the same first-numeral misbinding seen on Blue Energy Outburst. No CRD errata for this card.
verdicts.fixHint: Same as Blue Energy Outburst: scope numeral extraction to the individual anger clause.

verdicts.reason: Printed text contains 'Raise your anger 2 levels' and the parse holds only a foe-targeted anger effect, so the user gains no anger. The {user,+2} effect is plainly missing from the effects array.
verdicts.fixHint: Emit a second changeAnger with target user, delta 2 alongside the corrected foe effect.

verdicts.reason: CRD.txt line 1585 errata matches the stored text verbatim: 'Stops a physical or energy attack.' The parse hardcodes attackType 'energy', which would refuse a physical stop the card explicitly allows. 'any' exists in the AttackKind | 'any' union in abilities.ts. Core defect confirmed. Caveat: the suggested second effect for 'stops all attacks of the same type this card stopped' is a dynamic back-reference the Effect vocabulary cannot express precisely (thisCombat+any would be too broad) — treat that half as a modeling gap, not a blocker on the attackType fix.
verdicts.fixHint: Recognize the 'physical or energy' disjunction and emit attackType 'any'; the remainder-of-Combat same-type clause should be left as a manual/needsReview flag rather than forced into an overbroad thisCombat stop.

verdicts.reason: Printed text reads 'Stops an opponent's physical or energy attack.' The parse hardcodes attackType 'energy', silently dropping the physical half. Likely contaminated by the card's 'Energy Combat' type field, but the ability text plainly covers both. No CRD errata for this card.
verdicts.fixHint: Detect the 'physical or energy' disjunction in stop text and emit attackType 'any'; do not let the card's Combat type field override the parsed attack text.

verdicts.reason: CRD.txt line 1588 errata confirms the stored text: 'Stops an energy attack. Stop all energy attacks for the remainder of Combat.' The parse contains only the single-attack stop, dropping the second sentence — which is the card's defining effect (textOriginal is simply 'Stop all energy attacks in this combat'). window 'thisCombat' is defined in abilities.ts as 'all such attacks this combat'.
verdicts.fixHint: Parse 'for the remainder of Combat' / 'in this combat' as window 'thisCombat' with scope 'all'; note stopAttack thisCombat is currently emitted zero times across all 2764 cards, so the rule appears entirely absent.

verdicts.reason: Text reads 'stops all energy attacks for the rest of this combat' but the parse assigns window 'thisAttack', which expires after the current attack and loses the ongoing lock. 'thisCombat' with scope 'all' is exactly the modeled vocabulary. Separately, the stop is gated on 'If successful' which stopAttack cannot express — that is a genuine vocabulary gap and not part of this claim.
verdicts.fixHint: Map 'for the rest of this combat' to window 'thisCombat' and 'stops all' to scope 'all'; consider adding ifSuccessful to stopAttack to capture the gate.

verdicts.reason: Text reads 'stops opponents from making energy attacks for the rest of this combat' but the parse assigns window 'thisAttack', dropping the ongoing denial after one attack. Same missing rest-of-combat rule as Black Swift Elbow Strike.
verdicts.fixHint: Same fix as Black Swift Elbow Strike: 'for the rest of this combat' should yield window 'thisCombat', scope 'all'.

verdicts.reason: Text reads 'Power up your main personality to its highest stage' and the effects array carries only changeAnger and removeFromGameAfterUse — the clause is dropped. movePowerStage {to:'highest'} is defined in abilities.ts, and CRD lines 229/485/529 confirm 'highest power stage' is the game's own term for this. Not a vocabulary gap: the schema has the exact slot, the parser just never emits it (0 uses across 2764 cards).
verdicts.fixHint: Add a rule mapping 'power up (your main personality) to (its) highest stage' to movePowerStage {target:'user', to:'highest'}.

verdicts.reason: Text reads 'Power up 3 stages' and the parse contains only changeAnger and removeFromGameAfterUse, so the user silently loses the gain. changePowerStages {target,delta} is defined in abilities.ts but is emitted zero times across the entire dataset, confirming the rule is missing rather than misapplied.
verdicts.fixHint: Add a rule mapping 'power up N stages' to changePowerStages {target:'user', delta:N}, distinct from 'to its highest stage' which maps to movePowerStage.

verdicts.reason: Verified empirically across all 2764 cards: every card whose text begins 'Heroes only.' carries restriction {alignment:'Hero'} (Gohan's Stomp, Hero Enraged!, Piccolo's Stomp, Kami's Idea, and ~15 others), while every card beginning 'Villains only.' has no restriction at all (Alien Anger!, Android 18's Low Blow, Android 20's Enraged, Cell's Defense, Cell's Dark Attack, Just Thinking, and more). AbilityRestriction.alignment already supports 'Villain'. This is a systematic one-sided parser bug, not a single-card miss — worth prioritizing above the other findings.
verdicts.fixHint: The alignment-restriction rule matches only 'Heroes only'; extend the pattern to 'Villains only' mapping to {alignment:'Villain'}, then re-run across the corpus to backfill all affected Villain cards.

verdicts.reason: Text plainly reads "Raise Majin Buu to his highest power stage" and the card is "Majin Buu only", so the user's personality is the target. The vocabulary has an exact match — movePowerStage {target:'user', to:'highest'} — yet the parse contains only changeAnger user +1. This is the card's headline effect and it is silently absent, so the card resolves as a bare anger gain. Not a vocabulary gap.
verdicts.fixHint: Add a rule for "raise <personality/your MP> to his/its highest power stage" -> movePowerStage target:'user' to:'highest'. The parser appears to only scan for one effect per sentence group; it must continue past the first matched clause. (Note also the unclaimed "Shuffle 5 cards in your discard pile into your Life Deck" — rejuvenate is bottom-of-deck, not shuffle, so that one is a genuine vocabulary gap and should be left alone.)

verdicts.reason: Both anger clauses are printed as adjacent sentences: "Raise your anger 1 level. Lower your opponent's anger 1 level." The parse captured only changeAnger foe -1. changeAnger target:'user' exists in the vocabulary and is used elsewhere in this same dataset, so this is a dropped clause, not a modeling limit. Endurance 3 is correctly excluded (stored in the separate endurance field per CRD 1118).
verdicts.fixHint: Anger extraction is terminating after the first match. Make the anger matcher global rather than first-match, and keep 'raise your anger'->user distinct from 'lower your opponent's anger'->foe.

verdicts.reason: The text says "+1 life cards of damage for each card in your discard pile with 'Kamehameha' in the title" — a per-card MODIFIER, not a stated base. CRD 343 fixes the base of an energy attack that does not state its damage at 4 life cards. Per abilities.ts, setting lifeCards OVERRIDES that default, so lifeCards:1 makes the engine deal 1 where the card deals 4 plus the rider. That is a plain contradiction of printed text, and the error is at least 3 life cards even with an empty discard pile.
verdicts.fixHint: Never source a lifeCards base from a clause beginning with '+'. Require bare 'doing N life cards of damage' for a fixed base; treat '+N' as a modifier. Since no life-card modifier effect kind exists, emit energyAttack with no lifeCards and push the rider to needsReview.

verdicts.reason: The printed effect is optional and costed: "you may remove 7 Saiyan Style cards in your discard pile from the game to raise your anger b levels", gated on not having used a Constant Combat Power this turn. CRD line 1678 errata for Goku, Super Saiyan Lv.2 confirms the OCR 'b' is 6. The parse encodes an unconditional, free changeAnger user +1 under trigger 'defense', so the engine grants an anger level on every defense — wrong on optionality, wrong on cost, wrong on frequency, and wrong on magnitude (1 vs 6). Nothing on the card licenses a +1.
verdicts.fixHint: Treat 'you may ... to <effect>' as a costed optional and refuse to emit the effect unconditionally. Also gate anger extraction on a legible digit — 'b' should have forced needsReview rather than defaulting to 1. preventLifeCards amount:2 attackType:'any' is correct and should be kept.

verdicts.reason: Same dropped-clause bug as Energy Ricochet: "Raise your anger 1 level. Lower your opponent's anger 1 level." produced only changeAnger foe -1. energyAttack lifeCards:5 is correct (the card states a fixed amount, which CRD 455 says governs). The claim's expected list contains a visible self-correction on the life-card count but lands on 5, matching the parse, so only the missing user anger is at issue — and it is genuinely missing.
verdicts.fixHint: Same fix as tts-bf3b8d7f-62: make the anger matcher global instead of first-match. Leave energyAttack lifeCards:5 alone.

verdicts.reason: The unconditional clause is "Physical attack doing +3 power stages of damage" — PAT base plus a damageStages 3 modifier, both of which the vocabulary covers. The parse instead scavenged the +7 from the Drill-gated sentence and installed it as physicalAttack.lifeCards:7, which per abilities.ts overrides the Physical Attack Table entirely. So the card resolves as a flat 7 life cards regardless of board state, while the only guaranteed effect (+3 stages) is absent. Two plain contradictions in one parse.
verdicts.fixHint: Do not read effect values out of clauses introduced by 'If ...'. Restrict base/modifier extraction to the unconditional sentence, emit physicalAttack (no lifeCards) + damageStages stages:3, keep removeFromGameAfterUse, and flag the Drill conditional and the 'If successful' shuffle as needsReview.

verdicts.reason: Identical bug class to Goku's Face Break and equally plain. Unconditional text: "Physical attack doing +4 power stages of damage." The parse emits physicalAttack lifeCards:4, a fixed base pulled from the level-2+ conditional rider, which overrides the PAT per abilities.ts. The card's actual guaranteed damage (PAT + 4 stages) never occurs. Endurance 3 is correctly held in the separate endurance field.
verdicts.fixHint: Same as tts-043989cc-1: ignore 'If your Main Personality is at level 2 or above ...' when sourcing base damage. Emit physicalAttack + damageStages stages:4 and flag the conditional rider and the 'If successful' Drill search.

verdicts.reason: Two distinct printed effects: "Stops a non-focused energy attack." and "Stops all non-focused energy attacks performed against you for the remainder of Combat." Only the first was captured. CRD 1930 (Nappa's Energy Aura) shows this exact two-sentence pattern is a single-stop plus a floating combat-long stop, not a restatement. The vocabulary has window:'thisCombat' and scope:'all' for precisely this, so the omission is a dropped clause. The unmodeled 'non-focused' qualifier is a separate known gap and does not excuse dropping the whole effect — the parser already ignored that qualifier on the first stop.
verdicts.fixHint: Add a pattern for 'stops all <type> attacks ... for the remainder of Combat' -> stopAttack {window:'thisCombat', scope:'all'}, and let a card emit more than one stopAttack. Keep the Hero restriction and removeFromGameAfterUse.

verdicts.reason: changeAnger has no toZero flag (only changePowerStages does), so "lowers your opponent's anger to 0" is not expressible — but the parser wrote changeAnger foe delta:0 anyway, converting a set-to-zero into a literal delta of zero. That is a misreading of 'to 0' as a magnitude, not a vocabulary gap: the entry describes an effect the card does not have. It is also emitted unconditionally while the text gates the whole clause on "If used by a Fused Personality". Today it is an inert no-op; it is still false data and a landmine if delta 0 is ever given meaning. physicalAttack powerStages:6 is correct (stated fixed base per CRD 455).
verdicts.fixHint: Do not coerce 'to N' into delta:N — they are different operations. When a phrase has no representable effect kind, drop it and record needsReview rather than emitting a degenerate value. Also skip clauses under 'If used by a Fused Personality'. Keep physicalAttack powerStages:6 as the only effect.

verdicts.reason: This is a Physical Combat attack card — "Physical attack doing +3 life cards of damage" — parsed as trigger 'defense' with a lone stopAttack and no attack at all. 'Sensei Deck.' is a deck-placement note (Saiyan Assault in this same batch carries it while also being an attack), so it cannot be what marks a defense. The stop is independently wrong on three axes: it is gated on the opponent's MP being a Majin, it covers 'physical or energy' (attackType 'any', not 'energy'), and it applies to the NEXT attack this Combat, not the current one. Every substantive field contradicts the text.
verdicts.fixHint: Stop treating 'Sensei Deck.' as a defense signal. Trigger should come from the attack verb: emit trigger 'attack' with physicalAttack. The '+3 life cards' modifier on a physical attack has no effect kind — flag it, do not synthesize one. Drop the Majin-conditional next-attack stop to needsReview.

verdicts.reason: The provenance critique is fair but there is no defect to fix. The card states no damage amount, so CRD 343 sets the base at 4 life cards; the parse's energyAttack lifeCards:4 also yields 4. The claim itself concedes the numbers match. The asserted future harm does not hold either: if the Saiyan rider were later modeled as a +4 modifier, base 4 plus 4 still gives the correct 8 whether the 4 is explicit or defaulted. So the printed text does not contradict the parse now or under the natural future fix — this is a stylistic redundancy, not a wrong number, and filing it would spend engineering time for zero behavioral change.
verdicts.fixHint: Optional hygiene only, not a bug: suppress an explicit lifeCards when the value merely restates the CRD default and no bare 'doing N life cards' phrase appears, so a scavenged conditional value can never masquerade as a stated base. Worth folding into the tts-043989cc-1 / tts-a15907e0-63 fix rather than tracking separately.

verdicts.reason: The card stops nothing. "cards that stop attacks" appears only inside a cost-increase clause that EXEMPTS stoppers from a +2 power stage tax, and that clause is itself double-gated on Tokui-Waza declarations. The parser matched on that phrase and produced trigger 'defense' + stopAttack any thisAttack — a fabricated defensive ability on a Physical Combat card. Meanwhile both real effects (physical attack, +2 power stages) are absent. This inverts the card's function entirely and, unlike a no-op, would actively let a player cancel an attack they have no right to cancel.
verdicts.fixHint: Require a stop-matching phrase to be the governing verb of its clause ('Stops a/an/all ...') rather than a noun phrase appearing anywhere in the text, and exclude text following 'except for'. Emit trigger 'attack' with [{kind:'physicalAttack'},{kind:'damageStages',stages:2}] and no stopAttack; the OCR typo 'Physicaly' should not block the attack matcher. 'Empower 3' and the Tokui-Waza cost clause go to needsReview.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed against clean Lackey text (#123): 'Physical attack doing +7 power stages of damage. If performed against a Rogue Personality, this attack does an additional +4 life cards of damage.' The 4 life cards are (a) conditional on a Rogue target and (b) explicitly 'an additional' amount. abilities.ts documents that setting lifeCards OVERRIDES the base-damage default, so physicalAttack{lifeCards:4} makes the card always deal exactly 4 life cards and never consult the Physical Attack Table — the opposite of print on the common non-Rogue case. Not a vocabulary gap: the parser invented a fixed base that is nowhere on the card.
verdicts.fixHint: Emit {kind:'physicalAttack'} with no lifeCards so PAT base damage applies. The conditional '+4 life cards vs a Rogue' has no representation (no conditional/additive life-card effect exists) and should be left unmodeled or flagged via needsReview, not folded into the base.

verdicts.reason: The '+7 power stages of damage' is the card's headline effect, is unconditional, and is absent from the parse entirely — effects contains only physicalAttack. This is the textbook case for damageStages, which abilities.ts defines as '+/- modifier on PAT'. The claim correctly distinguishes '+N power stages' (modifier) from 'doing N power stages' (fixed base) and asks for the modifier. Lackey text confirms the +7 against the garbled OCR. Combined with the first defect, the parsed card deals 4 flat life cards instead of PAT+7 stages.
verdicts.fixHint: Add {kind:'damageStages', stages:7}. The parser appears to stop after matching the attack noun; it needs to also scan the same sentence for a leading-'+' stage modifier attached to the attack clause.

verdicts.reason: Both parsed effects contradict the print. (1) stopAttack{any}: the Location never stops anything — 'stops an attack' appears only inside the trigger condition describing what a Celestial Fighter's own stop card did. As parsed, a Location in play grants a free universal attack stop. (2) removeFromGameAfterUse is inverted: the card's whole point is letting that stop card go to the bottom of the Life Deck INSTEAD of being removed, yet the parse makes the Location remove itself. Parsing a Location under trigger 'defense' is itself a category error. This is not a missing-vocabulary complaint — it is two asserted effects that are wrong in substance and direction.
verdicts.fixHint: Trigger should be 'constant' with {kind:'manual'} (a replacement effect with no schema representation). Root cause: the parser matches the substring 'stops an attack' and 'removes itself from the game after use' without checking whether they sit inside a subordinate 'When ...' condition clause or refer to another card rather than this one.

verdicts.reason: A Non-Combat Drill parsed as trigger 'defense' with stopAttack{any, thisAttack}. 'Whenever you stop an attack' is unambiguously the trigger condition that fires the Drill's benefit, not a capability the Drill confers. As parsed the player can use a Drill as a universal stop for any attack — a fabricated capability, and a serious one since free universal stops are among the strongest effects in the game. The actual payload (moving the bottom discard card to the bottom of the Life Deck) maps cleanly onto the existing rejuvenate effect, so this is a parsing defect, not a vocabulary gap.
verdicts.fixHint: Trigger 'constant' with {kind:'rejuvenate', count:1, from:'bottom'} and no stopAttack. Same root cause as Grand Kai's Palace: a leading 'Whenever/When ...' clause must be treated as a condition, never mined for effects.

verdicts.reason: Identical defect to Black Conservation Drill and equally clear: a Non-Combat Drill given trigger 'defense' and stopAttack{any, thisAttack} because 'Whenever you stop an attack' was read as an effect rather than the firing condition. The parse fabricates a free universal stop and drops the entire real payload (shuffle bottom discard card into the Life Deck; +3 power stages if it is a Goku Named card). Both claims of this pair are the same underlying bug surfacing on two cards, which strengthens rather than weakens them.
verdicts.fixHint: Trigger 'constant', drop stopAttack. Payload is conditional and only partly modelable: the shuffle-into-Life-Deck is not strictly rejuvenate (which places at the bottom), so either approximate with rejuvenate and flag needsReview, or use {kind:'manual'}. The load-bearing fix is removing the stopAttack.

verdicts.reason: 'Use when you stop an energy attack' is a usage window — a precondition stating the stop has already been achieved by some other card — not an effect this card produces. The contrast is decisive within this same dataset: cards that actually stop print 'Stops a physical or energy attack' (Blue Shifting Maneuver, Blue Speediness), while this one prints 'Use when'. As parsed, every real energy-attack stop gets doubled into a second free stop. No errata exists for this card (grepped CRD; none found), so printed text governs.
verdicts.fixHint: Drop the stopAttack; keep drawCards and add the movePowerStage. The parser needs to treat a leading 'Use when ...' clause as a timing gate rather than an effect source — the same class of bug as the 'Whenever you stop an attack' Drills.

verdicts.reason: 'Raise your Main Personality to its highest power stage' is the card's primary payoff and is simply absent — the parse kept only drawCards. movePowerStage{target,to:'highest'} exists in the schema for precisely this wording, and 'your Main Personality' targets the user per the stated anger/target convention. Independently confirmed by Lackey #062. This is a dropped effect with exact vocabulary available, not a modeling gap.
verdicts.fixHint: Add {kind:'movePowerStage', target:'user', to:'highest'}. Worth checking whether the parser only recognizes 'raise ... to its highest power stage' in the 'all of your personalities' phrasing and misses the singular Main Personality form.

verdicts.reason: stopAttack{physical, thisAttack} is fabricated. The only stop in the text belongs to the opponent and appears inside a conditional describing when the opponent gets punished ('if your opponent stops a physical attack ... your opponent must skip his next Attacker Attacks phase'). The parse hands that stop to the card's user as a rider on their own attack, so performing this attack would also stop a physical attack — and CRD line 742 states a card that can attack and stop 'cannot do both when they are used', so even a legitimate dual-mode card could not behave this way. The rest of the parse (physicalAttack + damageStages 2 + removeFromGameAfterUse) is correct.
verdicts.fixHint: Remove the stopAttack effect. The parser is attributing an effect to the user without checking the grammatical subject — here 'your opponent' — of the clause containing 'stops'.

verdicts.reason: Two independent errors, both plain. (1) The stop is an alternative mode gated on a cost ('You can use this card to stop ... INSTEAD by removing 3 Rares in your discard pile from the game'), yet it sits as an unconditional rider inside the trigger:'attack' ability, so performing the attack also stops one for free with no cost paid. CRD line 742 is explicit: 'Some cards can perform AND stop attacks. Such cards can only be played as either an attack or to stop an attack. They cannot do both when they are used.' The parse directly violates that rule. (2) attackType is 'energy' though the text reads 'a physical or energy attack'. Confirmed against Lackey (Preview 5).
verdicts.fixHint: Attack ability = physicalAttack + damageStages 4 + removeFromGameAfterUse only.
