verdicts.reason: Text reads "+2 life cards of damage" but the parse emits physicalAttack.lifeCards=2. abilities.ts line 26 states explicitly that a set lifeCards/powerStages "OVERRIDES the default", and CRD line 343 makes PAT the base for physical attacks unless the card states a fixed amount. The '+' is silently dropped, so a PAT-damage attack with a strong life-card rider collapses into a flat 2 life cards and loses all power-stage damage. This is systematic: 51 cards across the batches turn a '+N life cards' modifier into a fixed override.
verdicts.fixHint: Make the attack-damage regex anchor on a leading '+' and treat '+N life cards' as a modifier, not a base. Since no Effect kind expresses additive life cards (damageStages is power-stages only), emit physicalAttack with no lifeCards and add a needsReview entry such as 'lifeCardModifier' rather than writing the number into the override field.

verdicts.reason: CRD errata line 1945 confirms the sentence is a restriction on the opponent's ability to stop this attack, not a stop the card grants. The card stops nothing, yet the parse adds stopAttack{attackType:'any',window:'thisAttack'} to an ability whose trigger is 'attack'. The engine would hand the attacker a free cancel of one of the opponent's attacks that the printed card never provides.
verdicts.fixHint: Do not fire the stopAttack matcher on sentences whose subject is the opponent and whose verb is negated ('your opponent may not use ... to stop this attack'). Require the stop clause to be an effect the card's own controller gets. Leave the anti-stop restriction unmodeled with a needsReview note.

verdicts.reason: The card prints a cost of 1 power stage ('Gosts' is a C-for-G OCR/source typo for 'Costs'; the upstream Lackey record carries the identical typo). The parse has no cost field, so per CRD lines 397 and 452 the engine applies the default 'Costs 2 power stages to perform' and charges double. The discount is the card's entire purpose. The parser clearly handles this construction in general: 74 of the 80 cards printing 'costs N power stage(s)' get a parsed.cost, and this is the only card in the corpus with the 'Gosts' spelling.
verdicts.fixHint: Add OCR-variant tolerance to the cost matcher (allow G/C confusion, e.g. /\b[GC][o0]sts?\b/i) so it emits cost:{powerStages:1} here. A cheap guard: when an energy attack's text contains 'power stage(s) to perform' but no cost was parsed, flag needsReview:['cost'].

verdicts.reason: The claim's supporting evidence does not survive checking. ifSuccessful:true on damageStages is the parser's consistent marker that the card carries an 'If successful' clause: of 79 cards with '+N power stages of damage' AND 'if successful' in the text, 73 get the flag; of 211 with the same damage wording and no such clause, 184 get no flag. The two siblings the claim cites as identically-worded counterexamples (Namekian Bash tts-f71532b6-43, Saiyan Power Kick tts-f71532b6-52) contain no 'If successful' text at all, so they are not comparable; Blue Fist Smash tts-40b278df-34, which does contain it, is flagged exactly like Blue Straight Jab. The flag is also behaviorally inert on damage: per CRD battle-sequence steps 12-13 a stopped attack deals no damage whatsoever, so gating a damage modifier on success changes nothing. The only genuine gap is that changeAnger cannot carry a success gate, which the claim itself concedes the Effect type cannot express - a known vocabulary gap, not a parsing defect.

The text plainly reads "Stops a physical or energy attack" and the parse restricts stopAttack to attackType:'energy'. A physical attack would pass straight through a card whose printed text stops it. Systematic and high-impact: of 40 cards with 'physical or energy attack' in the text, 38 are parsed as 'energy' only and 39 are narrower than 'any' (e.g. Android 19 is Stoic tts-49d99703-68, Mother's Touch and Namekian Pikkon's Defense, both of which the CRD errata at lines 1888 and 1906 restate as stopping either type).
verdicts.fixHint: Match the disjunction 'physical or energy' before the single-type alternatives - the current pattern appears to scan for 'energy attack' and win on the trailing noun. Map the disjunctive form to attackType:'any'.

verdicts.reason: CRD errata line 2212 restates this card as "Energy attack. If successful, every Ally your opponent has in play loses 4 power stages" - the 4 power stages are a rider against the opponent's Allies, not the attack's own damage. Setting energyAttack.powerStages=4 overrides the default base, and CRD lines 343 and 449 fix that default at 4 life cards for an energy attack that states no amount. The engine therefore deals 4 power stages to the defending personality and zero life cards, which is neither half of the printed card.
verdicts.fixHint: Scope the damage-amount extractor to the attack sentence itself. Do not let a number from a following 'If successful, deal N ... to every Ally' clause populate the attack's own lifeCards/powerStages. Emit energyAttack with no override plus needsReview:['allyRider'].

verdicts.reason: Same defect as Namekian Side Kick and provable by direct collision: this card ('+3 life cards of damage') and Saiyan High Jump Kick tts-f71532b6-58 ('doing 3 life cards of damage') produce byte-identical parses of physicalAttack{lifeCards:3}, despite the first being a PAT attack with a +3 rider and the second being a fixed 3-card base. Per abilities.ts line 26 the emitted form is the fixed-base reading, so the engine drops all power-stage damage from the rider card.
verdicts.fixHint: Same fix as tts-3ae57df1-24: distinguish '+N' from bare 'N' in the life-card damage matcher so the two card behaviors stop collapsing into one encoding.

verdicts.reason: The discard is an optional upgrade ('you may discard a card ... to do +8 power stages of damage instead'), but the parse emits discardCards{target:'user',count:1} unconditionally while leaving damageStages at 4. The engine makes the player pay the cost every time and never grants the +8 it buys - pure downside that appears nowhere on the card. Note the card also has no cost per CRD line 397 (the word 'cost' never appears), so this is not a cost field being misplaced.
verdicts.fixHint: Suppress effect emission for clauses governed by optional modal wording ('you may', 'if you do', 'instead'). Emit physicalAttack + damageStages 4 only, with needsReview:['optionalUpgrade'].

verdicts.reason: The +2 life cards and +2 power stages are gated behind two simultaneous conditions (a declared Tokui-Waza AND the performing personality at 0 power stages), yet the parse emits damageStages:2 with no gate, so every use of the attack gets the bonus. As with Saiyan Power Kick, the fault is not that the Effect type lacks a condition field - omitting the bonus would be correct by default - but that the parser actively emitted an unconditional bonus the card only sometimes grants. The Endurance 3 is correctly kept out of effects as a card-level field.
verdicts.fixHint: When a damage-modifier clause is inside an 'If <condition>' sentence, do not emit it as an unconditional damageStages. Emit energyAttack alone and record needsReview:['conditionalDamage'].

verdicts.reason: The card performs two anger changes and the parse keeps only one: stopAttack + changeAnger{foe,-1} is emitted, and 'Raise your anger 1 level' is dropped, so the user's anger never rises. Both effects are fully expressible with the existing changeAnger kind, and the parser demonstrably handles the exact 'Raise your anger 1 level' phrase - it emits changeAnger{user,+1} from that same sentence on Red Offensive Stance tts-f71532b6-45. This is a dropped effect, not a vocabulary gap.
verdicts.fixHint: The anger matcher appears to stop after the first hit per card. Scan all sentences and emit one changeAnger per anger clause, keying target off 'your anger' (user) versus "your opponent's anger" (foe).

verdicts.reason: 'Gain 5 power stages' is dropped entirely even though changePowerStages{target,delta} exists in the schema (abilities.ts line 31). The engine stops the attack and raises the user's anger but the defender never gains the 5 stages. Directly expressible with existing vocabulary, so this is a missing effect rather than a known gap.
verdicts.fixHint: Add a matcher for 'Gain N power stage(s)' -> changePowerStages{target:'user',delta:+N} (and the mirrored 'loses N power stages' -> foe/negative, which other cards in the corpus also need).

verdicts.reason: The card states a fixed 5-card base, which per CRD lines 343 and 455 overrides the 4-life-card energy default, but the parse omits lifeCards so the engine deals 4. The secondary consequence is real too: CRD line 358 and line 685 make 5 or more life cards of damage the Dragon Ball capture threshold, so the parse silently deletes a capture trigger. 'N cards of damage' means life cards here - the alternative reading is excluded because power-stage damage is always spelled 'power stages'. The parser did flag needsReview:['energyLifeCards'], which is honest, but the emitted parse is still the wrong number rather than a deferral.
verdicts.fixHint: Accept 'N cards of damage' as a life-card amount, not just 'N life cards of damage', so this emits energyAttack{lifeCards:5}. This is the only card in the corpus using the bare 'cards of damage' phrasing, so the fix is narrow and low-risk.

verdicts.reason: Text is '+1 power stages of damage for each C card in your discard pile, to a maximum of +10'. The parser's modifier regex grabbed the per-unit rate and emitted a flat damageStages:1, which setupAttackAbility adds straight into attack.modifiers on every use. The printed bonus is 0 with an empty discard pile and up to +10 late-game, so the flat +1 is correct only in the coincidental one-C-card state. This is a wrong number the engine executes, not merely an unmodeled mechanic.
verdicts.fixHint: Do not emit a flat damageStages from a 'for each X' clause. Detect the 'for each'/'to a maximum of' scaling phrase in the modifier match and suppress the numeric effect, pushing needsReview:'variableModifier' (or a manual effect) instead.

verdicts.reason: The printed stop is payable only 'by discarding a copy of that card from your hand'; the parse emits stopAttack any/thisAttack with no cost and no discard effect. The defense branch of parseAbility never calls parseCost or pushDiscardCards, so the requirement is dropped entirely and the engine exposes a free, universal attack stop. AbilityCost.discard is in the vocabulary, so this is not purely a vocabulary gap — though the 'copy of that card' matching requirement genuinely is.
verdicts.fixHint: Safest fix is to flag this card manual, since the copy-matching requirement is unmodelable and a bare cost.discard=1 would still let it stop any attack for one arbitrary card. At minimum, have the defense branch run parseCost/discard detection so a stop with an attached payment cannot be emitted costless.

verdicts.reason: The 8 is gated: 'If Goku and Gohan are in play, this attack does 8 life cards of damage instead.' The word 'instead' makes the ungated base explicitly the energy default of 4 life cards (CRD line 343: 'If an energy attack does not state the amount of damage it does, the Base Damage is 4 life cards'). The parse sets energyAttack.lifeCards=8 with no condition, and setupAttackAbility assigns energyLifeCards=8 unconditionally, so the engine doubles the card's damage in the normal case. needsReview lists only 'type', so nothing flags the condition.
verdicts.fixHint: parseAttackDamage should not read a damage number out of a clause opening with 'if ...'. Scope the damage match to the sentence declaring the attack, and when a conditional damage sentence is detected emit the attack with no override plus needsReview:'conditionalDamage'.

verdicts.reason: Same conditional-as-unconditional defect: 'If you declared a Tokui-Waza, this attack does 7 life cards of damage.' Declaring a Tokui-Waza is optional (CRD lines 45/72/189 — 'If any player is declaring a Tokui-Waza'), so a no-Tokui-Waza deck should deal the 4-life-card default. The parse emits energyAttack.lifeCards=7 unconditionally and the engine applies it every time. Endurance 1 is correctly stripped to rules.endurance and is not the problem here.
verdicts.fixHint: Same fix as Orange Uniting Strike: refuse damage numbers drawn from an 'If you declared a Tokui-Waza ...' clause; emit the default-damage energy attack and record needsReview:'conditionalDamage'.

verdicts.reason: '+5 power stages of damage' is correctly typed as a modifier rather than a base, but it is gated on 'If you declared a Tokui-Waza' and the parse emits damageStages:5 with no condition and no ifSuccessful. setupAttackAbility adds it to attack.modifiers on every use, so a no-Tokui-Waza deck gets +5 stages on its Physical Attack Table result it is not entitled to.
verdicts.fixHint: Apply the conditional guard to the '+N stages' modifier regex too, not just to base damage: if the matched clause sits inside an 'if ...' sentence, drop the effect and flag needsReview:'conditionalModifier'.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed at the regex level. parseAttackDamage's second life-card pattern matched '2 life cards of damage' out of the 'If successful' rider (which boosts this personality's FUTURE energy attacks), yielding physicalAttack.lifeCards=2 — and because dmg.lifeCards is then defined, the '+N stages' block at line 364 is skipped, so the attack's real '+2 power stages' modifier is dropped. Engine-side, damageLifeCards=2 replaces Physical Attack Table damage entirely, so a PAT attack becomes a flat 2 life cards. Both halves of the claim hold; this is not a complaint about the unmodeled Focused keyword.
verdicts.fixHint: Restrict parseAttackDamage to the attack-declaring sentence rather than the whole body, so rider text after 'If successful' cannot supply base damage. That alone restores the '+2 power stages' damageStages effect.

verdicts.reason: Card reads 'Stops a physical or energy attack.' The parse restricts stopAttack.attackType to 'energy'. Cause is the lazy quantifier in /stop\w*\s+.{0,40}?(physical|energy)?\s*attack/, which walks past 'physical or' and captures only the token adjacent to 'attack'. The engine will refuse this card against physical attacks, losing half its function. Lackey text confirms the wording exactly.
verdicts.fixHint: Add an alternation for the dual form: if /(physical|energy)\s+(or|and)\s+(physical|energy)\s+attack/ matches, set attackType 'any' before the single-type match runs.

verdicts.reason: The scan is garbled ('unNstopped', 'LOU', a stray backslash) but the word 'energy' is clean in both the rules text and the card name. The backslash between 'energy' and 'attack' defeats the (physical|energy)?\s*attack group, so the optional group falls through empty and at() returns 'any' — the drill will stop physical attacks it should not. Under CRD 1160-1164 the mislabel also wrongly makes it a both-types stop, which cannot stop a Focused attack at all, so the error cuts in two directions.
verdicts.fixHint: Widen the separator class between the type word and 'attack' to tolerate OCR debris (e.g. [\s|\\/]*), matching the tolerance already present in the damageStages regex. Note this card has no textVerified flag, so re-verify the scan before relying on it; the window ('thisAttack' for a 'first unstopped ... during Combat' shield) looks wrong too but was not claimed.

verdicts.reason: The '+1' comes from a remainder-of-Combat clause that scales per Dragon Ball: 'all physical attacks do +1 power stages of damage for each Dragon Ball in play.' The parse attaches a flat damageStages:1 to this one attack and the engine adds it to attack.modifiers immediately. With no Dragon Ball in play — the ordinary case — the printed bonus is +0, so the parse invents damage, and it also mis-scopes a combat-wide effect onto a single attack. Same per-unit-rate bug as Megaton Bull Crusher. The attack itself and changeAnger user +1 are correctly parsed.
verdicts.fixHint: Same 'for each X' guard as Megaton Bull Crusher, plus a scope guard: a modifier inside a 'for the remainder of Combat, all physical attacks ...' clause is a floating effect, not a rider on the declared attack, and should not become a damageStages on this ability.

verdicts.reason: 'If successful, gain 2 anger' produces no effect: pushAnger's user branch requires 'raise', or the literal word 'level' after 'gain ... anger', or 'anger level N' — the bare 'gain 2 anger' phrasing matches none, so the parse holds only the energy attack. changeAnger is in the vocabulary and the engine applies it in setupAttackAbility, so the effect is expressible and simply lost. Caveat on the claim's expected value: the printed damage is 3 life cards (confirmed in the Lackey text), not 5 — lifeCards:3 in the current parse is correct and must not be 'fixed' to 5.
verdicts.fixHint: Add a 'gain N anger' alternative to pushAnger's user branch that does not require the word 'level' (e.g. /gain\w*\s+(\d)\s*anger/). Keep energyAttack.lifeCards at 3 and add changeAnger target 'user' delta +2; note the vocabulary has no ifSuccessful flag on changeAnger, matching how the corpus already emits ungated anger effects.

verdicts.reason: [wrong-number] Card reads 'lower your opponent's anger 2 levels' but the parse has changeAnger foe -1. Confirmed cause: pushAnger's foe branch uses /anger[^0-9]{0,10}(\d)/, which finds the FIRST 'anger' in the string — the preceding 'raise your anger 1 level' — and takes that 1. The engine applies the wrong magnitude directly via changeMpAnger.
verdicts.fixHint: Search for the number relative to the foe clause rather than the first 'anger' in the text: match the foe phrase and its digit together (e.g. /low\w*[^.]*(?:foe|opponent)'?s?\s+anger[^0-9]{0,10}(\d)/) instead of re-scanning from the start.

verdicts.reason: [missing-effect] 'raise your anger 1 level' is dropped; only the foe effect is emitted. Confirmed cause: pushAnger's user branch is wrapped in `if (!/low\w*[^.]*(foe|opponent)[^.]*anger/.test(t))`, so any card that also lowers foe anger suppresses the user raise entirely. Both changes are printed on the card and both are expressible as changeAnger effects.
verdicts.fixHint: Drop the mutual-exclusion guard and instead evaluate the two clauses independently (split on 'and'/sentence boundaries), so a card carrying both a self-raise and a foe-lower emits both changeAnger effects. This guard likely suppresses the same effect on every other both-anger card in the corpus — worth a corpus-wide re-run after the fix.

verdicts.reason: [wrong-number] Vision-verified text (high confidence) is 'Raise your anger 1 level. Lower your opponent's anger 3 levels.' The foe clause plainly says 3, parsed as -1. Confirmed in engine/src/abilities.ts pushAnger: the foe branch pulls its number with t.match(/anger[^0-9]{0,10}(\d)/) against the WHOLE text, so it hits 'anger 1 level' from the earlier user sentence and never sees the 3. Exactly the mechanism the claim alleges.
verdicts.fixHint: In pushAnger (packages/engine/src/abilities.ts ~line 259), scope the number match to the foe clause itself rather than the whole card text — match on the matched foe sentence (split on '.') e.g. /low\w*[^.]*(foe|opponent)[^.]*anger[^0-9]{0,10}(\d)/ — so each anger sentence supplies its own delta.

verdicts.reason: [missing-effect] The card has two anger sentences; only one changeAnger was emitted. 'Raise your anger 1 level' targets the user per the errata-era wording rule, and changeAnger/target:'user' exists in the schema. Confirmed in pushAnger: the user branch matches, but is then suppressed by the guard `if (!/low\w*[^.]*(foe|opponent)[^.]*anger/.test(t))` — the presence of the opponent sentence anywhere in the text kills the user effect. Distinct defect from the wrong-number one, though both live in the same function and would likely be fixed together.
verdicts.fixHint: Drop the whole-text mutual-exclusion guard in pushAnger and evaluate anger per sentence: split the text on sentence boundaries, run the user and foe matchers on each, and emit one changeAnger per clause. Result here: {user,+1} and {foe,-3}.

verdicts.reason: [wrong-effect] Text confirmed by Lackey (#020): 'Physical attack doing +2 life cards of damage.' CRD line 433 ('added on top of the Base Damage... even if the attack doesn't deal the kind of damage that is being modified') and line 2505 ('base damage is PAT for physical... unless the card states a set amount') make this a modifier on PAT, not a set amount. abilities.ts states lifeCards OVERRIDES the default, and engine/src/abilities.ts line 67 confirms it (attack.damageLifeCards = e.lifeCards), so the parse deals a flat 2 life cards and drops all PAT stage damage. Mechanism confirmed: parseAttackDamage's first alternative correctly refuses 'doing +2', but the second alternative /([0-9b]+)\s*life\s*cards?\s*(?:of damage)/ matches '2 life cards of damage' with no sign awareness. This is not a vocabulary gap complaint — the parser silently produced wrong numbers where it should have declined.
verdicts.fixHint: In parseAttackDamage (packages/engine/src/abilities.ts ~line 200-206), make the sign-less life-card alternatives reject a preceding +/- (e.g. negative lookbehind on /[+-]\s*/ before the digits), matching how the power-stage branch already excludes signed amounts. Since the schema has no life-card modifier kind, signed life-card damage should fall through to a bare physicalAttack with needsReview rather than a fixed base.

verdicts.reason: [wrong-effect] Text confirmed by Lackey (C4): 'Stops all physical or all energy attacks for the remainder of Combat.' Parse is window:'thisAttack' (per schema comment, 'the current one') with no scope, so the lockout ends after one attack — a plain contradiction of 'for the remainder of Combat', which the schema expresses as window:'thisCombat', scope:'all'. attackType:'energy' is also an artifact: the lazy regex /stop\w*\s+.{0,40}?(physical|energy)?\s*attack/ skips past 'physical' because only 'energy' is directly followed by 'attack'. Note the claim's own suggestion of 'any' over-models slightly (the user picks ONE type), but the window/scope defect is undeniable.
verdicts.fixHint: In parseDefensiveEffects (~line 233-237) add a duration check alongside the existing next-phase check: /remainder of (the )?combat|for the rest of combat|this combat/ => window:'thisCombat', scope:'all'. Also handle the 'physical or energy' disjunction so attackType isn't decided by which word happens to sit next to 'attack'; here the user's choice should be flagged for review.

verdicts.reason: [wrong-effect] Text confirmed by Lackey (#048). window:'thisAttack' is the attack this rider is attached to, which is the user's own attack — it cannot stop it. The card stops the opponent's next attack, which the schema encodes as window:'nextPhase'. Confirmed mechanism: parseDefensiveEffects only checks /next\s*(phase|round)/, and this card says 'the next attack', so it falls through to 'thisAttack'; the rider path at line 376 uses `window: s.window ?? 'nextPhase'`, which cannot repair an already-set wrong window. The lost 'If successful' gate is a genuine schema gap (ifSuccessful exists only on damageStages), so that half is not independently actionable, but the window is plainly wrong.
verdicts.fixHint: Broaden the window detection to /next\s*(attack|phase|round)/ in parseDefensiveEffects (~line 235), or have the attack-rider path at line 376 force window:'nextPhase' for stops that are riders on the user's own attack. Separately consider adding ifSuccessful to stopAttack (or flag needsReview) so the success gate isn't silently dropped.

verdicts.reason: [wrong-effect] Vision-verified text (high confidence, 'Printed text matches altText exactly'): 'Stops a physical or energy attack.' The card explicitly covers both types; attackType:'energy' is wrong and the engine would refuse it against a physical attack. Same lazy-regex artifact as Cell's Defense: only 'energy' is adjacent to 'attack', so 'physical' is skipped. attackType:'any' is in the schema, so this is a parser defect, not missing vocabulary.
verdicts.fixHint: In parseDefensiveEffects (~line 233), match the disjunction before the single-type pattern: /(physical|energy)\s+or\s+(?:an?\s+)?(physical|energy)\s+attack/ => attackType:'any'.

verdicts.reason: [missing-effect] The parse is a bare physicalAttack and drops the card's entire second half, which changeAnger can express — a real defect. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the claim: the target is NOT the user. The stored text is unverified OCR (no textVerified flag, no lackey link, 'If successful.' as a stray fragment); the printed card is 'Android 17's Neckhold' (AndroidsSaga #001) and reads 'Physical attack. If successful, lower your OPPONENT'S anger 3 levels.' The claim's expected {target:'user',delta:-3} would ship a new bug — it should be {target:'foe',delta:-3}. Confirmed why nothing parsed: pushAnger's foe branch needs the word foe/opponent (OCR lost it) and its user branch only fires on raise/gain wording.
verdicts.fixHint: First re-verify the text for tts-514f40cb-0 against the image/Lackey (#001) — the stored OCR dropped "opponent's". Then the correct effect is {kind:'changeAnger',target:'foe',delta:-3}, gated on success; since changeAnger has no ifSuccessful flag, add needsReview or extend the flag beyond damageStages. Also teach pushAnger the 'lower ... anger N levels' form (it currently only reads 'anger level N').

verdicts.reason: [missing-effect] Text confirmed by Lackey (#011): 'doing 1 life card of damage and 1 power stage of damage.' Both are unsigned set amounts, and physicalAttack carries lifeCards and powerStages simultaneously, so both belong in the parse. Confirmed mechanism: parseAttackDamage returns early at line 206 on the life-card match and never evaluates the power-stage branch, so a card stating both can only ever keep the first. The lost 1 power stage of damage is real engine-visible damage.
verdicts.fixHint: Make parseAttackDamage (packages/engine/src/abilities.ts ~line 200-210) accumulate instead of returning on first hit: run both the life-card and power-stage matchers and return {lifeCards, powerStages} with whichever matched.

verdicts.reason: [missing-effect] Text confirmed by Lackey (#091). 'Raise you Main Pwersonality to its highest power stage' is exactly {kind:'movePowerStage',target:'user',to:'highest'}, which the schema has, and the parse omits it entirely while keeping the rejuvenate. Confirmed mechanism: pushMoveStage (~line 318) requires the literal 'your personality|your mp|all of your personalities' AND /highest\s*stage/ — it fails twice here, on the OCR typos ('you Main Pwersonality') and on the word 'power' sitting between 'highest' and 'stage'. The second half is a general gap, not OCR-specific.
verdicts.fixHint: In pushMoveStage, allow /highest\s*(power\s*)?stage/ and loosen the subject to /(your|his|her)?\s*(main\s*)?p\w*rsonalit(y|ies)|your mp/ so it tolerates the OCR typo; note the same 'highest power stage' wording appears on other cards (e.g. 'A Burst of Energy'), so this likely under-parses across the set.

verdicts.reason: [wrong-trigger] Text confirmed by Lackey (#053): 'When entering Combat, draw a card.' The schema has a dedicated 'whenEnteringCombat' trigger and the parse uses 'onPlay', so a recurring per-Combat draw becomes a one-shot at play. Confirmed mechanism: the Non-Combat branch (~line 419) hardcodes trigger:'onPlay' with no entering-combat detection anywhere in the parser.
verdicts.fixHint: In the Non-Combat branch of parseAbility (~line 405-421), detect /when(ever)?\s+(you\s+)?enter(ing)?\s+combat/ and set trigger:'whenEnteringCombat'. The second sentence ('choose a card from your hand and place it on top of your Life Deck') is still unmodeled and should keep the card out of full coverage.

verdicts.reason: [wrong-target] Text confirmed by Lackey (#100): 'Your opponent lowers his anger to 0.' The card is placed on the opponent's MP and zeroes the opponent's anger; target:'user' hits the wrong player. Confirmed mechanism: the card's OCR typo "opponen'ts" defeats pushAnger's foe-possessive stripper, leaving a bare 'your' that trips the user branch, while the foe branch's word-order patterns don't match 'opponent lowers his anger'. The claim is also right that delta:0 is a no-op — changeAnger has no toZero (only changePowerStages does), so even with the target fixed this resolves to nothing.
verdicts.fixHint: Add the 'opponent ... lowers/loses ... anger' word order to pushAnger's foe branch and make the possessive stripper tolerate the apostrophe typo. Since changeAnger cannot express set-to-zero, either add a toZero flag mirroring changePowerStages or leave this card as manual/needsReview rather than emitting a silent no-op. The 'may not raise anger until an Ally is placed' clause is unmodeled either way.

verdicts.reason: [wrong-effect] Text confirmed by Lackey (#056). The unconditional base is '+1 power stage of damage' — a PAT modifier, which the schema expresses as damageStages — and it is gone; in its place the parse hardcodes lifeCards:6, which per abilities.ts is a fixed base that overrides PAT, even though those 6 life cards are both conditional (Tokui-Waza declared) and optional ('you may'). A deck that never declares Tokui-Waza resolves completely wrong. Confirmed mechanism: parseAttackDamage's first alternative matched 'do 6 life cards' from the conditional sentence, which also suppressed the damageStages fallback at line 364 (it only runs when no fixed damage was found). The foe anger -1 in the parse is correct.
verdicts.fixHint: Restrict parseAttackDamage to the clause containing the attack declaration rather than scanning the full text, so conditional/optional alternatives ('if you declared ... you may do N instead') can't be lifted into the base. Correct encoding: {kind:'physicalAttack'} + {kind:'damageStages',stages:1} + the existing {changeAnger,foe,-1}, with the Tokui-Waza substitution added to needsReview.

verdicts.reason: Parse is [physicalAttack, damageStages 4, changeAnger foe -1]. Both anger effects are printed after "You may remove a 'Hidden Power Level' ... If you do", so neither is free. The engine executes changeAnger in setupAttackAbility (abilities.ts:78-80), so the foe loses a level of anger on every use with no cost paid. The sibling user +1 is dropped because pushAnger's guard at abilities.ts:256 suppresses the user branch whenever any foe-anger phrase appears in the text. Unpaid benefit plus half a clause; plainly contradicted either way.
verdicts.fixHint: Treat text after 'you may <cost> ... if you do' / 'you may <cost> to <benefit>' as gated: drop the whole clause or emit both changeAnger effects behind a cost. Separately, the abilities.ts:256 guard must not suppress a printed user-anger raise merely because a foe-anger phrase is also present.

verdicts.reason: Parse is trigger onPlay with only [discardCards user 1]. The card's entire payload (MP pays 2 power stages to perform a physical attack doing +3 stages) is absent, and the discard the parser kept is actually half the cost, so using the Drill discards a card for nothing. Not a vocabulary gap: physicalAttack, damageStages, and AbilityCost{powerStages,discard} all exist. The card fell into parseAbility's Non-Combat branch (abilities.ts:408-422), which only runs the rider emitters and never looks for an embedded attack.
verdicts.fixHint: In the Non-Combat branch, detect an embedded 'perform a physical/energy attack doing ...' clause and emit the attack effects plus cost {powerStages:2, discard:1} rather than surfacing the discard alone as an effect.

verdicts.reason: Parse is [energyAttack lifeCards 5, drawCards 1]. The draw is printed only as the payoff of 'You may remove a "Saiyan Energy Throw" ... to draw a card', so pushDraw (abilities.ts:271-274) matched inside an optional-cost clause and emitted it unconditionally. The +4 stages from the same clause is also dropped, because the modifier branch at abilities.ts:364 is gated off whenever a fixed lifeCards base was found. The parse takes the clause's benefit and neither its cost nor its other half.
verdicts.fixHint: Make rider emitters skip spans inside an optional 'you may remove ... to ...' clause; and lift the abilities.ts:364 gate so a '+N power stages' modifier can coexist with a stated lifeCards base.

verdicts.reason: Parse is [energyAttack lifeCards 5, changeAnger user +2]. The +2 anger is printed only as the payoff of 'you may remove 3 Commons in your discard pile from the game to ...', and changeAnger is one of the effects the engine actually executes (abilities.ts:78-80), so the user gains 2 anger levels free on every use. The sibling 'gain 3 power stages' is dropped even though changePowerStages exists; the attack branch has no emitter for a power-stage gain (pushSelfPowerLoss only matches losses, pushRaiseOwnPower only matches 'power rating by N' and is not called there).
verdicts.fixHint: Gate pushAnger on optional 'you may ... to ...' clauses, and add a 'gain N power stages' -> changePowerStages{target:'user'} emitter to the attack branch.

verdicts.reason: Parse is trigger onPlay with drawCards 1. The printed draw fires only 'When you use a card effect to discard any Allies in play', and the card's own errata line in the data ('You must discard an Ally in order to draw the card from this Drill') makes the gating explicit. onPlay per abilities.ts means 'Non-Combat: on play/use', so the parse grants a card the moment the Drill is played and never on the printed trigger. The card reached the Non-Combat branch (abilities.ts:408) which hardcodes trigger 'onPlay' for anything that yields an effect.
verdicts.fixHint: Recognize a leading 'When you <event>, ...' clause as a triggered condition: emit trigger 'constant' with the ally-discard trigger unmodeled (needsReview) instead of an unconditional onPlay drawCards.

verdicts.reason: Parse is physicalAttack{powerStages:5}, which abilities.ts documents as a FIXED base that overrides the default, and combat.ts:167 confirms it: PAT is consulted only when baseDamage is undefined, so damage is hard-capped at 5 stages regardless of the power-rating spread. The card's own attack is '+5 power stages of damage', a modifier. The 5 the parser captured is from the later requirement sentence ('must perform a focused physical attack doing 5 power stages of damage') -- parseAttackDamage's unsigned regex (abilities.ts:208) cannot match '+5' but does match that sentence.
verdicts.fixHint: Anchor the fixed power-stage regex to the opening attack sentence and reject a match whose number is preceded by '+' or '-', so a later next-turn requirement sentence cannot set the base; emit [{physicalAttack},{damageStages:5}].

verdicts.reason: The ability has no cost field. CRD line 397 and 452 are explicit that an energy attack not listing its cost gains 'Costs 2 power stages to perform', so the engine will charge 2 where the card prints 6 -- a 4-stage discount every use, on a card whose cost is its main balancing lever. Cause is the OCR typo 'poer': parseCost (abilities.ts:195) requires a literal 'power' (or 'stages of power to perform'), so 'Costs 6 poer stages to perform' matches neither alternative. AbilityCost.powerStages exists, so this is not a vocabulary gap.
verdicts.fixHint: Loosen parseCost to tolerate OCR damage in 'power' (e.g. cost\w*\s*([0-9b]+)\s*(?:p\w{1,4}r\s*)?stages?) so this yields cost {powerStages:6}.

verdicts.reason: Both halves check out. physicalAttack{lifeCards:1} was lifted from the conditional per-Android rider by parseAttackDamage's second lifeCards alternative (abilities.ts:203, matching '1 life card of damage'); per abilities.ts a lifeCards value overrides the default, and combat.ts:167/251 confirm PAT is then never consulted and the attack resolves as a flat 1 life card. The unconditional '+2 power stages of damage' is then dropped entirely because the modifier branch at abilities.ts:364 only runs when no fixed damage was found. Net: a PAT attack with a +2 bonus became a flat 1 life card.
verdicts.fixHint: Restrict parseAttackDamage to the opening attack sentence so conditional riders ('this attack does +1 life card ... for each ...') cannot set the base, and let the '+N stages' modifier parse independently of that lookup.

verdicts.reason: Same defect pattern as Ridge Hand and confirmed in code: parseAttackDamage's '([0-9b]+) life cards? of damage' alternative (abilities.ts:203) matched the Tokui-Waza per-Dragon-Ball rider, producing physicalAttack{lifeCards:2}, which combat.ts:251 resolves as a flat 2 life cards with PAT never consulted. The printed base modifier '+2 power stages of damage' is dropped by the abilities.ts:364 gate. The conditional rider is unmodelable, but hoisting its number into the base is a plain contradiction of the printed attack.
verdicts.fixHint: Same fix as tts-30fb99ff-8: scope fixed-damage extraction to the first attack sentence; emit [{physicalAttack},{damageStages:2}] and leave the conditional rider for needsReview.

verdicts.reason: CRD line 2519 defines a Defense Shield as activating 'when you do not stop an opponent's attack' and stopping 'the first unstopped attack', and battle-sequence step 7 (CRD line 337) fires shields only after an attack was not otherwise stopped -- that is exactly the enum's documented 'firstSuccessful' (the first that gets through), not 'thisAttack' (the current one, i.e. a hand-played stop). The parse also carries no trace of the persistent 'first 2 ... during Combat' scope. Cause is parseDefensiveEffects: the firstSuccessful branch (abilities.ts:223) requires the literal phrase 'first successful', so 'first 2 unstopped' falls through to the generic stop branch that defaults to 'thisAttack' (abilities.ts:235). Confidence is moderate: the count of 2 genuinely is a vocabulary gap (stopAttack has no count), and every Defense Shield in the corpus shares this window, so this is a parser-wide fix rather than a one-card slip -- but the window itself is expressible and currently wrong.
verdicts.fixHint: In parseDefensiveEffects, match 'Defense Shield:' and 'first N unstopped ... attack' to window 'firstSuccessful', and record the count (or flag it in needsReview) rather than falling through to the generic 'thisAttack' default.

verdicts.reason: The ability carries stopAttack{any, thisAttack} with no cost, but the card prints the hand discard as the price of the stop ('you may discard a card from your hand to stop a non-focused attack'). Since this is a Drill that sits permanently in play, an uncosted stop is an unlimited free stop of any attack. Confirmed cause: parseCost and pushDiscardCards are only invoked in the attack branch (abilities.ts:379, 373); the defense branch (abilities.ts:393-403) never parses a cost. AbilityCost.discard exists, so this is not a vocabulary gap. (The separate attackType 'any' vs printed 'non-focused' is the known unmodeled focused mechanic and is not part of this claim.)
verdicts.fixHint: Run parseCost and a 'discard N card(s) from your hand to <effect>' cost detector in the defense branch, emitting cost {discard:1} alongside the stopAttack.

verdicts.reason: The card prints two separate effects and the parse has one. 'If successful, gain 3 power stages' -- a changePowerStages{user,+3} the engine does execute (changeControllerStages, abilities.ts:81-83) -- is entirely absent, so the attacker never gains the stages. The remaining damageStages:3 came from the '+3 power stages of damage' modifier and was tagged ifSuccessful only because ifSucc() (abilities.ts:156) tests the whole text rather than the clause, so the 'if successful' from the second sentence bleeds onto the first. Worth noting for triage: the mis-tagging is currently damage-neutral, since combat.ts:259 sums modifiers and ifSuccessfulStages into the same post-stop total; the actionable defect is the missing power-stage gain.
verdicts.fixHint: Scope ifSucc() to the clause containing 'if successful' instead of the full text, and add a 'gain N power stages' -> changePowerStages{target:'user'} emitter so the reward is not silently absorbed into the damage modifier.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. pushAnger's magnitude regex /anger[^0-9]{0,10}(\d)/ captures the TARGET value from "anger to 0" and uses it as a relative delta, yielding {changeAnger, foe, delta:0}. setupAttackAbility -> changeMpAnger -> setAnger(mp.anger + 0) is a literal no-op, and the ability carries needsReview:[] so nothing signals the gap. This is not merely a missing-vocabulary complaint: the claim's own alternative fix (omit + flag) needs no schema change, and the same regex would mis-encode any "lower ... anger to N" as a relative -N. 12 cards dataset-wide carry a delta:0 changeAnger. One correction to the claim's supporting detail: on Goku's Conquering Stance (tts-514f40cb-18) the parser dropped the clause silently with needsReview:[] rather than flagging it, so that card is not the clean contrast the claim describes.
verdicts.fixHint: In parseAbility/pushAnger, detect set-semantics ("lower ... anger to N") before the delta match and either add a set/toZero field to changeAnger (mirroring changePowerStages.toZero) or emit no changeAnger and push needsReview:['angerSetTo']. Never emit delta:0.

verdicts.reason: Same confirmed root cause as Blue Foot Smash: "Lower your opponent's anger to 0" parses to {changeAnger, foe, delta:0}, which executes as anger + 0 and does nothing, with no needsReview. The claim's parenthetical is also correct - physicalAttack{powerStages:8} is right, since "doing 8 power stages of damage" is a fixed base that overrides the PAT.
verdicts.fixHint: Same pushAnger fix; the anger clause here is unconditional, so a set-to-zero encoding would fully model this card.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed, and systemic. pushMoveStage requires /rais\w*[^.]{0,60}(all of your personalities|your personality|your mp)[^.]{0,40}highest\s*stage/; this card prints "Raise all personalities in play to their highest power stage", which fails on both the subject and the "power stage" wording. The schema models this exactly (movePowerStage to:'highest'), so this is a regex miss, not a vocabulary gap. Dataset check: 112 cards mention "highest (power) stage" and 0 cards in cards.tts.enriched.json carry a movePowerStage effect - the effect kind is currently dead. The gap survived because parser.test.ts:35 tests the phrase "highest stage", which no real card prints. Android 19's Distress (tts-49d99703-21) drops the same clause as claimed.
verdicts.fixHint: Widen pushMoveStage: accept "highest power stage", and subjects beyond "all of your personalities" ("all personalities in play", "your Main Personality", OCR variants). Whether "in play" should emit both user and foe targets, as the claim proposes, is a separate design call - the load-bearing defect is that the clause is dropped entirely. Update the unit test to the real printed wording.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed, and in the dangerous direction. The printed clause buys the anger drop at a rate - the user may optionally sacrifice power stages, 1 anger level per 2 stages lost - but pushAnger's foe branch fires on the bare phrase and emits a flat {changeAnger, foe, delta:-1} with no changePowerStages cost. As parsed the engine hands the user a free anger level for playing a stop card, and it never scales past -1. The OCR text is garbled (this card has no textVerified flag), but the rate clause "For | every 2 power stages you lose in this lower your opponent's anger 1 level" is legible enough that the conditional structure is not in doubt.
verdicts.fixHint: Suppress the foe-anger effect when the sentence contains a rate/cost clause ("for every N power stages you lose", "you may choose to ... lose"); emit stopAttack only and push needsReview:['scaledAngerCost'].

verdicts.reason: Confirmed by the printed text alone, and independently by CRD.txt:1456 ("Physical attack. If you declared Tokui-Waza, this attack does 5 power stages of damage instead..."). parseAttackDamage's /(?:doing|does|deal\w*)\s+([0-9b]+)\s*(?:power\s*)?stages?\s*of\s*damage/ scans the whole body and picks up the 5 from the conditional "instead" clause, emitting physicalAttack{powerStages:5}, which per abilities.ts OVERRIDES the PAT base unconditionally. Tokui-Waza is an optional declaration made at setup (CRD.txt:71-91, 189; CRD.txt:1121 explicitly contemplates "no Tokui-Waza decks"), so 5 stages is not a given.
verdicts.fixHint: Scope base-damage extraction to the unconditional clause: skip text after "if you declared (tokui|toku)-waza" / any "... instead" clause when looking for a fixed base. Emit {kind:'physicalAttack'} with needsReview:['tokuiWazaAlternate'].

verdicts.reason: Confirmed and mechanically asymmetric. parseRestriction handles /heroes only/ -> {alignment:'Hero'} but has no Villain branch; its only villain pattern requires a named personality (/villains?[, ].{0,20}(goku|gohan)/). stripLead then removes the "Villains only." prefix from the body, so the constraint is silently discarded. Dataset check: 22 abilities carry alignment:'Hero', 0 carry alignment:'Villain', though AbilityRestriction.alignment accepts 'Villain'. Verified all 8 cited companion cards print a villains-only prefix and parse with restriction absent. One caveat on the claim's impact statement: nothing in the engine currently reads ability.restriction (it is written by the parser and never consumed), so the immediate harm is data completeness rather than an enforcement bypass - but the parse is still wrong where the schema and the mirrored Hero branch both say it should not be.
verdicts.fixHint: Add a Villain branch to parseRestriction before the namedOnly check, tolerant of the OCR spellings present in the data (Villains/Villians/Villans): /^\s*vill[ia]*n?s? only/ -> {alignment:'Villain'}. Keep the namedOnly pattern first so "Villains, Goku, and Gohan only" still wins.

verdicts.reason: The CRD errata is real (CRD.txt:1711 - "This card does not have 'Remove from the game after use.'"), but the parse is not a mis-parse: the card's printed text, captured identically by both TTS OCR and the independent Lackey source, ends with that line, and removesAfterUse rendered it faithfully. The divergence comes from a CRD ruling, and nothing anywhere in the pipeline applies CRD errata to card text - the only errata channel is the TTS mod author's per-card note (226 cards carry one; this card carries none) and the parser never reads it. Under the audit's bar (printed text plainly contradicts the parse) this fails, and the claim generalizes to every 'treat this card as if it read' entry in the CRD, i.e. a missing pipeline stage rather than a parser defect. Worth noting for the parent: this card's OTHER effect is genuinely wrong and was not claimed - the text says "Your opponent lowers his anger to 0" but the parse emits {changeAnger, target:'user', delta:0}, both the wrong side and a no-op.
verdicts.fixHint: Not a parser change. If desired, add a CRD errata override table keyed by set+number applied during enrichment, before parseAbility. Separately, fix the changeAnger target/set-to-zero on this card via the pushAnger fix.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed; two compounding errors, both traceable. parseAttackDamage's second life-card alternative /([0-9b]+)\s*life\s*cards?\s*(?:draws?|in damage|of damage)/ matches "3 life cards of damage" inside the conditional "you may discard the top card ... to do an additional +3 life cards" clause, so physicalAttack{lifeCards:3} is emitted. Per abilities.ts and setupAttackAbility (attack.damageLifeCards = 3), that REPLACES the PAT base. And because dmg.lifeCards is defined, the guard at parser line 364 skips the modifier branch entirely, so the card's actual printed "+4 power stages of damage" is dropped. The card resolves as a flat 3-life-card attack instead of a PAT attack at +4 stages.
verdicts.fixHint: Anchor base-damage extraction to the first (unconditional) sentence and reject signed values ("+3", "an additional +3") as bases - a signed amount is a modifier by definition. With lifeCards unset the existing modifier branch will then emit damageStages{stages:4}; flag the optional Tokui-Waza discard rider in needsReview.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. The printed text has no base override - it is a plain physical attack whose "+4 life cards" is ADDITIONAL damage double-gated on "If successful" and on declaring Tokui-Waza. The same unanchored /([0-9b]+)\s*life\s*cards?\s*of damage/ alternative matches "+4 life cards of damage" and emits physicalAttack{lifeCards:4}, which setupAttackAbility applies as attack.damageLifeCards, destroying the power-stage base. The parse also strips both gates (the changeAnger user +1 is emitted unconditionally with no ifSuccessful marker, though the schema only carries that flag on damageStages).
verdicts.fixHint: Same fix as Saiyan Face Stomp: a signed amount is never a base. Additionally, ifSucc(body) is already computed - use it to suppress or flag riders that sit inside an "if successful" clause rather than emitting them as immediate effects.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. The unconditional printed modifier is rendered "3+ power stages" (identically in the Lackey text, i.e. a transposed sign on "+3"), which the modifier regex /([+\-])\s?(\d+).../ cannot match because the sign trails the digit; the first thing it does match is the "+6" inside the conditional clause. So the card's own value is dropped and the replacement value is applied every time, doubling the stage bonus. The +6 requires BOTH a Tokui-Waza declaration (optional at setup, CRD.txt:189, 1121) and a paid Life Deck discard, neither of which the engine checks.
verdicts.fixHint: Two changes: tolerate the transposed sign (N+ before "power stages of damage") so the printed +3 is read, and scope modifier extraction to the clause before any "if you declared ... instead" sentence. Expected output damageStages{stages:3} plus needsReview for the alternate.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed, and in the strictly-stronger direction. The card is a defense that stops a physical attack only; the printed text (verified identically in the Lackey source) misspells it "phisical", so parseDefensiveEffects' optional (physical|energy) group fails to capture and at() falls back to 'any'. As parsed the card also stops energy attacks. The parser already carries OCR-tolerance elsewhere (toNum treats 'b' as 8, stripTypePlate, "doint"), so tolerating this spelling is in scope and not a vocabulary gap.
verdicts.fixHint: Make the attack-kind capture OCR-tolerant in parseDefensiveEffects (e.g. ph[iy]s\w*|energ\w*) and only fall back to 'any' when no near-match exists anywhere in the sentence. Do not infer the stopped type from the card's own type plate - a Physical Combat card can legitimately stop energy attacks.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. This is an attack card; the stop it grants is deferred ("the next physical attack performed against you this Combat"), so window:'thisAttack' is wrong on its face - there is no incoming attack while the user is performing one. Root cause is mechanical: parseAbility line 376 pushes stop riders as {...s, window: s.window ?? 'nextPhase'}, but parseDefensiveEffects ALWAYS assigns a window (defaulting to 'thisAttack' because /next\s*(phase|round)/ does not match "the next physical attack"), so the ?? fallback is dead code and the intended deferral never happens. Currently the effect only reaches applyIfSuccessful, which logs rather than resolves, so the live damage is limited - but the modeled data is wrong and will mis-resolve as soon as stops are automated.
verdicts.fixHint: In the attack-rider loop, OVERRIDE the window instead of defaulting it (stops on an attack card are never 'thisAttack'), and teach parseDefensiveEffects to recognize "stops the next <kind> attack performed against you this Combat" -> window:'nextPhase', scope:'single'.

verdicts.reason: Text is 'Energy attack doing 5 life cards of damage. Lower your anger 1 level.' and the parse contains only energyAttack{lifeCards:5}. 'your anger' targets the user per the anger convention, so changeAnger{target:'user',delta:-1} is plainly missing. Root cause is structural, not a vocabulary gap: pushAnger's raise branch (abilities.ts:253) needs /rais|gain...level|anger level N/ and 'Lower your anger 1 level' matches none (the text reads 'anger 1 level', not 'anger level 1'); the lower branch (:258) requires a foe/opponent mention, which is absent. No code path in pushAnger ever emits a negative user delta - line 256 always pushes toNum(...) positive. Self-anger reduction is the defining trait of the Straining cycle, so this silently drops the card's cost-side effect.
verdicts.fixHint: Add a lower-self-anger branch to pushAnger in packages/engine/src/abilities.ts: when /low\w*[^.]*anger/ matches and the foe-possessive-stripped text still shows a self marker (your / card user), push changeAnger{target:'user',delta:-N}. Also loosen the level-number match to accept 'anger 1 level' as well as 'anger level 1'.

verdicts.reason: Text is 'Energy attack. Raise your anger 2 levels. Lower opponent's anger 2 levels.' - two distinct anger effects on opposite sides. The parse has only changeAnger{foe,-2}. The user raise is genuinely dropped, and vocabulary for it exists. Root cause is the mutual-exclusion guard at abilities.ts:256: the raise branch matches correctly ('Raise your anger' survives the opponent-possessive strip), but is then suppressed by `if (!/low\w*[^.]*(foe|opponent)[^.]*anger/.test(t))` because the card also contains 'Lower opponent's anger'. The guard assumes a card cannot change anger on both sides, which this card does.
verdicts.fixHint: Remove or narrow the line-256 guard in packages/engine/src/abilities.ts so it only suppresses the user push when the ONLY anger clause is the foe one - e.g. split the text on sentence boundaries and run the raise/lower tests per clause, rather than testing the whole card text for both.

verdicts.reason: Text: 'If successful it also stops your opponent from making any more physical attacks in this combat.' 'any more physical attacks in this combat' is a combat-long lockout, which the vocabulary models exactly as window:'thisCombat' ('all such attacks this combat'). window:'thisAttack' is doubly wrong here: this is the user's own attack card, so there is no incoming attack for a thisAttack stop to consume - the engine would burn the effect on nothing and let every subsequent physical attack through. Root cause: abilities.ts:235 hardcodes 'thisAttack' as the fallback window; the only route to 'thisCombat' is the narrow 'no X attacks will work' regex at :219, which this wording misses.
verdicts.fixHint: Add a pattern in pushDefenseEffects (packages/engine/src/abilities.ts, near line 219) for /stops?\b[^.]*\b(any more|all)\s+(physical|energy)?\s*attacks?[^.]*(in this combat|rest of this combat|remainder of combat)/ that emits window:'thisCombat', scope:'all', and let it take precedence over the generic thisAttack fallback at :233-237.

verdicts.reason: Printed text says 'Stops all attacks for the remainder of Combat'; the parse emits window:'thisAttack', which stops exactly one attack. CRD.txt:1885 errata confirms and sharpens this: 'Stops a physical or energy attack and stops all attacks for the remainder of Combat.' So the card is a full combat shutdown and the parse understates it severely. One correction to the claim's expected shape: per the errata the card does BOTH - the existing thisAttack stop is a correct half, so the fix should ADD the thisCombat stop rather than replace the existing one as the claim's 'expected' implies. The defect itself (missing combat-long lockout) is unambiguously real.
verdicts.fixHint: Emit two effects for this card: keep stopAttack{attackType:'any',window:'thisAttack'} and add stopAttack{attackType:'any',window:'thisCombat',scope:'all'}. Requires both the thisCombat pattern and lifting the single-stop `alreadyStop` cap at abilities.ts:232.

verdicts.reason: Text is 'Stops all attacks from an opponent in this combat.' - a single clause, and it is explicitly combat-scoped ('all attacks', 'in this combat'). The parse's window:'thisAttack' reduces a combat-ending defensive card to a one-attack stop. No CRD errata exists for this card, so the printed text governs and it plainly contradicts the parse. Root cause is the same 'thisAttack' fallback at abilities.ts:235.
verdicts.fixHint: Same thisCombat pattern fix in packages/engine/src/abilities.ts; ensure 'in this combat' (not just 'remainder of Combat' / 'rest of this combat') is one of the recognised combat-duration phrases.

verdicts.reason: Text is 'Stops all energy attacks for the rest of this combat. Costs 2 life cards to use.' There is no single-attack clause anywhere in the text, so the claim's assertion that the card is purely a combat-long lockout is accurate and window:'thisAttack' is simply wrong (not merely incomplete). Unlike Frieza's Force Bubble (CRD.txt:1588), which has both a single-stop and a combat-long clause, this card has only the latter. The card name contains 'Focusing' but the text invokes no Focused mechanic, so the unmodelled-Focused caveat does not apply.
verdicts.fixHint: Same thisCombat pattern fix; here the emitted effect should REPLACE the thisAttack stop, yielding a single stopAttack{attackType:'energy',window:'thisCombat',scope:'all'}. Separately note the '2 life cards' cost is unrepresentable - AbilityCost has only powerStages/discard - but that is a known vocabulary gap, not part of this defect.

verdicts.reason: Text: 'Energy attack. If successful it stops the opponent from playing any other energy attack cards in this combat.' The rider is explicitly combat-long ('any other energy attack cards in this combat'), so window:'thisAttack' understates it - the engine would stop at most one energy attack and allow the rest. Same structural cause as Krillin's Power Block: an attack card whose rider got the generic thisAttack fallback at abilities.ts:235. The separate fact that stopAttack cannot carry the 'If successful' gate (ifSuccessful exists only on damageStages) is a real vocabulary gap but is NOT what this claim alleges, so it does not weaken the claim.
verdicts.fixHint: Same thisCombat pattern fix in packages/engine/src/abilities.ts. Note the attack-card rider path at :376 rewrites window to 'nextPhase' only when window is undefined, so the pattern must set 'thisCombat' explicitly for it to survive.

verdicts.reason: CRD-confirmed. CRD.txt:2403 reads: Vegeta's Jolting Slash (Frieza Saga - #17) - Treat this card as if it read, 'Energy attack. Stop all physical attacks performed against villains for the remainder of Combat. Lower your opponent's anger 2 levels. Remove from the game after use.' That matches the enriched text verbatim, so the vision-derived text is trustworthy. 'for the remainder of Combat' plainly contradicts window:'thisAttack'. The textOriginal variant ('against you' rather than 'against villains') differs only in who is protected - both versions say 'for the remainder of Combat', so the window claim holds regardless of which text version is authoritative.
verdicts.fixHint: Same thisCombat pattern fix, replacing the thisAttack stop with stopAttack{attackType:'physical',window:'thisCombat',scope:'all'}. The 'performed against villains' restriction on WHO is protected remains unmodelled (no such field on stopAttack) - flag via needsReview rather than pretending coverage.

verdicts.reason: Text is 'Stops an energy attack and stops all energy attacks for the rest of this combat.' - two grammatically distinct clauses joined by 'and'. The parse emits only one stopAttack (energy/thisAttack), correctly covering clause one, and silently drops clause two. Root cause is exact and mechanical: the `alreadyStop` flag at abilities.ts:232 gates the generic stop branch so at most ONE stopAttack is ever emitted per card, and the first clause consumes it. Fix is additive, matching the claim's expected shape.
verdicts.fixHint: Lift the single-stop restriction in packages/engine/src/abilities.ts:232 - split the text on 'and'/sentence boundaries and evaluate stop clauses independently so a thisAttack stop and a thisCombat stop can coexist on one card.

verdicts.reason: CRD-confirmed. CRD.txt:2455 reads: Yamcha's Good Wishes (Frieza Saga - #108) - Treat this card as if it read, 'Stops a physical attack and stops all physical attacks for the remainder of Combat. Remove from the game after use.' The enriched text's 'and all stops all' is an OCR stutter of 'and stops all', and the errata resolves it definitively as two clauses. The parse has only the first. Same `alreadyStop` root cause at abilities.ts:232.
verdicts.fixHint: Same clause-splitting fix at abilities.ts:232 so both stops emit. Optionally normalise the OCR stutter 'and all stops all' -> 'and stops all' during text cleanup so the second clause is matchable at all.

verdicts.reason: Text: 'Playing this card stops a single named opponent from making an energy attack on his next combat phase.' The vocabulary documents nextPhase as 'foe's next', which is precisely this timing; window:'thisAttack' is a different window entirely and would mis-time the lockout onto the current attack. Root cause is a pinpointable regex miss: abilities.ts:235 selects nextPhase via /next\s*(phase|round)/, which requires 'phase' to follow 'next' with only whitespace between. This card says 'next combat phase' - the interposed 'combat' defeats the match, so it falls through to the thisAttack default. The scope:'single' the parser already derived is correct and should be retained. CRD.txt:2077 mentions this card only to note it is a 'Saiyan Heritage only' card, which does not bear on the window.
verdicts.fixHint: Widen the window regex at packages/engine/src/abilities.ts:235 from /next\s*(phase|round)/ to tolerate an interposed qualifier, e.g. /next\s+(\w+\s+)?(phase|round|combat\s+phase)/, so 'next combat phase' resolves to nextPhase.

verdicts.reason: The parse's effects array contains ONLY removeFromGameAfterUse - the card has zero modelled function, so the engine would play it, remove it from the game, and stop nothing. Printed text 'Stops an opponent's current or next combat.' plus CRD.txt:2053 (Frieza Saga #19: 'use it during Combat, in place of an attack, to either a) end the current Combat, or b) make your opponent skip his next Combat step') confirm the card is entirely a combat-denial card. This is not a vocabulary gap - both halves have vocabulary (stopAttack window:'thisCombat' and stunSkipNextPhase). Root cause: the stop regex at abilities.ts:233 requires the literal token 'attack', and this card's text says 'combat', so no stop effect is generated at all.
verdicts.fixHint: Add a pattern recognising 'stops an opponent's current or next combat' in packages/engine/src/abilities.ts. Since the card is modal (player chooses), emit the more common mode plus a needsReview flag, or emit stopAttack{attackType:'any',window:'thisCombat'} and stunSkipNextPhase with a needsReview:'modalChoice' marker rather than silently applying both - Effect has no modal/choice representation today.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed by running the parser. The card's final sentence 'If successful, remove from the game.' is self-removal of the card, and removeFromGameAfterUse is in the vocabulary and applied on sibling cards in the same batch (Red Shielded Strike tts-40b278df-16, Orange Energy Setup tts-40b278df-2) whose text reads 'Remove from the game after use.' The only difference is wording: removesAfterUse in packages/engine/src/abilities.ts:324 requires the literal 'after use', so this variant is dropped. Probe: 'Focused energy attack doing 5 life cards of damage. Remove from the game after use.' -> emits removeFromGameAfterUse; the same text with 'If successful, remove from the game.' -> does not. Not a vocabulary gap, and the gate is honored anyway: removeFromGameAfterUse falls through setupAttackAbility's default branch into attack.ifSuccessfulEffects, so it only resolves on success. (The discard-pile shuffle clause is genuinely unmodeled and is not part of this claim.)
verdicts.fixHint: Broaden removesAfterUse to accept the objectless self-removal sentence, e.g. /remov\w*\s+(this card\s+)?from (the )?game/ anchored on a sentence with no object, while excluding object-bearing sentences on this same card ('Remove 2 of them from the game', which refers to discard-pile cards). Anchoring on sentence start plus absence of a following noun before 'from' is enough.

verdicts.reason: The parse is right on everything the vocabulary can express: energyAttack with no lifeCards (defaults to 4), cost 3 power stages overriding the default 2, discard target foe, count 1, and Endurance 2 correctly kept out of the attack. The sole complaint is that the discard's gating is not represented — but Effect has no conditional field at all, and there is no Tokui-Waza concept anywhere in the model, so this reduces to missing vocabulary, which is a known gap rather than a parse defect. It also matches settled corpus behavior for conditional riders (e.g. Black Energy Assault emits discardCards foe 1 from an 'If successful, you may discard...' clause). Flagging this card alone would send an engineer to a corpus-wide modeling decision, not a bug.

Every field the vocabulary can carry is correct: stopAttack physical in the ordinary thisAttack window, and 'raise your anger 1 level' correctly resolved to target 'user' delta 1 (the errata-era 'your anger' wording, which pushAnger handles explicitly). The claim is only that the Tokui-Waza gate is missing, and Effect has no conditional field to hold it. This is the established pattern, not a one-off: 18 of the 28 corpus cards with a Tokui-Waza-gated anger clause emit changeAnger unconditionally (Orange Rage, Red Knee Bash, Blue Speediness, Orange Surprise Reaction all identical in shape). Same known vocabulary gap as tts-40b278df-1.

'Attack, or stops an attack' dual-mode cards are represented corpus-wide as one attack-trigger ability holding both modes: 12 of the 13 such cards parse exactly this way (Blue Arm Blast, Blue Impulse, Black Knife Hand Strike, Fierce Left Kick, Trunks Draws Steel, ...). This card follows that convention, so the parse is consistent rather than defective, and the claim's expected output would make it the outlier. The alleged harm also does not occur: stopAttack is not handled in setupAttackAbility's switch, so it falls into attack.ifSuccessfulEffects, and applyIfSuccessful (packages/engine/src/abilities.ts:138) only writes a log line for stopAttack — no attack is actually stopped. What is genuinely absent is mode selection and the Tokui-Waza condition, neither of which the vocabulary can express.

Confirmed real and root-caused. The card is a printed dual-mode card, and the corpus convention for that construction is trigger 'attack' with [attack, stopAttack] — 12 of 13 such cards parse that way. This one is the sole outlier: the attack mode is dropped entirely, so firstAttackAbility can never find it and the card cannot be played as a physical attack. Cause is an ordering bug in stripLeadingNoise (packages/engine/src/abilities.ts:188): stripLead is applied before stripEndurance and is anchored at ^, so on 'Endurance 3. Namekian Heritage only. Physical attack, ...' the Endurance prefix shields the 'Namekian Heritage only.' restriction from being stripped; body still starts with 'namekian', startsPhysical fails, and it falls to the defense branch. Verified by probe: dropping either the Endurance prefix or the restriction yields the correct {physicalAttack, stopAttack} attack ability. This also silently loses the restriction, which parseRestriction never sees.
verdicts.fixHint: In stripLeadingNoise, run the strippers to a fixed point instead of in a fixed order — loop stripEndurance / stripTypePlate / stripLead until the string stops changing — so 'Endurance N.' followed by an 'X only.' restriction is fully peeled. parseRestriction should likewise run against the stripped body (or on a pre-stripped copy) so the Namekian-Heritage-only restriction is captured.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed, and it is a systematic bug rather than a one-card slip. CRD glossary line 2519: Defense Shields are activated when you do not stop an opponent's attack and attempt to stop the first unstopped attack; CRD battle-sequence step 7 (line 337) fires them only after the attack was not otherwise stopped. That is exactly the documented meaning of the window enum's 'firstSuccessful' ('the first that gets through'), so 'thisAttack' — the currently declared attack in the normal defense window — is the wrong value and loses the once-per-Combat, only-if-nothing-else-stopped-it semantics. Root cause verified: the firstSuccessful branches (abilities.ts:223 and the ternary at :235) match only the literal 'first successful', so 'first unstopped' falls through to thisAttack. Corpus scan: 33 cards print 'first unstopped', 0 print 'first successful' — the firstSuccessful enum value is currently dead code and every Defense Shield in the corpus is mis-windowed.
verdicts.fixHint: Widen both firstSuccessful matches to accept the unstopped wording, e.g. /first\s+(successful|un\W?stopped)\s+(physical|energy)?\s*(?:life\s*card\s*)?attack/ at abilities.ts:223 and the same alternation in the window ternary at :235. Keying on a leading 'Defense Shield:' label as a second signal would also catch OCR-mangled variants.

verdicts.reason: Same confirmed defect as tts-930d6a1e-63, energy variant. Parse emits window 'thisAttack' because the firstSuccessful branch only matches the literal 'first successful'. attackType 'energy' is correct; only the window is wrong.
verdicts.fixHint: Same fix as tts-930d6a1e-63: accept 'first unstopped' alongside 'first successful' in both firstSuccessful branches (abilities.ts:223 and :235).

verdicts.fixHint: Same fix as tts-930d6a1e-63 — one regex change at abilities.ts:223 and :235 corrects all 33 affected Defense Shield cards.

verdicts.fixHint: Same fix as tts-930d6a1e-63 (abilities.ts:223 and :235).

verdicts.reason: The window defect holds independently of the OCR damage. Even in the garbled text the shield wording survives ('Stops the first unNstopped energy \ attack ... during Combat'), so this is the same Defense Shield mechanic and the same mis-window: 'thisAttack' where CRD glossary line 2519 / battle-sequence step 7 call for the first attack not otherwise stopped, i.e. 'firstSuccessful'. Judged on window only, as the claim scopes it; the attackType 'any' on this record is a separate issue driven by the 'unNstopped' corruption breaking the (physical|energy) capture.
verdicts.fixHint: Same regex widening at abilities.ts:223 and :235; make it tolerant of OCR noise between words (e.g. /first\W+un\W?\w{0,2}stopped/ and allowing stray punctuation before 'attack'), which would also let the energy qualifier be captured on this record.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Text: "After you stop an attack with a Red Style card that does not remove itself from the game, place it on the bottom of your Life Deck." That is a trigger condition on a stop achieved by some OTHER card, not a grant. The parse emits stopAttack{attackType:'any',window:'thisAttack'} under trigger 'defense', handing the engine a free universal attack-stopper the Mastery never provides. Contrast tts-3ae57df1-56 Blue Style Mastery ("you may discard a card from your hand to stop a physical or energy attack") whose stopAttack IS warranted — the parser cannot tell "after you stop" from "to stop". Note also that most Masteries in the corpus are correctly left with no abilities at all, so this is over-extraction on a card that should have been left alone. The 'constant' trigger in the claim's expected output is unreachable (see other verdicts), but the defect stands independently of it: the stopAttack must be dropped.
verdicts.fixHint: In the stop-detector, require the stop verb to be in the card's own grant position. Exclude clauses introduced by "After you stop", "Whenever you stop", "When you stop" — these are recursion triggers. Only "Stops a/an ..." or "... to stop a/an ..." should emit stopAttack. Leave Red Style Mastery with a manual effect.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Full text: "Energy attack. Empower 3. All your other energy attacks do +1 life cards of damage for the remainder of Combat. Lower your opponent's anger 2 levels." The card states NO damage amount for itself, so CRD applies: "Energy attacks cost 2 power stages to perform and deal 4 life cards of damage" (docs/CRD.txt, the '2 kinds of attacks' paragraph). The parser scraped the 1 out of "+1 life cards" — a clause about OTHER attacks — and installed it as this attack's fixed base. Two compounding errors: wrong scope (other attacks, not this one) and wrong semantics ("+1" is a modifier, never a base; only "doing N life cards of damage" sets a base, per CRD "Cards that state damage... the damage from the attack is what is stated on the card itself"). Engine deals 1 instead of 4.
verdicts.fixHint: Only bind lifeCards on an attack from a bare "doing N life card(s) of damage" phrase attached to this attack's own sentence. Reject any number preceded by '+' and any number inside a clause scoped to "all your other ..." / "all your ..." attacks. Emit {kind:'energyAttack'} with no lifeCards here; route the floating +1 buff to needsReview.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Text: "Physical attack doing +5 power stages of damage or stops a focused energy attack." The 'or' is an exclusive mode choice made at play time. The parse emits physicalAttack + damageStages{5} + stopAttack{energy} together in one effects list under trigger 'attack', so the engine resolves both modes from a single play — a +5-stage attack that also cancels an incoming energy attack. Independently, a stopAttack cannot even fire meaningfully under an 'attack' trigger, which is corroborating evidence the effect was appended mechanically rather than understood. The fix requires no new vocabulary, just dropping the second mode.
verdicts.fixHint: Detect the top-level disjunction "<attack clause> or <defense clause>" before effect extraction and stop scanning at the ' or ' boundary. Emit the attack mode only ([physicalAttack, damageStages:5]) and add needsReview:['modalChoice'] so the defensive alternative is resolved by hand.

verdicts.reason: The value loss is real but this is not a card-level parsing defect — it is an unimplemented extractor, which the brief excludes. changePowerStages appears ZERO times across the entire enriched corpus (0 effects in 1160 abilities), while 38 cards carry the literal phrase "Gain N power stages" — including Namekian Fist Block ("Stops a physical attack. Gain 3 power stages."), Namekian Energy Catch, Black Arm Stretch, and Red Passive Block. The parser has no rule for this phrase at all; it did not fail on this card specifically. The claim's premise ("changePowerStages is in the vocabulary") is true of packages/shared/src/abilities.ts but not of the parser, so filing 1 of 38 as a per-card defect mis-scopes the work. This card also silently drops "Your opponent discards the top card of his Life Deck" — same class. Contrast tts-117cae92-66, where an extractor that demonstrably works elsewhere fails, which I did mark real.
verdicts.fixHint: Do not patch this card. Open one systemic ticket: add a "Gain/Lose N power stages" -> changePowerStages{target:'user',delta:±N} extractor (guarded against "+N power stages of damage", which is damageStages, and against "Costs N power stages to perform", which is cost.powerStages), then re-run and diff all 38 matching cards at once.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Text: "If used by Majin Buu, this attack is focused and raises your anger 1 level." The parse emits changeAnger{target:'user',delta:+1} unconditionally alongside physicalAttack and damageStages{3}, with no restriction and no needsReview. Any personality playing this card gains an anger level the card does not grant — the printed text plainly contradicts the parse. This is over-extraction (asserting something false), not a vocabulary gap: the minimum correct fix is simply not to emit the effect, which needs no new schema. The parser does own a 'performerCondition' review flag (used on tts-514f40cb-36 Android 17's Back Bash) but it appears exactly once in 1160 abilities and was not applied here.
verdicts.fixHint: When an effect clause sits inside a performer conditional ("If used by X", "If performed by X", "If this attack is performed by X"), do not hoist it into the unconditional effects list. Either attach restriction.namedOnly:['Majin Buu'] on a separate ability or drop the effect and set needsReview:['performerCondition']. Worth applying corpus-wide: 43 cards match this phrasing and effects are currently being hoisted from several (e.g. Gotenks Flight, Red Android 13's Rapid Blasts).

verdicts.reason: The claim's premise does not survive checking the source. The text the parser received is OCR-garbled and self-contradictory: data/ocr.tts.json textRaw reads "Focused energy attack doing 3 life\n\n4 cards of damage" at 70% text confidence. Every line in that raw block begins with a spurious border glyph ("|!", then "4", then "§", then "|"), so the stray 4 is almost certainly art bleed and the true base is likely 3 — but nothing in the text as given PLAINLY states 3, which is the bar. The parser did the right conservative thing: it declined to guess a base and set needsReview:['energyLifeCards','focusedAttack']. That is the designed escape hatch working, and the claim concedes the flag exists. Filing this as a parser defect duplicates a review item the system already raised, and the real fault is upstream in OCR, not in parsing.
verdicts.fixHint: No parser change. Fix at the OCR layer: strip line-leading single-glyph artifacts before joining lines in the tts OCR pipeline, which would yield the clean "doing 3 life cards of damage" and let the existing extractor bind lifeCards:3. Until then, a human reviewer clearing the existing needsReview:'energyLifeCards' flag should set lifeCards:3.

verdicts.reason: Unimplemented extractor rather than a per-card omission. cost.discard is emitted ZERO times corpus-wide, against 19 cards carrying a discard-to-do-X cost pattern (Total Defense Drill, Blue Style Mastery, Saiyan Hurricane Kick, Red Style Mastery, Saiyan Face Stomp, and this card among them). The claim's supporting argument is misleading: the 80 abilities that do carry a cost all use cost.powerStages, extracted from the single formulaic sentence "Costs N power stages to perform" — a different field reached by a different rule. There is no discard-cost rule for this card to have failed. The free-unlimited-stop consequence is genuine, but it applies identically to all 19 cards, so this belongs in one systemic ticket, not a card fix.
verdicts.fixHint: Do not patch this card. Open one ticket to add a discard-cost extractor for "(you may) discard a/one/N card(s) [from your hand|in your hand|the top card of your Life Deck] to <effect>" -> cost.discard:N, then diff all 19 matching cards. The "card that can perform an energy attack" qualifier stays unmodelable and should go to needsReview.
