verdicts.reason: Confirmed, and it is a bug in an extractor that demonstrably works — which is what separates it from the other missing-field claims here. 26 abilities in the corpus carry a restriction, and of 32 cards whose text opens with "Heroes only"/"Villains only", the parser captures 20 and drops 12 — every single captured one is {alignment:'Hero'} and every single dropped one is a "Villains only" card (Android 18's Low Blow, Android 20's Enraged, Cell's Dark Attack, Cell's Defense, Just Thinking, Saiyan City Destruction, this card, and others). The alignment matcher plainly handles only the Hero branch. CRD confirms the restriction binds usability, not just deck construction: a Rogue personality declared Hero "still would not be able to use 'Villains only' cards". Parsed effects (energyAttack lifeCards:3, changeAnger foe -2) are otherwise correct.
verdicts.fixHint: The "only" prefix regex is matching Heroes but not Villains — extend it to the Villain branch and emit restriction:{alignment:'Villain'}. One fix clears all 12 dropped cards; verify against the 20 Hero cards that already pass. (The "+1 life card per Villains-only card in discard" clause remains unmodelable.)

verdicts.reason: The schema comment does read "'constant' // Drills / continuous", but the parser emits only three triggers across the whole corpus — attack 760, defense 334, onPlay 66 — and 'constant', 'personalityPower' and 'whenEnteringCombat' appear ZERO times in 1160 abilities. There is no classifier to have misfired. Worse, the fix as filed would make this card inconsistent with 36 sibling Drills: all 37 defensive Drills are parsed 'defense', including the Defense Shield family ("Stops the first unstopped energy attack performed against you during Combat"), which is every bit as automatic and always-on as this one. The printed text contradicts nothing in the parse, and the effect payload — preventLifeCards{amount:2,attackType:'any'} — is correct. Changing one card out of 37 is the kind of false alarm the brief warns about.
verdicts.fixHint: No card fix. If the team wants trigger fidelity, open one design ticket to decide the convention and reclassify all 37 defensive Drills together — continuous/passive Drills to 'constant', activated ones (Total Defense Drill, Namekian Precise Aim Drill) staying 'defense' — and confirm the engine actually branches on trigger before spending the effort.

verdicts.reason: Same systemic gap: 'personalityPower' is emitted ZERO times in 1160 abilities. All nine "Power:"-labeled personality cards in the corpus are parsed 'defense' — Majin Buu, Jeice the Avenger, Bulma, Goku the Mighty, King Kai, Mighty Mask, Goku Super Saiyan, Bulma the Wife, and this one. The root cause is upstream classification, not the ability parser: data/ocr.tts.json records this card as isPersonality=false with type "Physical Combat" and an empty needsReview, and the ability trigger simply follows that type. The text itself is heavily garbled ("1.325.000 J fA Majin Power:", "4 the top 3 cards"), so the personality signal was never available downstream. The stopAttack effect is correct, as the claim concedes, and nothing in the printed text contradicts the parse's effects.
verdicts.fixHint: Fix upstream, not per-card: the OCR type classifier should set isPersonality=true when a power-rating numeral pattern (e.g. 1.325.000 / 1,325,000) co-occurs with a "<X> Power:" or "Constant Combat Power:" label, and flag needsReview:['type'] when confidence is low as it already does for Majin Buu and Jeice. Once isPersonality is right, add the 'personalityPower' trigger mapping and re-run all nine affected cards together.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Text: "Physical attack doing +3 power stages of damage. This attack can only be stopped as if it were an energy attack." That sentence is a rules note constraining how the OPPONENT may stop this attack — it grants this card no stopping ability whatsoever. The parse appends stopAttack{attackType:'energy',window:'thisAttack'} to an 'attack'-triggered card, so the engine would let this attack card cancel an incoming energy attack. Classic passive-voice inversion: "can only be stopped" was read as "stops". The correct parse is physicalAttack + damageStages{3} only, which needs no new vocabulary — just deletion.
verdicts.fixHint: Add a negative lookaround to the stop-detector so passive constructions about this card being stopped never emit stopAttack: exclude "can only be stopped", "cannot be stopped", "is stopped", "if this attack is stopped". Drop the clause or route to needsReview:['stopTypeOverride'] — the 'stopped as if energy' mechanic has no schema representation.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Text: "Physical attack. Your opponent cannot take life cards or power stages of damage from this attack." The parse is a bare {kind:'physicalAttack'}, which per the schema comment falls back to the Physical Attack Table default and deals real power-stage damage. The card explicitly deals none — it is a damage-less attack whose purpose is to satisfy attack-dependent triggers. The printed text directly contradicts what the engine will do, and this is the only card in the corpus with this pattern, so it is a genuine one-off rather than a systemic gap. The fix needs no new vocabulary: the schema already documents that a set powerStages OVERRIDES the PAT default, and 0 is a valid value (no attack in the corpus currently uses an explicit 0, so also add a test).
verdicts.fixHint: Emit {kind:'physicalAttack',powerStages:0} when the text contains a "opponent cannot take (life cards|power stages) of damage from this attack" clause, and confirm the engine treats powerStages:0 as a genuine override rather than falsy-coercing it back to the PAT lookup — that coercion is the likely trap. Set needsReview if the twice-per-Combat clause matters.

verdicts.reason: CRD line 2323 prints the errata verbatim: "Heroes only. Energy attack. If performed by Tien, draw a card." The draw is gated on the performer; the parse lists drawCards as a peer of energyAttack with no gate, so any Hero performing it draws. The pre-errata textOriginal is even weaker ("If Tien is in play anywhere, you may draw another card" — optional as well as conditional), so the unconditional draw is wrong under either printing. This is not a vocabulary complaint: drawCards exists and is modeled, the parser simply asserts it in a case the card forbids. Corpus sampling confirms the parser is inconsistent here — it drops the rider on Android 14's Power Kick, Broly's Might, and Cooler's Surprise Attack but hoists it on Underwater Kick and Majin Buu's Childish Taunt.
verdicts.fixHint: When a clause is prefixed with a personality/board condition ("If performed by X", "If used by X", "If <card> is in play"), do not emit its effects into the unconditional effects array. Drop them and record the clause in needsReview (e.g. 'conditional:performedByTien'). Do not use restriction.namedOnly here — that is ability-level and would wrongly bar non-Tien Heroes from using the card at all.

verdicts.reason: Card type is Physical Combat and the text opens "Physical attack doing +4 power stages of damage", yet the parse has trigger 'defense' and a single stopAttack{any,thisAttack} — the attack and its modifier are dropped entirely. The only occurrence of "stop an attack" is inside the Majin-conditional clause describing which card may be chosen from hand and put into play; it stops nothing. So the parse both loses the card's real function and grants a universal attack-stop the card never offers.
verdicts.fixHint: Anchor trigger detection on the leading attack declaration ("Physical attack ..." / "Energy attack ...") before any stop-phrase scan, and only treat "stops a/an ... attack" as a stopAttack when it is the sentence's main verb with the card as subject — not when it sits inside a relative clause qualifying another card ("a card ... that can perform an attack or stop an attack"). Correct parse: trigger 'attack', effects [{physicalAttack},{damageStages,stages:4}], with the Majin clause in needsReview.

verdicts.reason: Same wrong-trigger failure as Heroic Charge and worse. Text opens "Physical attack doing +3 power stages of damage" on a Physical Combat card, but the parse is trigger 'defense' with stopAttack{any,thisAttack}; physicalAttack and damageStages 3 are both missing. The stop in the text is triple-qualified — conditional on the target being Majin, limited to focused attacks, and delayed to the opponent's next Attacker Attacks phase — and the parse asserts it as an unconditional stop of the current attack of any type. Per CRD line 1160 'focused' is its own mechanic the engine does not model, so the stop should be dropped, not widened. changeAnger{user,+1} for "Raise your anger 1 level" is the one correct part.
verdicts.fixHint: Same conditional/relative-clause gating as Heroic Charge, plus: never widen a qualified stop into attackType 'any' + window 'thisAttack'. Correct parse: trigger 'attack', effects [{physicalAttack},{damageStages,stages:3},{changeAnger,target:'user',delta:1}], with the Majin/focused clause routed to needsReview.

verdicts.reason: abilities.ts lines 24-27 state that when lifeCards is set it is a fixed amount that OVERRIDES the default base, so physicalAttack{lifeCards:2} means 'physical attack causing exactly 2 life cards' and the Physical Attack Table is never rolled. The card prints a bare "Physical attack" (PAT base) plus "+2 life cards of damage for each Dragon Ball you control" — a per-Dragon-Ball multiplier, not a base. At 0 Dragon Balls the parse deals a flat 2 life cards where the card should deal the PAT result plus nothing; at 3 Dragon Balls it still deals 2 instead of PAT +6. Endurance 3 was correctly split off into its own field, so it is not the source of the number. The same conflation appears on Carpet Attack Technique (tts-bf3b8d7f-9), where "doing 3 power stages of damage" became lifeCards:3.
verdicts.fixHint: Only emit lifeCards/powerStages on an attack when the number is attached to the attack declaration itself ("Physical attack doing N ..."). A separate sentence beginning "This attack does +N ..." is a modifier, and one carrying a scaling phrase ("for each ...") is variable and unmodelable. Correct parse: [{physicalAttack}] with the Dragon Ball scaling in needsReview.

verdicts.reason: The card contains no stop effect at all. Its one mention of stopping is a negative qualifier — the clause ends floating effects "that do NOT stop attacks" — so the parser inverted the sense of the exclusion and emitted stopAttack{any,thisAttack}. The consequence is concrete: an attack card would additionally cancel the opponent's current attack of either type, which nothing on the card authorizes. The rest of the parse (physicalAttack, damageStages 3, changeAnger user +1) is sound.
verdicts.fixHint: Suppress stopAttack extraction when the trigger phrase falls inside a negated or exclusionary clause ("that do not stop attacks", "cannot be stopped", "except ..."). Correct parse: [{physicalAttack},{damageStages,stages:3},{changeAnger,target:'user',delta:1}], floating-effect removal to needsReview. Adjacent (not claimed, lower priority): damageStages carries ifSuccessful:true, but the "If successful" in the text governs only the floating-effect clause, not the +3.

verdicts.reason: Nothing on the card removes it from the game. "remove themselves from the game after use" is a restrictive qualifier identifying which of your Non-Combat/Non-Drill cards the floating effect applies to, and the actual instruction for those cards is the opposite disposition — bottom of the Life Deck. Blue Backhand is a Physical Combat card, so the floating effect does not even reach itself. The parse would exile the card instead of discarding it, which is a real behavioral difference for later rejuvenation and recycling. physicalAttack{powerStages:5} is correct — "doing 5 power stages of damage" is a fixed base.
verdicts.fixHint: Only emit removeFromGameAfterUse when the removal is an imperative about this card ("Remove from the game after use."), not when the phrase appears inside a relative clause describing a class of other cards. Correct parse: [{physicalAttack,powerStages:5}].

verdicts.reason: "If used by Majin Buu, raise your anger 1 level" is gated on the personality, but changeAnger{user,+1} sits unconditionally alongside physicalAttack and damageStages 4, so any personality performing the card gets a free anger raise. Structurally identical to the Tien's Jolting Aura defect and confirmed by the corpus as the same parser behavior (the rider is dropped on Broly's Might and Cooler's Surprise Attack but hoisted here, on Underwater Kick, and on Majin Buu's Childish Taunt).
verdicts.fixHint: Same fix as tts-7b6b6ee0-15: gate-prefixed clauses must not contribute unconditional effects. Drop the changeAnger and flag the clause. restriction.namedOnly:['Majin Buu'] is the wrong remedy — it is ability-level and would stop every other personality from using an otherwise unrestricted attack.

verdicts.reason: [wrong-effect / stopAttack window] The text scopes the stop to "your opponent's next 'Attacker Attacks' phase", which is exactly the schema's window 'nextPhase' (abilities.ts line 37-39: nextPhase = foe's next). The parse uses 'thisAttack', so on an attack card the stop would be consumed against a current attack that does not exist while you are attacking, and the delayed defensive window it should create is lost entirely. CRD line 2179 (Saiyan Energy Aura, errata'd to "stops an energy attack AND stops an energy attack during your opponent's next Attacker Attacks phase") shows the game treats the immediate and next-phase stops as two separate grants — Black Shift Kick prints only the delayed one.
verdicts.fixHint: Detect the trailing scope phrase "during your opponent's next 'Attacker Attacks' phase" and map it to window:'nextPhase' rather than defaulting to 'thisAttack'. Default to 'thisAttack' only when the stop clause carries no timing qualifier.

verdicts.reason: [missing-effect / rejuvenate] "Place the bottom 2 cards of your discard pile at the bottom of your Life Deck" is precisely the modeled rejuvenate effect — discard pile to bottom of Life Deck, with `from` naming which end of the discard pile the cards come off (abilities.ts lines 44-50). The parse omits it, so the card silently returns nothing. This is not a vocabulary gap: the parser already emits rejuvenate elsewhere (Piccolo's Power Ball, tts-be34bddc-66), and CRD line 1541 shows the same wording pattern on Earth Dragon Ball 5. The OCR typo "y our" in the source text is the likely reason the pattern failed to match.
verdicts.fixHint: Add a rejuvenate pattern for "place the (top|bottom) N card(s) of your discard pile at the bottom of your Life Deck", mapping the named end to `from` and the count to `count`; make the matcher whitespace-tolerant so OCR splits like "y our" do not defeat it. Add {kind:'rejuvenate',count:2,from:'bottom'}.

verdicts.reason: "Place the top card of your discard pile at the bottom of your Life Deck" is the rejuvenate effect with count 1 and from 'top', and the parse drops it while correctly capturing the stopAttack, the anger raise, and the removal from game. Same modeled-vocabulary-exists situation as Black Shift Kick, so this is an extraction miss rather than a coverage gap.
verdicts.fixHint: Same rejuvenate pattern as above, with the singular form ("the top card") mapping to count 1. Add {kind:'rejuvenate',count:1,from:'top'}.

verdicts.reason: "Raise your Main Personality to his highest power stage" maps one-to-one onto the modeled movePowerStage{target:'user',to:'highest'} (abilities.ts line 32), yet the parse holds only physicalAttack and damageStages 5. The power swing — often the whole reason to play the card — never fires. Confirmed as a real game action by CRD lines 529 and 1231, which use the identical phrasing for the anger-advance reset.
verdicts.fixHint: Add a pattern for "raise your Main Personality to his highest power stage" -> {kind:'movePowerStage',target:'user',to:'highest'} (and the symmetric 'lowest'/opponent forms). Note the trailing "Place at the bottom of your Life Deck after use" refers to this card, not the discard pile, so it must NOT become a rejuvenate.

verdicts.reason: Identical omission on a defense card: the text raises the user's Main Personality to his highest power stage, a directly modeled effect, but the parse contains only stopAttack{physical,thisAttack}. The trigger 'defense' is correct (per the rule that "Stops a physical attack" marks a defense card), so the only defect is the dropped movePowerStage. The trailing "prevent 1 power stage of damage" clause is genuinely unmodelable — preventLifeCards covers life cards, not power stages — and is correctly absent.
verdicts.fixHint: Same movePowerStage pattern as tts-2b332fa4-3, and make effect extraction continue past the trigger-determining clause on defense cards so riders after the stop are not dropped. Add {kind:'movePowerStage',target:'user',to:'highest'} alongside the stopAttack; leave the power-stage prevention in needsReview.

verdicts.reason: [wrong-effect] Holds. Printed text is 'Stops the FIRST UNSTOPPED energy attack performed against you during Combat', which is exactly what the schema documents as window 'firstSuccessful' (packages/shared/src/abilities.ts:39, 'the first that gets through'). The parse records window 'thisAttack' (= the current attack), a different and strictly broader window. This is a parser near-miss, not a vocabulary gap: parseDefensiveEffects already emits 'firstSuccessful' at packages/engine/src/abilities.ts:223-224 and re-checks /first successful/ at line 235, but only matches the literal word 'successful', so the synonym 'unstopped' falls through to the generic stop branch (line 233-237) and defaults to 'thisAttack'. CRD:337 and CRD:2519 confirm the Defense Shield semantics ('Defense Shields attempt to stop the first unstopped attack'). Affects the whole Defense Shield family (36 cards carry that phrase).
verdicts.fixHint: In packages/engine/src/abilities.ts, add 'unstopped' alongside 'successful' in both the firstSuccessful matcher (line 223) and the window selector (line 235), e.g. /first\s+(successful|unstopped)/, so 'first unstopped ... attack' yields window 'firstSuccessful'.

verdicts.reason: [wrong-trigger] Does not hold. The claim's premise — 'a Non-Combat card cannot [be played to defend] during Combat' — is contradicted by the CRD. Battle-sequence step 5 (CRD:329) reads 'The defender plays a card from his hand OR USES A NON-COMBAT CARD or personality power to defend against that attack', and CRD:304-305 lists the two defense options as (1) play a starburst card from hand and (2) 'Use one of your Non-Combat cards in play if that card has a starburst on it.' So trigger 'defense' ('used to defend') is a defensible classification for a Non-Combat card. Separately this is a class-wide taxonomy question, not a per-card parse defect: the parser has no branch that ever emits 'constant' (corpus trigger counts are defense:334, attack:760, onPlay:66, constant:0), and nothing in the engine consumes the defense trigger at all (resolveDefense at combat.ts:232-240 accepts any offered card without reading abilities). Retagging every stop-card is a modeling decision, and the printed text does not plainly contradict the current value.
verdicts.fixHint: None needed for this card. If a distinct permanent-in-play trigger is wanted, that is a schema/classifier design change across all 334 'defense' abilities (and would need a rule for Defense-Shield-at-step-7 vs. chosen-at-step-5), not a fix to this parse.

verdicts.reason: [wrong-trigger] Does not hold — the asserted consequence does not occur. The claim says the +5 is 'treated as a post-step-15 secondary effect instead of part of the attack's own damage calculation', but the engine sums both buckets in one expression: combat.ts:259 computes total = baseDamage + empower + modifiers + ifSuccessfulStages, and abilities.ts:74-77 routes damageStages into one or the other. Those are the ONLY two readers of either field in the whole repo (verified by grep across engine/shared/server/client). That total is computed solely on the 'take the damage → attack is successful' path (combat.ts:242-260), so a stopped attack deals zero stages either way. Removing the flag would change no game outcome. It is also not wrong in rules terms: physical stage damage is only ever dealt on a successful attack (CRD steps 8-15), so tagging the modifier ifSuccessful is redundant, not contradictory. The genuinely unmodeled part (opponent discards top 2 Life Deck cards) is a vocabulary gap the claim itself concedes.
verdicts.fixHint: Cosmetic only. If desired, tighten ifSucc (abilities.ts:156) so it scopes to the sentence containing the modifier rather than the whole text — but it is a no-op for damageStages given combat.ts:259.

verdicts.reason: [wrong-trigger] Does not hold, same reasoning as Saiyan Flying Kick. abilities.ts:74-77 puts the 2 stages into ifSuccessfulStages instead of modifiers, and combat.ts:259 adds both into the identical damage total on the successful-attack path only; no other code reads either field. The parse therefore deals exactly PAT+2 whether or not the flag is present, so nothing about the attack's damage calculation is lost. The card's real coverage gap (choose and discard a card from the opponent's hand, plus the unmodeled 'Focused' mechanic) is already flagged via needsReview:['focusedAttack'].
verdicts.fixHint: Cosmetic only; no behavioral fix required. Optional: sentence-scope the ifSucc heuristic at abilities.ts:156/366.

verdicts.reason: [wrong-effect] Holds, and this is the most damaging item in the set. The card performs no attack — it is a defensive cap ('Energy attacks do a maximum of 2 life cards and 0 power stages of damage for the remainder of Combat'), the exact category the parser's own header comment warns about (abilities.ts:8-10: cards that merely MENTION attacks must not be treated as attacks). Traced the failure: stripEndurance removes 'Endurance 3.' (line 184), leaving the body starting 'energy attacks do a maximum of...', which satisfies startsEnergy /^(a\s+)?energy\s+attack/ at line 345. parseAttackDamage then finds nothing ('do a maximum of 2 life cards' does not match the 'doing/does/do + digits' or 'N life cards of damage' forms), so the effect is a bare energyAttack, and abilities.ts:72 / combat.ts:250 default it to 4 life cards. Result: a defensive card is playable as a 4-life-card energy attack — worse than the printed effect in the opposite direction. needsReview:['type','energyLifeCards'] flags uncertainty but the ability is still live to firstAttackAbility (abilities.ts:27-29).
verdicts.fixHint: Guard startsEnergy/startsPhysical against plural-subject statements the way the 'all physical attacks' case is already noted at abilities.ts:338-340 — require singular 'energy attack' not followed by a plural verb, or reject when the sentence contains 'a maximum of'/'for the remainder of Combat' with no attack declaration. Emit no attack effect; nearest vocabulary is preventLifeCards or manual.

verdicts.reason: [spurious-effect] Holds. The clause is a PROHIBITION on both players using stop cards ('cards that stops all physical attacks or energy attacks, cannot be used for the remainder of Combat'), confirmed by the stored errata ('Neither player may use cards that end Combat, stop all physical attacks and stop all energy attacks'). The card grants no stop whatsoever, yet the parse carries stopAttack{physical, thisAttack}. Traced: parseDefensiveEffects runs on the FULL text (abilities.ts:348) and the generic matcher /stop\w*\s+.{0,40}?(physical|energy)?\s*attack/ (line 233) fires inside the prohibition clause; line 376 then appends it as an attack rider. It lands in ifSuccessfulEffects (line 91-94). Today applyIfSuccessful only logs it (line 138) rather than actually stopping an attack, so the claim overstates the immediate blast radius, but the recorded ability is plainly contradicted by the printed text and will misfire as soon as stopAttack is implemented.
verdicts.fixHint: In parseDefensiveEffects, skip stop matches whose clause is negated/prohibitive — e.g. bail when the surrounding clause contains 'cannot be used', 'may not', 'no longer', or when the match is the object of 'cards that ...'. Expected effects: physicalAttack + damageStages 3 only.

verdicts.reason: [spurious-effect] Holds. 'Energy attack doing 5 life cards of damage, OR stops a physical attack' is two mutually exclusive modes; the parse records them as one ability whose effects list contains both energyAttack{lifeCards:5} and stopAttack{physical}, i.e. an unconditional AND. Same root cause as Gohan's Kick: parseDefensiveEffects scans the whole text and line 376 appends the stop as a rider on the attack. This is not merely an engine-vocabulary gap — rules.abilities is already an Ability[] and the schema has both an 'attack' and a 'defense' trigger, so the two modes are expressible; parseAbility just returns a single Ability (verified: 0 of 2764 cards carry more than one ability). Six cards in the corpus use the ', or stops' construction (Blue Arm Blast, Namekian Fist Dodge, Black Knife Hand Strike x2, Black Body Destruction, Blue Round Throw).
verdicts.fixHint: Detect the ', or stops ...' alternation and either (a) have parseAbility return Ability[] with a second {trigger:'defense', effects:[stopAttack]} entry, or (b) conservatively keep only the attack mode and flag the card. Do not leave both effects on one attack ability.

verdicts.reason: [wrong-effect] Holds. Printed text: 'Stops the first PHYSICAL OR ENERGY attack your opponent performs in Combat if your anger level is 3 or higher.' The parse records attackType:'energy', so the drill declines to stop physical attacks — half the printed coverage. Cause is the lazy quantifier in the generic matcher at abilities.ts:233, /stop\w*\s+.{0,40}?(physical|energy)?\s*attack/: the first position where 'attack' can anchor is 'energy attack', so '.{0,40}?' swallows 'the first physical or ' and the capture group takes 'energy'. The at() helper (line 216) already supports 'any', so the correct value is in vocabulary. The claim's comparison is sound — Black Shifting Drill (physical) and Blue Prepared Drill (energy) really are single-type in print. (Side note, not part of this claim: the anger>=3 condition and the 'first ... in Combat' window are also unmodeled here.)
verdicts.fixHint: Add an explicit 'physical or energy' / 'energy or physical' alternation check before the generic matcher in parseDefensiveEffects (or test for both words in the matched clause) and emit attackType:'any'.

verdicts.reason: [wrong-effect] Holds on both counts. (1) parseAttackDamage's second life-card pattern (abilities.ts:203, /([0-9b]+)\s*life\s*cards?\s*(?:draws?|in damage|of damage)/) matches the '+1 life card of damage' bonus and returns lifeCards:1. Per the schema comment (shared/src/abilities.ts:24-27) and the engine (abilities.ts:67 sets attack.damageLifeCards, combat.ts:248-255 short-circuits to life-card damage), a fixed lifeCards OVERRIDES the Physical Attack Table — so this attack deals exactly 1 life card and no table damage. The printed '+1 life card ... FOR EACH Cell Jr.' is a variable additive bonus, not a base. (2) Because dmg.lifeCards is defined, the modifier block at abilities.ts:364 is skipped entirely, so the printed '+2 power stages' is silently lost. Note the pattern does not require the sign, so the '+' that marks it as a modifier is ignored.
verdicts.fixHint: Require the life-card base pattern to be sign-free (reject a preceding '+'/'-') and reject 'for each'/'for every' scaling clauses; then fall through to the damageStages branch so the +2 survives. Expected: physicalAttack (no lifeCards) + damageStages 2, with the per-Cell-Jr. bonus left unmodeled/flagged.

verdicts.reason: [missing-effect] Holds, and it is net-harmful: the parse keeps only the cost. The single recorded effect is discardCards{target:'user', count:1}, so the user pays a card and receives nothing. Traced: pushDiscardCards' self-branch (abilities.ts:307) matches 'discard 1 card from your hand', while pushMoveStage (line 317-319) requires /(all of your personalities|your personality|your mp)[^.]{0,40}highest\s*stage/ — the card says 'your MAIN personality' and 'highest power RATING', so neither the subject nor the noun matches, and pushRaiseOwnPower (line 268) needs 'power rating BY N'. The payoff is squarely in vocabulary: movePowerStage{target:'user', to:'highest'} is emitted verbatim at abilities.ts:319 and the schema defines it at shared/src/abilities.ts:32. The claim's file:line citation checks out (engine abilities.ts:319). Trigger 'onPlay' is also wrong — it fires the discard when the drill hits the table, not once per Combat after dealing 5+ life cards.
verdicts.fixHint: Broaden pushMoveStage to /highest\s*(power\s*)?(stage|rating)/ and allow 'your main personality'; route a 'discard N from your hand to <benefit>' construction into ability.cost.discard rather than an effect (parseCost at abilities.ts:194 currently only handles power-stage costs). Never emit a bare user-discard as the sole effect.

verdicts.reason: [missing-effect] Holds. The stored text contains a clean standalone line 'Gain 3 power stages.' and the parse has no changePowerStages, so the card under-delivers by 3 stages of self-empowerment. This is a parser gap, not a vocabulary gap: changePowerStages{target:'user', delta} is in the schema (shared/src/abilities.ts:31) and is fully executed by the engine (abilities.ts:81-83 -> changeControllerStages, which moves the combat controller's stageIndex and re-syncs the rating). The parser simply has no pattern for 'gain N power stages' — pushSelfPowerLoss (line 264) only matches 'attacker N stages of power' and pushRaiseOwnPower (line 268) only matches 'power rating BY N'. Corpus-wide: 79 cards use the 'gain N power stages' phrasing and ZERO of them produce a changePowerStages effect, so this is a systematic miss. Caveat worth passing on: this record has no textVerified flag and no lackey cross-reference, and the tail is visibly garbled OCR ('and 2 then immediately draw the | same number of cards'); the 'Gain N power stages' phrasing is nonetheless confirmed on verified cards (e.g. CHARGE!: 'Gain 4 power stages').
verdicts.fixHint: Add a pushGainStages rule, e.g. /gain\s+([0-9b]+)\s*(?:power\s*)?stages?/ -> {kind:'changePowerStages', target:'user', delta:N}, and call it from both the attack and non-combat branches (alongside pushSelfPowerLoss at abilities.ts:369). Re-OCR this card to confirm the text before locking it in.

verdicts.reason: [wrong-number] Holds. '1 life card of damage FOR EACH U card in your discard pile, to a maximum of 10 life cards' — the 1 is a per-card rate, not a total, but parseAttackDamage's first pattern (abilities.ts:202, 'doing 1 life card') captures it and line 359 emits energyAttack{lifeCards:1}. The engine then pins the attack at exactly 1 (abilities.ts:72 sets energyLifeCards = 1; combat.ts:248-251 uses it in place of the 4-card default), so a card that scales to 10 always deals 1 — below even the energy default and far from the printed ceiling. The scaling itself is genuinely uncomputable today, which is why committing to a flat number is the wrong call rather than a coverage decision.
verdicts.fixHint: Have parseAttackDamage bail out when the amount is followed by a 'for each'/'for every'/'to a maximum of' clause; emit a bare energyAttack (which already sets needsReview 'energyLifeCards' at abilities.ts:382) or a manual effect instead of a fixed lifeCards. Same guard fixes Cell Jr.'s Flight.

verdicts.reason: Card image confirms the printed text: "Stops a physical attack. Your opponent loses 4 power stages, to a minimum of 0." The second sentence is unconditional and maps exactly onto changePowerStages{target:'foe',delta:-4}, but the parse carries only the stopAttack. Root cause is in the parser, not the vocabulary: the defense branch (packages/engine/src/abilities.ts:393-402) calls only pushAnger/pushRaiseOwnPower/pushDraw, and no helper anywhere matches "your opponent loses N power stages" (pushSelfPowerLoss at :263 only matches "attacker ... stages of power"). Systematic: 12 cards print that wording and 0 of them parsed a changePowerStages effect.
verdicts.fixHint: Add a foe power-loss branch (e.g. /(?:foe|opponent) loses ([0-9b]+) power stages?/ -> changePowerStages{target:'foe',delta:-N}) and call it from the defense branch as well as the attack branch. The "to a minimum of 0" floor is already the engine's clamping behavior.

verdicts.reason: Printed text is "Physical attack doing +6 power stages of damage. Lower your anger 1 level." (Lackey #085 agrees). The attack half is parsed correctly as damageStages 6 (the +N modifier form), but the unconditional self-anger drop is dropped entirely, turning a card with a real cost into pure upside. changeAnger{target:'user',delta:-1} covers it exactly, so this is not a vocabulary gap. Root cause: pushAnger (abilities.ts:247-262) has only two branches — raise-user (:253, requires a "rais/gain" verb) and lower-FOE (:258, requires foe/opponent in the sentence). "Lower your anger" matches neither, so nothing is emitted. 8 cards print "lower your anger N" and only 1 parsed any changeAnger.
verdicts.fixHint: Add a lower-user branch to pushAnger for /low\w*[^.]*your anger/ (and the 2001-era "card user's anger") that emits changeAnger{target:'user',delta:-N}, guarded so it does not double-fire with the existing foe branch.

verdicts.reason: Printed text (Lackey #084 agrees) ends "If successful, raise your opponent's anger 6 levels" — the card's defining drawback — and the parse emits nothing for it with needsReview empty, so the loss leaves no trace. This is not the 'engine lacks vocabulary' case: changeAnger{target:'foe',delta:6} is fully expressible, and pushAnger simply has no raise-FOE branch at all (abilities.ts:258 matches only low/reduc). Proof the gap is the branch and not the success-gate: sibling card Straining Cry Baby Move prints "Raise your opponent's anger 1 level" with NO 'if successful' clause and also parsed to zero anger effects; Majin Buu's Taunt got the target inverted to 'user'. Only the gating is a genuine schema gap — changeAnger has no ifSuccessful flag while damageStages does (and ifSuccessful is already used 83 times in the dataset).
verdicts.fixHint: Add a raise-foe branch to pushAnger emitting changeAnger{target:'foe',delta:+N}. Because the effect is success-gated and would otherwise fire on a stopped attack, either widen ifSuccessful to changeAnger (mirroring damageStages at abilities.ts:29) or, until then, push 'foeAngerIfSuccessful' onto needsReview so the card cannot silently reach 'full' coverage.

verdicts.reason: "Lower your opponent's anger to 0" is a wipe, but the parse encodes changeAnger{target:'foe',delta:0}, which is a literal no-op — the card's main effect resolves as nothing while looking modeled. Root cause is exact: pushAnger:259 does `t.match(/anger[^0-9]{0,10}(\d)/)` , which grabs the "0" out of the phrase "anger to 0" and negates it to -0. Systematic, not a one-off: 12 cards carry changeAnger delta===0, and every one of them prints "lower/reduce ... anger to 0" (Goku's Dashing Punch, Blue Foot Smash, Blue Head Charge, Captain Ginyu Transformed, etc.). The claim's framing is right that the union has no toZero for anger, so encoding delta 0 is worse than not encoding it.
verdicts.fixHint: Detect "anger to 0" before the digit scrape and stop treating it as a delta. Cleanest fix is to add `toZero?: boolean` to changeAnger, mirroring changePowerStages at abilities.ts:31; short of that, emit no changeAnger and flag needsReview. Also worth noting this card's wipe is deferred ("at the end of this Combat"), which the schema cannot express either.

verdicts.reason: WRONG-TRIGGER claim. Card image confirms the print: "Use when entering Combat. Raise your anger 1 level..." The AbilityTrigger union already has 'whenEnteringCombat' (abilities.ts:13) and the CRD makes it a distinct Prepare-Phase step, used once per effect by each player (CRD lines 261 and 267, as cited). The parse says 'onPlay'. Root cause confirmed in source: the Non-Combat branch (abilities.ts:408-421) hardcodes `trigger: 'onPlay'` for every card that reaches it, with no test for the "when entering Combat" phrase anywhere in the parser. Caveat noted but not disqualifying: this record lacks textVerified and its OCR is garbled elsewhere ("Oraw the card"), but the opening clause is legible in both the OCR and the card image.
verdicts.fixHint: In the Non-Combat branch, test the body for /use\s+when\s+entering\s+combat/ and set trigger 'whenEnteringCombat'. Cards that further qualify it ("as the defender"/"as the attacker", common per CRD 1663/1741/2347) have no representation in the union and should go to needsReview.

verdicts.reason: MISSING-EFFECT claim. The card image reads "Raise your Main Personality to his highest power stage." — an unconditional effect with a dedicated kind, movePowerStage{target:'user',to:'highest'} (abilities.ts:32), and the parse omits it. The helper exists but its regex is effectively dead code: pushMoveStage (abilities.ts:317-319) requires the alternation (all of your personalities|your personality|your mp) immediately followed by /highest\s*stage/, so it misses both "your MAIN personality" and the printed noun phrase "highest POWER stage". Measured across the dataset: 42 cards print "to his/her/their highest power stage" and movePowerStage was emitted 0 times in the entire corpus.
verdicts.fixHint: Loosen pushMoveStage to /rais\w*[^.]{0,60}(all of your personalities|your (main )?personality|your mp)[^.]{0,40}highest\s*(power\s*)?stage/. Fixing this one regex should recover all 42 cards. Note this card also drops "Draw the bottom card from your discard pile" (a rejuvenate/draw effect), which is outside this claim.

verdicts.reason: "Piccolo and Nail only." is a hard personality gate and AbilityRestriction.namedOnly is documented for exactly this shape (abilities.ts:64-65, whose doc comment cites the analogous "Villains, Goku, and Gohan only"). The parse has no restriction, so any personality could play it. Root cause: parseRestriction (abilities.ts:158-161) handles only two literals — "heroes only" -> alignment Hero, and a hardcoded villains/goku/gohan pattern — and has no general "<Name> and <Name> only" branch, returning undefined here. Systematic: only 4 cards in the whole corpus carry namedOnly, while a sample of Namekian cards opening with a two-name gate (Blocking Stance, Determination, Dodging Technique, Energy Absorption, Focusing Effort) all parsed with no restriction. The defensive half of this card is parsed correctly.
verdicts.fixHint: Add a general leading-gate branch matching /^([a-z][a-z']+(?:,? and | and |, )[a-z][a-z']+) only\b/ on the pre-strip text, splitting the captured names into namedOnly, and make stripLead (abilities.ts:163) strip the same clause so it does not disturb the attack/defense opener test.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed from the card image (#72): the card actually prints "Physical attack doing +4 power stages of damage." The "4+" in the data is a transcription artifact with the sign transposed (Lackey carries the same artifact). So this is unambiguously the +N MODIFIER form and the correct encoding is damageStages{stages:4} — exactly what the claim expects — yet the parse carries no damage effect at all, leaving a bare PAT result. Root cause pinned: parseAttackDamage:208 requires the digit immediately after "doing" (so "doing 4+" fails), and the modifier matcher at :365 requires sign-BEFORE-digits /([+\-])\s?(\d+)/ (so "4+" fails too). The value falls through both branches and nothing is pushed to needsReview. The claim is right that this is systematic: Red Knee Bash and Saiyan Flying Tackle ("3+") share the artifact, while Namekian Elbow Smash ("+4") and Red Lifting Kick ("+6") parse correctly.
verdicts.fixHint: Extend the modifier regex at abilities.ts:365 to accept the transposed form, e.g. /(?:([+\-])\s?(\d+)|(\d+)\s?([+\-]))[\s|\\]*(?:power\s*)?stages?\s*of\s*damage/, and add a fallback that flags needsReview when an attack card mentions "stages of damage" but no damage effect was emitted — that guard would have caught all three cards.

verdicts.reason: Same defect as Orange Uppercut and confirmed the same way: the card image (#75) prints "Physical attack doing +4 power stages of damage. If you declared Tokui-Waza, raise your anger 1 level." The parse keeps the anger rider but carries no damage effect, so the card resolves as a vanilla PAT attack and loses its primary effect. Same root cause — the "4+" transposed sign matches neither the fixed-base branch (abilities.ts:208) nor the +N modifier branch (:365), and nothing is flagged. Independent of the claim, note the retained changeAnger{user,+1} is itself encoded unconditionally even though the printed rider is gated on "If you declared Tokui-Waza"; that is a separate issue and not what was claimed here.
verdicts.fixHint: Fixed by the same regex change as tts-49d99703-2 — accept the transposed "N+" form in the modifier matcher and add a needsReview guard when an attack names damage but no damage effect is emitted.

verdicts.reason: Card image (#39) confirms a Physical Combat ATTACK card: "Sensei Deck. Physical attack doing +3 life cards of damage. If you declared a Tokui-Waza and your opponent has used a Combat card earlier this Combat, your opponent cannot play Combat cards that do not stop attacks until the end of your next turn." The parse is trigger 'defense' with stopAttack{attackType:'any'} and no attack effect whatsoever — it both grants a power the card does not have (stopping any attack) and omits the attack it must perform. Root cause is two-fold and confirmed in source: the attack-opener test (abilities.ts:343) anchors on /^(a\s+)?phys\w*\s+attack/, and the "Sensei Deck." prefix is not removed by stripLead/stripTypePlate, so startsPhysical is false; the card then falls into the defense branch because parseDefensiveEffects:233 /stop\w*\s+.{0,40}?(physical|energy)?\s*attack/ fires on the restriction clause "cards that do not stop attacks". Corroborated: the other Sensei-prefixed attacks (Black Chained Strike, Heroic Force, Heroic Shoulder Slam, Heroic Final Strike) also parsed with no attack effect.
verdicts.fixHint: Strip a leading "Sensei Deck." (and similar deck-source prefixes) before the opener test, and negate the stop matcher when the phrase is preceded by "do not"/"cannot"/"that do not" so a restriction clause cannot manufacture a stopAttack. The '+3 life cards' rider has no Effect kind — leave it out and flag it rather than writing it into lifeCards (see Black Backstab).

verdicts.reason: The card prints a plain "Energy attack" with no fixed damage (Lackey Preview 3 agrees); the '1' was scraped from the conditional per-Drill rider "+1 Life Card of damage for each Blue Style Drill". That the field is an override, not a bonus, is confirmed in the engine itself, not just the doc comment: packages/engine/src/abilities.ts:72 does `attack.energyLifeCards = e.lifeCards ?? 4`, so lifeCards:1 replaces the CRD default of 4 (CRD line 449). The card is silently downgraded to a quarter of its damage. Root cause: parseAttackDamage's second alternative (:203) matches /([0-9b]+)\s*life\s*cards?\s*of damage/ anywhere in the text, ignoring both the preceding '+' and the fact that the clause sits inside an "If ... is in play" conditional. Aggravating: because dmg.lifeCards came back defined, the 'energyLifeCards' needsReview flag at :382 was suppressed — the wrong value silenced the guard that existed to catch exactly this.
verdicts.fixHint: Anchor the life-card matcher to the attack's own opening clause and require the number not be preceded by a sign; do not scan text after "if"/"for each". Emit {kind:'energyAttack'} with no lifeCards here so the default 4 applies, and leave the conditional per-Drill scaling unmodeled.

verdicts.reason: "Physical attack doing +2 life cards of damage" is a modifier ON TOP of the Physical Attack Table result, but the parse writes physicalAttack{lifeCards:2}, which the engine treats as a fixed base: packages/engine/src/abilities.ts:67 does `if (e.lifeCards !== undefined) attack.damageLifeCards = e.lifeCards`, replacing the PAT power-stage damage with a flat 2 life cards. So the parse resolves materially wrong, usually undercutting the attack. This is not merely 'the engine lacks vocabulary' — the objection is that a missing modifier kind was papered over by writing a wrong base. Root cause is the same sign-blind alternative at parseAttackDamage:203. Systematic across the '+N life cards' wording: Goku's Right Knee Smash (+2 -> lifeCards 2), Saiyan Face Stomp, Saiyan Left Kick, Tiens Flight all show the same promotion.
verdicts.fixHint: Require the fixed-base life-card match to have no leading '+'/'-' (the power-stage branch at :208 already does this correctly — mirror it). Then emit {kind:'physicalAttack'} with no lifeCards and push something like 'lifeCardModifier' onto needsReview; a proper fix adds a damageLifeCards modifier kind alongside damageStages at abilities.ts:29.

verdicts.reason: Printed text has three independent clauses; the middle one, 'Gain 4 power stages.', is a standalone immediate effect on the user and is absent from the parse. changePowerStages{target,delta} is existing vocabulary that expresses it exactly, and needsReview is empty, so the effect was dropped silently rather than deferred. Confirmed against the card record: effects are only [physicalAttack, damageStages 4].
verdicts.fixHint: Recognize the standalone sentence 'Gain N power stages.' as {kind:'changePowerStages', target:'user', delta:N} and append it after the attack effects. Note this is distinct from 'doing +N power stages of damage' (a damageStages modifier) — the parser is currently consuming the damage clause and discarding the rest of the sentence chain.

verdicts.reason: 'Raise your Main Personality to his highest power stage.' is a separate sentence and a modelable immediate effect; movePowerStage{target:'user', to:'highest'} is precisely the vocabulary for it. Parse contains only [physicalAttack, damageStages 2]. needsReview lists only 'type', so the omission is unflagged.
verdicts.fixHint: Add a pattern for 'raise your Main Personality to his highest power stage' -> {kind:'movePowerStage', target:'user', to:'highest'}. The mirror phrasing 'lower ... to his lowest power stage' should map to to:'lowest'.

verdicts.reason: Text has four clauses; the third, 'Your opponent must skip his next "Attacker Attacks" phase.', maps one-to-one onto the parameterless stunSkipNextPhase effect kind. The parse stops after the first two clauses (stopAttack, changeAnger foe -1) and does not flag the omission. This is a dropped modelable effect, not a vocabulary gap.
verdicts.fixHint: Add a phrase rule for 'must skip his next "Attacker Attacks" phase' -> {kind:'stunSkipNextPhase'}. The parser appears to stop consuming clauses after the second sentence on defense-trigger cards; check that the clause loop runs to the end of the text.

verdicts.reason: Both halves of this claim fail. (a) The ifSuccessful:true on damageStages is not a defect: CRD battle-sequence steps 8-13 place all Base Damage calculation and damage dealing strictly after the attack is deemed successful, so a stopped attack deals no +5 stages either way. Flagging it true is harmless and arguably more correct than the alternative. (b) The changeAnger gate is unexpressible: the Effect union gives ifSuccessful only to damageStages, not to changeAnger. The claim itself concedes this. The only genuine fix is extending the type, which is a known vocabulary gap and out of scope for a parse audit. The fallback suggestion 'omit it' would be worse — it would silently delete a real printed effect.
verdicts.fixHint: No parser change warranted. If the team later wants step-15 fidelity, add an optional ifSuccessful?: boolean to changeAnger (and other secondary effects) in abilities.ts — a type change, not a parse fix. Separately, the parser's ifSuccessful flag on damageStages is inconsistent across cards (set here and on tts-c611d949-32, unset on tts-2b332fa4-14 and tts-89fe8da5-18 for identical '+N power stages of damage' phrasing), which is worth normalizing for tidiness but changes no engine behavior.

verdicts.reason: This reduces entirely to the missing-vocabulary gap. changeAnger in abilities.ts is {kind, target, delta} with no ifSuccessful field, so the parser has no way to encode 'If successful, raise your anger 2 levels.' Everything the parser could get right, it did: target 'user' is correct per the anger rule ('raise your anger' = the card user), delta +2 is correct, and lifeCards:5 correctly overrides the 4-card default per CRD step 9. The suggested fallback of omitting the effect would lose a real printed effect and make the parse strictly worse.
verdicts.fixHint: No parse fix available. Would require adding ifSuccessful?: boolean to the changeAnger variant (and a corresponding engine step-15 hook). The card's other unmodeled clause — 'your opponent cannot use Endurance against your Red Style attacks' for the remainder of Combat — is likewise a vocabulary gap.

verdicts.reason: The printed base is a bare 'Focused energy attack.' with no stated amount. CRD step 9 is explicit: 'If an energy attack does not state the amount of damage it does, the Base Damage is 4 life cards', and step 10 adds modifiers separately. The '+1 life cards ... for each card' clause is a step-10 modifier, and 'Focused' is only a stop-resistance keyword (CRD line 1160), not a damage statement. Per the comment on abilities.ts line 26, setting lifeCards:1 OVERRIDES the default, so the engine deals 1 life card where the card deals 4 plus the per-card bonus. The printed text plainly contradicts the parse.
verdicts.fixHint: Require the damage-amount extractor to reject clauses whose number carries a leading '+' or a 'for each' multiplier before writing lifeCards/powerStages. Emit {kind:'energyAttack'} with no lifeCards field and push the variable bonus to needsReview. Same regex bug as tts-434ce590-24.

verdicts.reason: Same modifier-as-base confusion, and here the '+' sits directly in the attack clause: 'Focused energy attack doing +1 life cards of damage for each card ...'. Both the '+' sign and the 'for each' quantifier mark it as a step-10 modifier, not a stated Base Damage under CRD step 9. The parse's lifeCards:1 replaces the 4-card default, understating damage by 4x before the per-card bonus is even counted. The restriction {alignment:'Hero'} and the focusedAttack needsReview flag are both correct; only the damage base is wrong.
verdicts.fixHint: Same fix as tts-434ce590-35: the 'doing N life cards of damage' capture must not fire when the number is signed (+N/-N) or followed by 'for each'. Signed values belong in a modifier effect (or needsReview), never in the energyAttack lifeCards field.

verdicts.reason: Wrong-number claim. Scanning the full text, the only opponent-anger clause is 'Lower your opponent's anger 3 levels.' Nothing on the card lowers the foe's anger by 1, yet the parse emits changeAnger{target:'foe', delta:-1}. The card also has 'Raise your anger 1 level' immediately before it, which is the likely source of the stray 1 — the parser took the target from one clause and the magnitude from its neighbor. CRD line 1102 confirms these clauses are live by default: an Empower only deletes following text if the player declares it, so an undeclared CHARGE! resolves every clause as printed.
verdicts.fixHint: Bind the magnitude and the target within a single clause span. The 'Empower N.' sentences appear to be breaking clause segmentation and letting a number leak across the boundary — treat 'Empower N.' as its own token that terminates the preceding clause rather than as a number source. Correct value: {kind:'changeAnger', target:'foe', delta:-3}.

verdicts.reason: Missing-effect claim, and independent of the wrong-number one. 'Raise your anger 1 level.' targets the user per the anger convention, and changeAnger with target:'user' is in the vocabulary — the parser uses that exact shape on tts-e3673ab6-8. The parse has no user-targeted anger effect at all. It is not a deliberate Empower-related exclusion: the parser did model the other Empower-preceded clauses (damageStages 3 under Empower 5, the foe anger under Empower 2), and CRD line 1102 confirms all clauses resolve when no Empower is declared. needsReview is empty, so the drop is silent.
verdicts.fixHint: Add {kind:'changeAnger', target:'user', delta:1}. Likely the same clause-segmentation bug as the sibling claim — this clause was consumed as the delta source for the foe-anger effect instead of emitting its own. Note 'Gain 4 power stages.' (Empower 4) is also dropped on this card and is equally modelable via changePowerStages, though not claimed here.

verdicts.reason: The alternate defensive mode reads 'stops a physical or energy attack' and the parse encodes attackType:'energy'. attackType accepts 'any' in the union, so this is a plain narrowing that contradicts printed text — the engine would refuse the card against a physical attack, losing half its function. Judging only the attackType error as the claim scopes it: the unmodeled below-500,000 condition is a separate vocabulary gap and I am not counting it, and the mode-choice (attack OR defend) is likewise not expressible.
verdicts.fixHint: Fix the 'physical or energy' disjunction handler to emit attackType:'any' — it is currently keeping only the last-mentioned type. Same root cause as tts-89fe8da5-8 and tts-18cbdeb1-19. Consider also flagging the unmodeled power-rating condition in needsReview so the engine does not offer the stop mode unconditionally.

verdicts.reason: Text reads 'Stops a physical or energy attack.' and the parse restricts attackType to 'energy'. 'any' is available in the AttackKind | 'any' union, so this is a plainly wrong value, not a gap: the engine will not let the card stop a physical attack, which is half its printed defensive function. Nothing on the card narrows the stop to energy, and needsReview is empty.
verdicts.fixHint: Same disjunction bug: 'a physical or energy attack' must map to attackType:'any', not to whichever type the regex matched last. A single shared phrase rule fixes this card, tts-2b332fa4-25, and tts-18cbdeb1-19.

verdicts.reason: Primary clause is 'Stops a physical or energy attack.' but the parse emits attackType:'energy', so the engine cannot use the card against a physical attack. Plain contradiction with printed text, with 'any' available in the union. I am counting only the primary stop, as the claim scopes it — the floating remainder-of-Combat conditional stop is a genuine vocabulary gap and is excluded from this verdict. Worth noting for the fix: per CRD line 1160, a card that stops both types cannot stop a Focused attack, so correcting this to 'any' also makes the card correctly subject to the Focused rule once that is modeled.
verdicts.fixHint: Same 'physical or energy' -> attackType:'any' fix. Once cards correctly carry attackType:'any', the engine's Focused handling (CRD line 1164) becomes relevant: such cards may still be played for their secondary effects but must not stop a Focused attack.

verdicts.reason: Text plainly reads "Take two cards from your discard pile and put them at the bottom of your life card deck" and the parse emits only stopAttack + removeFromGameAfterUse. This is the textbook rejuvenate pattern, and the parser emits rejuvenate 31 times elsewhere in this same dataset — including from:'choose' for near-identical wording (Gohan's Peaceful Stance: "Choose 3 cards from your discard pile" -> {rejuvenate, count:3, from:'choose'}). Not a vocabulary gap; a dropped modeled effect. needsReview is empty, so nothing flags the loss.
verdicts.fixHint: Add {kind:'rejuvenate', count:2, from:'choose'} to the defense ability. The clause-splitter appears to stop after the first sentence on cards whose OCR header is garbled (this card's text begins 'rexs7ch 33 = rQ — Stops an energy attack.'); check whether a leading-noise line is truncating downstream sentence extraction.

verdicts.reason: Text: "Take any 2 cards from your discard pile and place them at the bottom of your life deck." Parse keeps changeAnger +2 and removeFromGameAfterUse but drops the rejuvenation. Same modeled-vocabulary miss as tts-4caf6df6-24; 'take any N ... bottom of your life deck' is exactly {rejuvenate, from:'choose'}, a form the parser already produces elsewhere. textVerified is true, so the source text is not in doubt.
verdicts.fixHint: Add {kind:'rejuvenate', count:2, from:'choose'}. Extend the rejuvenate matcher beyond 'place the bottom/top N cards' to cover 'take any N cards from your discard pile' -> from:'choose'; it already handles 'choose N cards'.

verdicts.reason: This is a Drill (Non-Combat, 'Drill' in title) whose text is 'Lower your opponent's anger 1 level AFTER EVERY successful energy attack against your opponent.' Parsed as trigger 'onPlay', which makes the engine apply -1 foe anger once, at the moment the Drill enters play, and never again — contradicting both the timing (after an attack resolves) and the repetition (every one). CRD line 636 states Drills 'are constantly in use ... and may even create effects multiple times within a turn', and AbilityTrigger defines 'constant' as 'Drills / continuous'. The value exists and was not used; 'constant' has 0 occurrences dataset-wide while 19 Drill cards were flattened to onPlay, so this is a systematic trigger bug, not a one-off.
verdicts.fixHint: Route cards of type Non-Combat whose title contains 'Drill' (and/or whose text has a recurring-condition clause like 'after every ... attack') to trigger:'constant' instead of onPlay. Note that 'constant' alone still does not encode the 'after a successful energy attack' condition — pair it with needsReview (e.g. 'trigger:conditional') so the unconditional payout is not silently trusted.

verdicts.reason: Same class as the Frieza Drill but with a worse payout error. Text gates the anger on a compound condition — 'when you successfully do a physical AND energy attack in the same combat', 'Once per combat' — and the parse is trigger:'onPlay' + changeAnger user +1, i.e. a free, immediate, unconditional +1 anger on play. The printed condition is plainly contradicted, and 'constant' is the defined trigger for Drills (CRD line 636). Rejecting this as 'the engine lacks conditional vocabulary' would not excuse it: the wrong trigger alone converts a hard-to-meet payoff into an automatic one.
verdicts.fixHint: Set trigger:'constant' and do NOT emit a bare changeAnger — either gate it behind a modeled condition or downgrade to {kind:'manual', note:'+1 anger on physical+energy both successful, once per combat'} with needsReview, so the engine does not hand out free anger.

verdicts.reason: 'Reduce opponent's anger to 0' is a set-to-zero; changeAnger with delta 0 adds nothing, so the engine's foe anger is unchanged. The parse looks modeled but is a no-op, which is worse than an honest gap because coverage reads 'partial' with needsReview empty. Confirmed systematic: 12 cards with 'anger to 0' text carry changeAnger delta:0 (Goku's Dashing Punch, Blue Head Charge, Yamcha's Right Cross, Frieza's Finger Tip Energy Blast, and others), and one (Goku's Heart Disease) even has the target inverted to 'user'. changePowerStages has a toZero flag; changeAnger has none.
verdicts.fixHint: Add a toZero?: boolean to the changeAnger variant mirroring changePowerStages, and have the 'to 0'/'set ... to 0' matcher emit {changeAnger, target:'foe', toZero:true}. Until that lands, emit {kind:'manual'} + needsReview rather than delta:0. Fix all 12 delta:0 sites, not just this card. (Separately, the 'costing 1 life card to use' cost is unmodeled — AbilityCost has only powerStages/discard — but that is a real vocabulary gap and outside this claim.)

verdicts.reason: The effect KIND is right — '+1 power stages' is a modifier, so damageStages is correct, not a fixed base — but the magnitude is not a constant. 'for each Non-Combat card in your discard pile' makes it a count-scaled modifier, and stages:1 is correct only when the discard pile holds exactly one Non-Combat card; it also wrongly fires for +1 with an empty discard pile. This is not merely 'the engine lacks vocabulary': the parser has bail-out machinery it declined to use here — Majin Babidi's scaled damage got needsReview:['ability:energyLifeCards'], while this card has needsReview:[] and presents a bogus number as verified.
verdicts.fixHint: Either add a scaled modifier (e.g. damageStages gaining a perCard source) or, minimally, drop the fixed stages:1 in favour of {kind:'manual'} plus needsReview:['ability:scaledDamage'] whenever a 'for each' clause follows a damage number. This is broad: the same flattening hits Blue Windup Blast, Cell Jr.'s Flight, and Gohan's Kamehameha.

verdicts.reason: Text says 'Stops the FIRST physical attack in the NEXT combat'; the parse uses window:'thisAttack', documented in abilities.ts as 'the current one'. That is the wrong end of the timeline — the card is a Non-Combat placed before the combat it affects and explicitly does not apply to the current one, and it stops a mandated first attack rather than one the player picks. The parser demonstrably has and uses a forward-looking window (Saiyan Energy Aura / Saiyan Sweeping Defense, 'in the next phase' -> nextPhase), so this is its own convention applied inconsistently, not a vocabulary ceiling. Weaker half of the claim: the trigger. 'defense' is defensible since the stop resolves when the foe attacks, and CRD line 632 says Non-Combat/Non-Drill cards are placed in the Non-Combat Step but used in the Combat Step — I would not change the trigger on this evidence. The window is the load-bearing defect.
verdicts.fixHint: Change window to 'nextPhase' (closest modeled value) and leave trigger:'defense'. Teach the window matcher that 'in the next combat' is forward-looking, same as 'in the next phase'; today only the latter is recognised. Add needsReview since 'first attack in the next combat' is still not exactly 'foe's next phase'. Recoome Boom (tts-7b6b6ee0-7) has the same 'next combat' -> thisAttack miss.

verdicts.reason: The strongest claim in the batch — the printed text, the CRD, and the abilities.ts comment all use the same words. Card: 'Stops the first UNSTOPPED physical attack performed against you during Combat.' abilities.ts: "firstSuccessful = the first that gets through." CRD line 2519: 'Defense Shields attempt to stop the first unstopped attack', and battle-sequence step 7 fires shields only 'If the attack was not stopped'. window:'thisAttack' instead lets the shield be spent reactively on any physical attack, including one another card already stopped. 'firstSuccessful' has 0 occurrences dataset-wide despite 27 Defense Shield cards, so the value was defined and never wired up.
verdicts.fixHint: Emit {kind:'stopAttack', attackType:'physical', window:'firstSuccessful'}. Gate on the literal 'Defense Shield:' prefix and/or 'first unstopped' and apply across all 27 Defense Shield cards (Black Shifting Drill, Blue Prepared Drill, Orange Steady Drill, Namekian Ready Drill, etc.). Note Super Saiyan Trunks stops the first TWO unstopped physical attacks — firstSuccessful has no count, so flag that one for review.

verdicts.reason: Text: 'If successful it does no damage.' The parse is a bare physicalAttack, which per abilities.ts falls through to the Physical Attack Table default — so the engine deals full PAT power stages on a card that deals none. abilities.ts states powerStages, when set, OVERRIDES the default, so powerStages:0 expresses this exactly, and CRD step 8 confirms 'an attack is considered successful even if it deals no damage', so a zero-damage attack still reaches its riders. The 'If successful' qualifier does not rescue the parse: an unsuccessful attack deals no damage either way, so 0 is correct in both branches. This is the only card in the dataset with 'no damage' text and it got no special handling.
verdicts.fixHint: Emit {kind:'physicalAttack', powerStages:0}. Add a matcher for 'does no damage' / 'it does no damage' that pins the base to 0 rather than leaving it undefined. The drill-discard payload stays unmodeled — discardCards is hand-only per its comment — so keep a needsReview note for that half.

verdicts.reason: Claim 1 of 2 on this card (wrong-number, anger delta). Printed text is 'Raise your anger and power stages by 2' and the parse emits delta:1 — half the printed value, with no source anywhere on the card for a 1. Both the stored text and textOriginal agree, and the vision record is confidence:'high' with a note stating explicitly that the wording is 'by 2'. The number is plainly contradicted.
verdicts.fixHint: Emit {kind:'changeAnger', target:'user', delta:2}. The bug looks like the anger matcher defaulting to 1 when the numeral trails a conjoined object ('anger AND power stages by 2') instead of following the 'anger N levels' shape — parse the shared trailing quantifier.

verdicts.reason: Claim 2 of 2 on this card (missing-effect, power stages). The same sentence raises power stages by 2 and the parse contains no changePowerStages at all — only stopAttack and the (also wrong) anger change. changePowerStages {target, delta} is modeled vocabulary, so this is a catchable omission rather than a gap, and needsReview lists only 'type', flagging nothing about the dropped effect.
verdicts.fixHint: Add {kind:'changePowerStages', target:'user', delta:2} alongside the corrected anger effect. Same root cause as the delta bug: the conjoined-object sentence 'raise your X and Y by N' is being reduced to a single effect on the first noun. Worth a targeted sweep for other 'anger and power stages' cards.

verdicts.reason: abilities.ts is explicit that a set lifeCards OVERRIDES the base damage default, so {physicalAttack, lifeCards:3} tells the engine this attack deals 3 life cards INSTEAD of its Physical Attack Table damage. The card says 'Physical attack. If successful it ALSO does 3 life cards of damage' — PAT damage plus a rider. The parse therefore deletes the card's actual physical damage. The claim correctly anticipates the vocabulary objection: since there is no additive life-card effect, the right move is to keep the PAT base and note the rider, not to substitute an override that removes real damage. Systematic — the same additive-to-override conversion hits Cell's Choke Hold, Super Android 13's Ridge Hand, and is worse on energy attacks (Gohan's Kamehameha: '+1 life cards' -> lifeCards:1, overriding the default of 4 and cutting damage by 75%).
verdicts.fixHint: Drop lifeCards from the physicalAttack so the PAT base survives, and add {kind:'manual', note:'also does 3 life cards if successful'} plus needsReview. Longer term the real fix is a damageLifeCards additive effect mirroring damageStages (with ifSuccessful), since '+N life cards' currently has no correct representation; until then the parser must never map 'also'/'+N life cards' onto the override field.

verdicts.reason: Text reads 'Stops an energy [attack] during your next ... Attacker Attacks phase' — names ENERGY and a later window. Parse emits attackType:'any', window:'thisAttack', wrong on both axes, turning a delayed single-type stop into a free instant catch-all defense. Decisive: the parser already handles this exact pattern correctly elsewhere — Saiyan Energy Aura (tts-8cbb81b5-25, tts-a42f5098-25) 'stops energy attacks in the next phase' parses to {attackType:'energy', window:'nextPhase'}, and Saiyan Sweeping Defense does the physical equivalent. So this is a regression on a supported pattern, not a vocabulary gap. CRD lines 2179/2182 confirm the delayed-phase stop is a real distinct mechanic.
verdicts.fixHint: The 'stops an <type> attack during your next Attacker Attacks phase' branch that fires for Saiyan Energy Aura is not matching here because the OCR text is garbled ('Stops an energy | during your next 4, Attacker Attacks" phase'). The type token 'energy' and the phrase 'next ... Attacker Attacks phase' are both intact; loosen the matcher to key off '(stops a|stops an) (energy|physical)' plus a 'next ... phase' lookahead tolerant of interposed OCR junk, rather than requiring the literal 'attack' noun and a contiguous 'in the next phase'. Falling back to attackType:'any'/window:'thisAttack' when the type/window tokens ARE present is the worst outcome — default to needsReview instead of the permissive values.

verdicts.reason: Spurious. The card contains no anger adjustment at all. The clause is a triggered replacement effect ('When a card effect is lowering your opponent's anger while his anger is at 0, he discards 1 life card for each level of anger that remains to be lowered'), which describes what happens when SOME OTHER card lowers anger. The parser keyed on the substring "lowering your opponent's anger" and emitted {changeAnger, target:'foe', delta:0}. delta:0 is a no-op that does nothing useful while miscategorizing a damage Drill as an anger-manipulation card; the 'onPlay' trigger also implies a one-shot fire on entry that the text never describes. The confirmed original wording ('When you lower your opponent's anger but his anger level is 0...') is likewise a trigger, not an effect.
verdicts.fixHint: The anger matcher is firing inside a 'When ...' / 'When a card effect is ...' subordinate trigger clause. Gate anger extraction so it only runs on imperative main clauses ('Raise your anger', 'Lower your opponent's anger') and bails on any clause introduced by When/If/Whenever describing a condition. Separately, never emit a changeAnger with delta:0 — a zero delta means the magnitude was not recovered, which should route to manual/needsReview instead of a no-op effect.

verdicts.reason: Missing effect. Printed text has two distinct stops: 'Stops an energy attack.' AND 'Stops all of your opponent's energy attacks for the remainder of Combat.' Only the first was parsed. The second is the card's headline ability and the reason it is a remove-from-game promo; without it the parse reduces a combat-locking shield to an ordinary one-shot energy stop. The vocabulary represents this exactly: window:'thisCombat' with scope:'all' are both defined in abilities.ts, so this is a dropped modelable effect rather than a vocabulary gap.
verdicts.fixHint: window:'thisCombat' is emitted zero times across all 2764 cards, so the 'for the remainder of Combat' / 'for the rest of Combat' branch appears to be entirely unimplemented. Add a matcher for 'stops all of your opponent's <type> attacks for the remainder of Combat' -> {stopAttack, attackType, window:'thisCombat', scope:'all'}. Also make the stop extractor emit one effect per sentence rather than stopping after the first match, since this card legitimately carries two.

verdicts.reason: Wrong number. The printed bonus is '+1 power stages of damage FOR EACH power stage your opponent's Main Personality is above 0' — a per-stage multiplier that can reach 10+ stages — and it is gated on 'If performed by Krillin', together with a Non-Combat discard. The parse flattens all of that to an unconditional damageStages:1, which simultaneously understates the bonus for Krillin (by up to an order of magnitude) and grants a phantom +1 to every non-Krillin personality who plays the card. Both the multiplier and the gate are plainly in the text and plainly absent from the parse.
verdicts.fixHint: The damageStages matcher is grabbing the literal '+1' and discarding the trailing 'for each ...' quantifier. Make any '+N ... for each <X>' construction disqualify the fixed-number path and route to manual/needsReview, since a scaling bonus has no representation in the Effect union. Same for the 'If performed by <Name>' prefix — it should either produce a restriction or suppress the gated effects entirely. Note the ability already carries needsReview:['energyLifeCards'], so the review channel exists; this bonus should be added to it.

verdicts.reason: Spurious. The discard is explicitly conditional: 'If Namek Dragon Ball 4 is in play, your opponent must discard 2 cards from his hand.' The parse emits {discardCards, target:'foe', count:2} with no gate, so the engine strips two cards from the opponent's hand on every use regardless of board state — a significant unearned swing on a common attack. This is not a vocabulary-gap complaint: the correct conservative behavior is to omit the effect and flag it, which the parser already does for other unrepresentable conditions. Note the rest of this parse is fine — Endurance 3 was correctly split into its own field and not folded into the attack, and '+3 power stages' correctly became a damageStages modifier rather than a fixed base.
verdicts.fixHint: Add a guard that drops (or routes to needsReview) any effect extracted from a clause whose subject is a board-state condition — 'If <card name> is in play', 'If you have ... in play'. There is no conditional wrapper in the Effect union, so emitting the consequent unconditionally is strictly worse than emitting nothing.

verdicts.reason: Spurious, and the worst of the gating cases. Both riders are printed Kogu-only: 'If used by Kogu, this card can stop a physical attack instead' and 'If used by Kogu, your opponent discards a card from his hand.' The parse applies both to any user. Worse, the word 'instead' means the stop REPLACES the attack, but the parse emits physicalAttack and stopAttack in the same effects array, so the engine would both attack and stop — a mode the card never permits for anyone. Any personality can therefore use this attack card as a physical-attack stopper and mill a card every time.
verdicts.fixHint: Two separate fixes. (1) 'If used by <Name>' must gate or suppress its consequents, same as the Namek Dragon Ball case. (2) The 'can ... instead' construction signals mutually exclusive modes; the Effect union has no alternation, so a stop introduced by 'instead' should never be appended alongside the attack it replaces. Also worth checking the unrelated damageStages:4 on this card, which carries ifSuccessful:true — the 'If successful' clause here governs the Ally search, not the '+4 power stages' in the opening sentence, so that flag looks misattributed too (outside this claim's scope).

verdicts.reason: Spurious. The rejuvenation is printed as 'If used by a Fused Personality, place this card and the bottom card of your discard pile at the bottom of your Life Deck after use', yet {rejuvenate, count:1, from:'bottom'} is emitted unconditionally, so any personality recycles a discard-pile card. The cited precedent checks out and makes this an internal inconsistency rather than a judgment call: Vegito's Uppercut (tts-2b332fa4-30) has the same 'If used by a Fused Personality, ... gain 3 power stages, and place this card at the bottom of your Life Deck after use' clause and the parser dropped ALL of its Fused-gated consequents — no changePowerStages, no rejuvenate. Two cards in the same set, same clause type, opposite handling.
verdicts.fixHint: Same root cause as the Kogu and Namek cases: 'If used by <a Fused Personality|Name>' consequents are being hoisted out of their conditional on some cards and dropped on others. Unify the handling — suppress plus needsReview is the behavior already demonstrated on Vegito's Uppercut and is the safe default.

verdicts.reason: Missing effect. 'Your attacks do +2 power stages of damage' is an unconditional continuous bonus and is the Drill's entire offensive purpose, but the parse carries no damageStages at all (its only effect is the bogus changeAnger from the other claim). Every attack the user makes resolves 2 stages light. Both halves of the representation exist in abilities.ts — the 'constant' trigger is documented as 'Drills / continuous' and damageStages is documented as a '+/- modifier on PAT' — so this is a dropped modelable effect, not missing vocabulary. Distinct from the Underdog Drill case because this clause carries no condition.
verdicts.fixHint: Constant-trigger damageStages is emitted zero times across all 2764 cards while 22 cards print 'Your attacks do +N power stages of damage', so the Drill continuous-bonus branch looks entirely unimplemented — one parser fix would clear the whole class. Add: sentence matching /your attacks do \+(\d+) power stages of damage/ on a Non-Combat/Drill -> ability {trigger:'constant', effects:[{kind:'damageStages', stages:N}]}. Also note this card's sole ability is currently trigger:'onPlay', which is wrong for a Drill regardless.

verdicts.reason: Missing restriction. The text opens 'Bojack only.' and the parse carries no restriction object, so the engine lets any personality play a card printed for one named personality. AbilityRestriction.namedOnly exists for exactly this, and the parser demonstrably uses it — Recoome Boom, Saiyan Rapid Deflection and Saiyan Training all carry namedOnly:['Villains','Goku','Gohan'] — so the capability is live and this is a drop on a card the parser should have caught. 26 abilities dataset-wide carry a restriction, only 4 of them namedOnly, which suggests the simple '<Name> only.' form is under-matched relative to the compound 'Villains, Goku, and Gohan only' form.
verdicts.fixHint: The namedOnly matcher appears tuned to the multi-name list form. Add the single-name leading form: /^([A-Z][\w' ]+) only\./ -> restriction:{namedOnly:[name]}. Guard against swallowing archetype phrases that are not personality names ('Saiyan Heritage only', 'Fused Personality only') — those need their own handling and should not be shoved into namedOnly.

verdicts.reason: Spurious. The entire card body sits behind 'If your Main Personality's highest power rating is below 500,000, then ...' and the parse emits {preventLifeCards, amount:2, attackType:'any'} with the condition stripped. The engine grants a permanent 2-life-card shield against every incoming attack for the whole game. This is not a marginal over-application: an MP's highest power rating exceeds 500,000 for most of the roster past the early sagas, so the ungated parse is wrong in the majority of real board states, and it is wrong in the player's favor. The condition is plainly printed and plainly absent from the parse.
verdicts.fixHint: Same conditional-hoisting bug as the other spurious-effect findings, but on a leading 'If <numeric threshold>, then ...' clause rather than an 'If used by X'. The Effect union has no conditional wrapper and no power-rating predicate, so the consequents should be suppressed with a needsReview marker (e.g. 'powerRatingCondition') rather than emitted bare. Whatever guard is added should cover the trailing conjunct too, since 'and all your attacks do +1 power stages' is governed by the same 'If'.

verdicts.reason: Not independently real, and the proposed fix would be a regression. The claim describes '+1 power stages of damage' as a 'second continuous clause', but it is not continuous — it sits inside the same conditional as the prevention ('If your Main Personality's highest power rating is below 500,000, then prevent 2 life cards ... AND all your attacks do +1 power stages of damage'). The expected remedy is to add {damageStages, stages:1} under a 'constant' trigger with no gate, which would introduce exactly the ungated-conditional defect the sibling claim against this same card correctly flags. Omitting an unrepresentable conditional clause is the conservative-correct behavior, so the absence is defensible rather than a defect, and the underlying issue (the power-rating condition is unmodeled) is already fully covered by the spurious-effect claim on this card. Filing it twice double-counts one root cause. Contrast the Blue Biting Drill and Black Groveling Drill claims, which I did confirm — those '+2 power stages' clauses carry no condition, so adding them unconditionally is correct there.
verdicts.fixHint: No parser change should be made for this claim in isolation. When the power-rating condition is addressed (per the spurious-effect finding on this card), both consequents should be handled together — either both suppressed with a shared needsReview marker, or both emitted only once a conditional representation exists in the Effect union. Adding the damageStages alone, ungated, would make the card strictly worse.

verdicts.reason: Missing effect. The card prints two unconditional continuous clauses — 'Your attacks do +2 power stages of damage.' and 'Prevent 2 life cards of damage from your opponent's attacks.' — and only the prevention was parsed, so every attack the user makes resolves 2 stages light. Neither clause carries a condition (confirmed against the errata text and the recorded textOriginal), so unlike the Underdog Drill case the effect can be added as-is with no gating question. damageStages plus the 'constant' trigger cover it exactly, so this is a dropped modelable effect.
verdicts.fixHint: Same single root cause as the Blue Biting Drill missing-effect finding — the 'Your attacks do +N power stages of damage' branch is unimplemented across the dataset. One matcher fixes both cards and the ~20 others carrying the clause. Secondary: this card's ability is trigger:'defense'; a Drill's continuous prevention is better modeled under 'constant', and the two clauses should live on one constant ability rather than the damage bonus being bolted onto a defense trigger.
